正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
愚嘗端居而思致治之大典
惟賓興賢能亘古今而弗替
者曷故焉曰是三綱之所繫
也九疇之所屬也故自成周
以降至于後世雖正朔偏安
裔夷雲擾而猶知科舉取士
===
之為重際遇我
朝
列聖稽古右文其典益備耳目之
所睹記蓋蔑以加矣正德己
卯復當大比之期巡按廣西
監察御史曹珪祗奉
德音此為首務棘闈既拓士類爭
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

愚嘗端居而思致治之大典，惟賓興賢能亘古今而弗替者，曷故焉？曰：是三綱之所繫也，九疇之所屬也。故自成周以降，至于後世，雖正朔偏安，裔夷雲擾，而猶知科舉取士之為重。際遇我朝列聖稽古右文，其典益備，耳目之所睹記，蓋蔑以加矣。正德己卯，復當大比之期，巡按廣西監察御史曹珪祗奉德音，此為首務。棘闈既拓，士類爭
translation_en:
Preface to the Guangxi Provincial Examination Record

In my humble reflections, sitting quietly, I have pondered the great institutions by which good government is achieved. Why is it that honoring and recommending the worthy and capable has endured from antiquity to the present without being abandoned? The answer is that upon this depend the Three Bonds, and to this pertain the Nine Categories of the Great Plan. Thus, from the Zhou dynasty onward into later ages, even when legitimate dynastic rule was confined to a corner of the realm and outlying peoples stirred up turmoil like gathering clouds, the importance of selecting officials through the civil-service examinations was still recognized. Under our dynasty, successive sage emperors have studied antiquity and esteemed literary learning, making these institutions ever more complete. Among all that has been witnessed or recorded, surely nothing surpasses them.

In the jimao year of Zhengde [1519], the time for the triennial examination came around once more. Cao Gui, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Guangxi, reverently received the imperial pronouncement and made this his foremost responsibility. Once the examination compound had been opened up, the scholars vied …

translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In quiet retirement, I have often reflected: among the great institutions for achieving good government, why has the ceremonial selection and advancement of the worthy and able endured unchanged from antiquity to the present? My answer is that on it depend the Three Bonds of human relationships, and to it pertain the Nine Categories of the Great Plan. Thus, from the Zhou dynasty onward into later ages, even when legitimate dynastic rule was confined to a regional refuge and outlying peoples rose in turmoil like gathering clouds, men still recognized the importance of selecting officials through the examinations. Under our dynasty, successive sage emperors have studied antiquity and honored literary learning, making these institutions ever more complete. Among all that has been witnessed or recorded, surely nothing surpasses them.

In the jimao year of Zhengde [1519], the time for the triennial Provincial Examination came round again. Cao Gui 曹珪, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Guangxi, reverently obeyed the imperial pronouncement and made this his foremost duty. title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
先維時總督兩廣都御史楊
旦執經用武注意斯文而總
鎭太監王堂總兵官撫寧侯
朱麒鎭守太監傅倫副總兵
張祐皆預聞焉今致仕左布
政使何珊先事授畫旣即厥
緖於是合四道所簡之士鎖
===
院而三試之其在內提調則
右叅政黃衷右叅議梁億為
之監試則按察使宗璽僉事
俞緇為之至於監臨獨任其
責者御史曹珪也暨考校試
卷則敎諭周尚文楊國本李
從龍林德振常儒甫陳錫實
punctuated: 先。維時，總督兩廣都御史楊旦執經用武，注意斯文，而總鎭太監王堂、總兵官撫寧侯朱麒、鎭守太監傅倫、副總兵張祐皆預聞焉。今致仕左布政使何珊先事授畫，旣即厥緖，於是合四道所簡之士，鎖院而三試之。其在內提調，則右叅政黃衷、右叅議梁億為之；監試，則按察使宗璽、僉事俞緇為之。至於監臨獨任其責者，御史曹珪也。暨考校試卷，則敎諭周尚文、楊國本、李從龍、林德振、常儒甫、陳錫實
translation_en:
…to be first. At that time, Yang Dan, Censor-in-chief and Supreme Commander of Guangdong and Guangxi, upheld the Classics while employing military force and devoted attention to literary learning. Wang Tang, the eunuch in overall command; Zhu Qi, Marquis of Funing and Regional Commander; Fu Lun, the Regional Military Director, a eunuch; and Zhang You, Vice Regional Commander, all participated in deliberations on the matter. He Shan, the now-retired Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, had provided plans in advance. Once the undertaking was under way, the candidates selected by the four circuits were assembled, the examination compound was locked, and they were examined in three sessions.

Within the compound, Huang Zhong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, and Liang Yi, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner, served as Proctors. Zong Xi, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Yu Zi, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, supervised the examinations. Sole responsibility as Supervising Official rested with Censor Cao Gui. title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
應聘而來其在外襄理則右
布政使翁茂南左參政彭夔
右參政宋愷副使張祐劉潮
僉事姚鵬楊譽李淳都指揮
同知戴儀皆夙夜匪懈聿觀
厥成旣遵
制額取士刻文為錄以獻世讓
===
忝兹文柄其為自幸實多矣
惡能已於言乎惟昔先王之
世若井田若封建若賓興賢
能皆所謂大經大法也然彼
二者同塗殊歸不能保其不
變也是故井田之後變而為
稅畝徵租封建之後變而為
punctuated:
應聘而來。其在外襄理，則右布政使翁茂南、左參政彭夔、右參政宋愷、副使張祐、劉潮、僉事姚鵬、楊譽、李淳、都指揮同知戴儀，皆夙夜匪懈，聿觀厥成。旣遵制額取士，刻文為錄以獻。世讓忝兹文柄，其為自幸實多矣，惡能已於言乎？

惟昔先王之世，若井田，若封建，若賓興賢能，皆所謂大經大法也。然彼二者，同塗殊歸，不能保其不變也。是故井田之後，變而為稅畝徵租；封建之後，變而為
translation_en:
…came in response to invitations. Those assisting with arrangements outside the examination compound were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Weng Maonan, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Peng Kui, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Song Kai, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang You and Liu Chao, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yao Peng, Yang Yu, and Li Chun, and Regional Military Vice Commissioner Dai Yi. All worked tirelessly day and night and saw the undertaking through to completion. Having selected candidates according to the imperially prescribed quota, we had the compositions engraved for printing as a record to be presented. I, Shirang, have undeservedly held the authority to judge these writings and have much cause to count myself fortunate. How could I refrain from saying something?

In the age of the ancient kings, the well-field system, the enfeoffment system, and the ceremonial reception and advancement of the worthy and capable were all what are called great guiding principles and fundamental institutions. Yet the former two, though following the same path, reached different ends; there was no assurance that they would remain unchanged. Thus the well-field system subsequently changed into taxation by acreage and the collection of rents; the enfeoffment system subsequently changed into…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
罷侯置守獨賓興之典萬世
炳如日星嗚呼此可以觀世
道之所寄矣夫廣西古百粤
之區也當先王盛時井田封
建猶未嘗及猶不識不知而
况鄉舉里選之制乎以今日
人文之盛觀之可以知我
===
列聖化成天下之績矣諸士子生
逢
景運睹河洛而不思禹功可乎
或曰今之選舉賓興果如周
禮之三物而無變乎否也愚
應之曰學校以善其基明倫
以敦其本養之六經以造其
punctuated:
罷侯置守，獨賓興之典，萬世炳如日星。嗚呼！此可以觀世道之所寄矣。夫廣西，古百粤之區也。當先王盛時，井田、封建猶未嘗及，猶不識不知，而况鄉舉里選之制乎？以今日人文之盛觀之，可以知我列聖化成天下之績矣。諸士子生逢景運，睹河洛而不思禹功，可乎？
或曰：「今之選舉賓興，果如《周禮》之三物而無變乎？否也。」愚應之曰：「學校以善其基，明倫以敦其本，養之六經以造其……」
translation_en:
…abolishing the feudal lords and appointing governors. Only the institution of honoring and recommending worthy men has shone through the ages like the sun and stars. Alas! Here we may see where the moral order of the world finds its support. Guangxi was anciently the territory of the Hundred Yue. Even at the height of the former kings’ rule, the well-field system and feudal enfeoffment had never reached it and remained unknown there; how much less could there have been a system of recommending men from townships and selecting them from villages? Judging by the flourishing of literary culture today, we can recognize the achievements of our successive sage emperors in transforming and perfecting the realm. You scholars have been born into an auspicious age: can you behold the Yellow and Luo Rivers without reflecting on the achievements of Yu?
Someone says: “Do today’s selection and recommendation of worthy men truly follow the three categories of instruction prescribed in the Rites of Zhou, without alteration? They do not.” I humbly reply: “Schools serve to lay a sound foundation for them; clarification of human relationships strengthens their roots; nurturing them through the Six Classics develops their …”

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
道博之五策以試其能然則
三物固在是矣又何變焉雖
然吾所憂者吾人之變耳靜
言庸違嚮道中廢脩于家而
壞于
天子之庭者聖賢之罪人也又焉
得為三代之士乎世讓不敏
===
願諸士子幸更相勉圖之
直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒
學教諭方世讓謹序
punctuated:
道，博之五策以試其能。然則三物固在是矣，又何變焉？雖然，吾所憂者吾人之變耳。靜言庸違，嚮道中廢，脩于家而壞于天子之庭者，聖賢之罪人也，又焉得為三代之士乎？世讓不敏，願諸士子幸更相勉圖之。
直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒學教諭方世讓謹序。
translation_en:
…their Way, and test their abilities broadly through five policy questions. Thus the three categories are surely embodied in these practices; what, then, has changed? Nevertheless, what concerns me is change in ourselves. Those whose words are fair but whose conduct contradicts them, who turn toward the Way but abandon it halfway, who cultivate themselves at home but become corrupt at the Son of Heaven’s court, are offenders against the sages and worthies. How could they qualify as scholars of the Three Dynasties? I, Shirang, am slow of understanding, but hope that you scholars will encourage one another and strive toward this.
Preface respectfully composed by Fang Shirang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yingshang County, Yingzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region.

直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒學教諭方世讓謹序。
translation_en:
…the Way; broaden their inquiry through five policy questions to test their ability [?]. Thus the three categories are surely present here; what, then, has changed? Nevertheless, what concerns me is change in ourselves. Those whose words are fine but whose conduct contradicts them, who turn toward the Way but abandon it midway, or who cultivate themselves at home yet fall into corruption at the Son of Heaven’s court are offenders against the sages and worthies. How could they qualify as scholars of the Three Dynasties? I, Shirang, am slow of understanding, but I hope that you examination candidates will encourage one another to strive toward this.
Preface respectfully composed by Fang Shirang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yingshang County, Yingzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
正德十四年鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史曹珪〔廷獻湖廣黃岡縣人辛未進士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政黃衷〔子和廣東南海縣人丙辰進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參議梁億〔叔永廣東順德縣人辛未進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使宗璽〔朝用直隸建平縣人己未進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事俞緇〔子宜江西鄱陽縣人戊辰進士〕
===
考試官
直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒學教諭方世讓〔伯禮湖廣巴陵縣人庚午貢士〕
江西南昌府新建縣儒學教諭周尚文〔質夫福建閩縣人庚午貢士〕
同考試官
廣東惠州府博羅縣儒學教諭楊國本〔在培福建莆田縣人庚午貢士〕
江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭李從龍〔引雨福建莆田縣人丁卯貢士〕
山東濟南府青城縣儒學教諭林德振〔如玉福建閩縣人丙子貢士〕
山東兗州府城武縣儒學教諭曾儒雨〔遜學福建莆田縣人癸酉貢士〕
福建興化府仙遊縣儒學教諭陳錫〔元與廣東南海縣人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
正德十四年鄉試。

監臨官：巡按廣西監察御史曹珪〔廷獻，湖廣黃岡縣人，辛未進士〕。

提調官：廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政黃衷〔子和，廣東南海縣人，丙辰進士〕。廣西等處承宣布政使司右參議梁億〔叔永，廣東順德縣人，辛未進士〕。

監試官：廣西等處提刑按察司按察使宗璽〔朝用，直隸建平縣人，己未進士〕。廣西等處提刑按察司僉事俞緇〔子宜，江西鄱陽縣人，戊辰進士〕。

考試官：直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒學教諭方世讓〔伯禮，湖廣巴陵縣人，庚午貢士〕。江西南昌府新建縣儒學教諭周尚文〔質夫，福建閩縣人，庚午貢士〕。

同考試官：廣東惠州府博羅縣儒學教諭楊國本〔在培，福建莆田縣人，庚午貢士〕。江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭李從龍〔引雨，福建莆田縣人，丁卯貢士〕。山東濟南府青城縣儒學教諭林德振〔如玉，福建閩縣人，丙子貢士〕。山東兗州府城武縣儒學教諭曾儒雨〔遜學，福建莆田縣人，癸酉貢士〕。福建興化府仙遊縣儒學教諭陳錫〔元與，廣東南海縣人，庚午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Provincial Examination of the Fourteenth Year of Zhengde (1519).

Supervising Official:
Cao Gui, Regional Inspector of Guangxi and Investigating Censor. His courtesy name was Tingxian; he was from Huanggang County, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the xinwei year.

Proctors:
Huang Zhong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner in the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Zihe; he was from Nanhai County, Guangdong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.
Liang Yi, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner in the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Shuyong; he was from Shunde County, Guangdong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Examination Monitors:
Zong Xi, Surveillance Commissioner in the Guangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Chaoyong; he was from Jianping County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.
Yu Zi, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in the Guangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he was from Poyang County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Examiners:
Fang Shirang, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yingshang County, Yingzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Boli; he was from Baling County, Huguang, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the gengwu year.
Zhou Shangwen, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he was from Min County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the gengwu year.

Associate Examiners:
Yang Guoben, Instructor in the Confucian School of Boluo County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong. His courtesy name was Zaipei; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the gengwu year.
Li Conglong, Instructor in the Confucian School of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Yinyu; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the dingmao year.
Lin Dezhen, Instructor in the Confucian School of Qingcheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. His courtesy name was Ruyu; he was from Min County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the bingzi year.
Zeng Ruyu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Chengwu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. His courtesy name was Xunxue; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.
Chen Xi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xianyou County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Yuanyu; he was from Nanhai County, Guangdong, and was a tribute student of the gengwu year.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
印卷官
廣西等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨汪福〔大錫江西樂平縣人吏員〕
廣西等處提刑按察司照磨所照磨易智〔天機湖廣南漳縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
桂林府知府童旭〔賓暘湖廣沔陽州人己未進士〕
慶遠府知府陳大中〔時甫湖廣蘄州人戊辰進士〕
受卷官
南寧府知府李津〔濟之廣東四會縣人壬戌進士〕
平樂府同知陳珖〔朝用廣東饒平縣人甲子貢士〕
===
彌封官
潯州府推官朱恩〔廣仁直隸無錫縣人辛酉貢士〕
桂林府全州知州章諍〔直言直隸太湖縣人戊午貢士〕
南寧府橫州知州馮會〔宗元廣東南海縣人戊午貢士〕
謄錄官
太平府養利州知州萬應選〔克賢江西安福縣人癸卯貢士〕
平樂府賀縣知縣曹獻〔廷璧直隸通州人監生〕
南寧府武緣縣知縣姚明誠〔廷教廣東潮陽縣人監生〕
太平府永康縣知縣楊斅〔學文江西豐城縣人辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
印卷官
廣西等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨汪福〔大錫，江西樂平縣人，吏員〕。
廣西等處提刑按察司照磨所照磨易智〔天機，湖廣南漳縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官
桂林府知府童旭〔賓暘，湖廣沔陽州人，己未進士〕。
慶遠府知府陳大中〔時甫，湖廣蘄州人，戊辰進士〕。

受卷官
南寧府知府李津〔濟之，廣東四會縣人，壬戌進士〕。
平樂府同知陳珖〔朝用，廣東饒平縣人，甲子貢士〕。

彌封官
潯州府推官朱恩〔廣仁，直隸無錫縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
桂林府全州知州章諍〔直言，直隸太湖縣人，戊午貢士〕。
南寧府橫州知州馮會〔宗元，廣東南海縣人，戊午貢士〕。

謄錄官
太平府養利州知州萬應選〔克賢，江西安福縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
平樂府賀縣知縣曹獻〔廷璧，直隸通州人，監生〕。
南寧府武緣縣知縣姚明誠〔廷教，廣東潮陽縣人，監生〕。
太平府永康縣知縣楊斅〔學文，江西豐城縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Officials in Charge of Printing Examination Papers
Wang Fu, Examiner of Documents in the Documents Examination Office of the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Daxi and was from Leping County, Jiangxi. He entered service as a clerk.
Yi Zhi, Examiner of Documents in the Documents Examination Office of the Guangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Tianji and was from Nanzhang County, Huguang. He was an Imperial University student.

Officials in Charge of the Custody of Examination Scripts
Tong Xu, Prefect of Guilin, had the courtesy name Binyang and was from Mianyang Subprefecture, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiwei year.
Chen Dazhong, Prefect of Qingyuan, had the courtesy name Shifu and was from Qizhou, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Officials in Charge of Receiving Examination Scripts
Li Jin, Prefect of Nanning, had the courtesy name Jizhi and was from Sihui County, Guangdong. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.
Chen Guang, Vice Prefect of Pingle, had the courtesy name Chaoyong and was from Raoping County, Guangdong. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiazi year.

Officials in Charge of Sealing Candidates’ Names
Zhu En, Prefectural Judge of Xunzhou, had the courtesy name Guangren and was from Wuxi County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.
Zhang Zheng, Magistrate of Quanzhou Subprefecture in Guilin Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhiyan and was from Taihu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.
Feng Hui, Magistrate of Hengzhou Subprefecture in Nanning Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zongyuan and was from Nanhai County, Guangdong. He was a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.

Officials in Charge of Transcription
Wan Yingxuan, Magistrate of Yangli Subprefecture in Taiping Prefecture, had the courtesy name Kexian and was from Anfu County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.
Cao Xian, Magistrate of He County in Pingle Prefecture, had the courtesy name Tingbi and was from Tongzhou in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an Imperial University student.
Yao Mingcheng, Magistrate of Wuyuan County in Nanning Prefecture, had the courtesy name Tingjiao and was from Chaoyang County, Guangdong. He was an Imperial University student.
Yang Xiao, Magistrate of Yongkang County in Taiping Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xuewen and was from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
三十而立四十而不惑
人莫不飲食也鮮能知味也
天子討而不伐諸侯伐而不討
易
忠信所以進德也脩辭立其誠所以居業
也知至至之可與幾也知終終之可與
存義也
===
聖人亨以享上帝而大亨以養聖賢
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛
陽卦奇陰卦耦
書
惟德動天無遠弗屆滿招損謙受益時乃
天道帝初于歷山往于田日號泣于旻
天于父母負罪引慝祗載見瞽瞍夔夔
齋慄瞽亦允若至誠感神矧茲有苗
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
三十而立，四十而不惑。
人莫不飲食也，鮮能知味也。
天子討而不伐，諸侯伐而不討。

易
忠信所以進德也，脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。
聖人亨以享上帝，而大亨以養聖賢。
歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。
陽卦奇，陰卦耦。

書
惟德動天，無遠弗屆。滿招損，謙受益，時乃天道。帝初于歷山，往于田，日號泣于旻天，于父母負罪引慝。祗載見瞽瞍，夔夔齋慄，瞽亦允若。至誠感神，矧茲有苗！
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
“At thirty, I stood firm; at forty, I was free from perplexity.”
“Everyone eats and drinks, but few can discern the flavors.”
“The Son of Heaven punishes but does not wage war; the feudal lords wage war but do not exercise the authority to punish.”

Book of Changes
“Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue. Refining one’s words and establishing their sincerity are the means of maintaining one’s work. Knowing the point to be reached and reaching it, one can apprehend the first stirrings of things; knowing the end and carrying it through, one can preserve what is right.”
“The sage cooks offerings to sacrifice to the Lord on High, and prepares great feasts to nourish sages and worthies.”
“Place the remaining stalks between the fingers to symbolize an intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalations; therefore, place the remainders between the fingers twice before setting aside a stalk again.”
“Yang trigrams are odd; yin trigrams are even.”

Book of Documents
“Virtue alone moves Heaven; there is no distance beyond its reach. Complacency invites loss; humility receives benefit: this is the Way of Heaven. When the emperor [Shun] was first at Mount Li, he went into the fields and daily cried out in tears to compassionate Heaven, taking upon himself guilt and wrongdoing toward his parents. He reverently attended upon Gusou, his father, with solemn awe and trembling vigilance, until Gusou, too, became truly well-disposed toward him. Utmost sincerity moves the spirits—how much more these people of Youmiao!”

translation_en:
Aid the worthy and support the virtuous; honor the loyal and advance the good. Do not undertake useless things to the detriment of useful ones, and your work will succeed; do not prize exotic objects while despising useful goods, and the people will have enough. If the attendant servants are upright, their ruler can be upright.

Knowing that you have come to me, I present you with assorted girdle pendants; knowing your kindness toward me, I offer you assorted girdle pendants in greeting; knowing your affection for me, I repay you with assorted girdle pendants. 之食

合生氣之和道五常之行
===

第貳場

臺諫以天下公議為主

擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔文帝二年

…the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. Ninth year of Duke Xi.
Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu. Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao. Xun Wu of Jin led an army to destroy the Rong of Luhun. Seventeenth year of Duke Zhao.

After three years of cultivation, there must be enough food for one year; after nine years of cultivation, there must be enough food for three years.
Heaven displays its signs, and the sage takes them as his model. The suburban sacrifice serves to illuminate the Way of Heaven.
Bring together the harmony of life-giving energies and guide the operation of the five constant principles.
A ruler must not use small matters to plan great ones, discuss what is near on the basis of what is distant, or devise external affairs on the basis of internal ones.

Second Session
Discourse
Censors and remonstrance officials should take the impartial judgment of all under Heaven as their guiding principle.

One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty granting the people remission of half of this year's land tax. Second year of Emperor Wen.
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty additionally appointing Fang Xuanling, Vice Director of the Left, as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. Thirteenth year of Zhenguan.
Compose a memorial in the voice of Su Shi and others of the Song dynasty presenting the memorials of Lu Zhi of the Tang dynasty. Eighth year of Yuanyou.

第叁場
策五道
問帝王之御極皆有典則垂訓而其後世
===
之君能守文繼志者亦或鮮矣若我
孝宗敬皇帝暨惟
今上大明會典之作誠所謂善繼善述而集一
代之大成者故其制作損益皆本於
聖祖高皇帝御製群書然其實有因事而類見
者有專主以立法者可得而詳言歟予
嘗伏讀而歎其大綱日麗萬目星羅體
統截然而名分不易也可指言其實歟
唐虞而下致治莫備於周不知會典之
punctuated:
判語〔五條〕
出使不復命。
官馬不調習。
告狀不受理。
徒囚不應役。
造作不如法。

第叁場
策五道

問：帝王之御極，皆有典則垂訓，而其後世之君能守文繼志者，亦或鮮矣。若我孝宗敬皇帝暨惟今上，《大明會典》之作，誠所謂善繼善述而集一代之大成者。故其制作損益，皆本於聖祖高皇帝御製群書。然其實有因事而類見者，有專主以立法者，可得而詳言歟？予嘗伏讀而歎其大綱日麗，萬目星羅，體統截然而名分不易也。可指言其實歟？唐虞而下，致治莫備於周，不知《會典》之
translation_en:
Legal judgments 〔five items〕
Failure to report back upon completing an official mission.
Failure to train government horses.
Failure to accept and process a complaint.
Failure of convicts sentenced to penal servitude to perform their assigned labor.
Manufacture or construction that does not conform to regulations.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When emperors and kings occupy the throne, they all establish statutes and standards to transmit instruction to posterity. Yet among their successors, those able to uphold the established institutions and carry on their intentions have perhaps been few. As for our Emperor Xiaozong Jing and His Present Majesty, their compilation of the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian) truly exemplifies skill in carrying forward their predecessor’s purposes and undertakings, bringing together the comprehensive achievements of a dynasty. Thus, its institutional arrangements, modifications, and additions all derive from the various works imperially authored by the Sagely Progenitor, Emperor Gao. In their actual contents, however, some provisions appear under categories according to the matters concerned, while others focus specifically on establishing regulations. Can you explain these in detail?

I have reverently read this work and marveled that its main principles shine like the sun and its myriad particulars are arrayed like the stars; its institutional hierarchy is sharply defined, and its distinctions of status and duty are unalterable. Can you point to concrete examples and explain them? From the ages of Tang and Yu onward, no dynasty’s arrangements for achieving good government were more comprehensive than those of the Zhou. 問：帝王之御極，皆有典則垂訓，而其後世之君能守文繼志者，亦或鮮矣。若我孝宗敬皇帝曁惟今上，《大明會典》之作，誠所謂善繼善述而集一代之大成者。故其制作損益，皆本於聖祖高皇帝御製群書。然其實有因事而類見者，有專主以立法者，可得而詳言歟？予嘗伏讀而歎其大綱日麗，萬目星羅，體統截然而名分不易也，可指言其實歟？唐虞而下，致治莫備於周，不知《會典》之
translation_en:
Legal judgments 〔five items〕
Failure to report upon returning from an official mission; failure to train government horses; failure to accept and hear a complaint; failure of convicts sentenced to penal servitude to perform their assigned labor; manufacture or construction that does not conform to regulations.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When emperors and kings ascend the throne, they all leave authoritative rules and instructive precepts for posterity. Yet among their successors, those capable of preserving the established institutions and carrying forward their intentions may be few indeed. As for our Emperor Xiaozong Jing and His Present Majesty, their compilation of the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian) truly exemplifies skill in carrying on their predecessor’s work and intentions, bringing together the crowning achievements of a dynasty. Thus its institutional provisions, modifications, and additions all draw upon the various works imperially composed by the Sagely Ancestor, Emperor Gao. Yet among their actual contents, some provisions appear under classifications according to the matters concerned, while others are devoted specifically to establishing regulations. Can you explain these in detail?

I have reverently read this work and marveled that its principal outlines shine like the sun and its myriad particulars are arrayed like stars, that its institutional order is sharply defined and its distinctions of status and duty remain unaltered. Can you point to concrete examples and explain them? From the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun onward, no achievement of orderly government was more comprehensive than that of the Zhou. I wonder whether the Collected Statutes’…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
規模大要有合於周制者果何在歟自
是而降若漢唐宋若胡元皆未嘗無一
代之作也叅之會典可同日而語乎至
於所謂制異墳典法殊紀傳事雖微而
必錄令已寢而亦書文移之載華去潤
色而務從實者又未必無其說也爾諸
生誦法傾心之日久矣願鋪張揚厲探
本遡源以對毋遜毋忽
問立德立功立言儒者之業也固有優於
===
德而功或不逮茂於功而言則不文信
乎其兼長之難矣抑不知先立乎其大
者則其次者可畧不然則交致之功果
亦有要乎否耶蓋嘗迹古人之故而疑
焉姑舉其著者質之夫忠直廉約德之
屬也理治安攘功之屬也詞章訓詁又
言之屬也然忠潔而負讒於楚顧以為
過嚴直而見憚於漢恒疑於褊去官留
犢者或斥其矯垢衣惡食者或辨其姦
punctuated:
規模大要有合於周制者，果何在歟？自是而降，若漢唐宋，若胡元，皆未嘗無一代之作也。叅之會典，可同日而語乎？至於所謂制異墳典，法殊紀傳，事雖微而必錄，令已寢而亦書，文移之載華去潤色而務從實者，又未必無其說也。爾諸生誦法傾心之日久矣，願鋪張揚厲，探本遡源以對，毋遜毋忽。
問：立德、立功、立言，儒者之業也。固有優於德而功或不逮，茂於功而言則不文，信乎其兼長之難矣！抑不知先立乎其大者，則其次者可畧？不然，則交致之功，果亦有要乎否耶？蓋嘗迹古人之故而疑焉，姑舉其著者質之。夫忠直廉約，德之屬也；理治安攘，功之屬也；詞章訓詁，又言之屬也。然忠潔而負讒於楚，顧以為過；嚴直而見憚於漢，恒疑於褊；去官留犢者，或斥其矯；垢衣惡食者，或辨其姦。
translation_en:
…where precisely do the general framework and main principles accord with the institutions of the Zhou? From that time onward, the Han, Tang, and Song, as well as the Mongol Yuan, each produced works establishing the institutions of their dynasty. Compared with the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming, can they be spoken of in the same breath? As for the claims that its organization differs from the ancient canonical writings, that its method differs from annalistic and biographical histories, that it records matters however minor and includes ordinances even after they have ceased to be enforced, and that its inclusion of official correspondence dispenses with embellishment and strives to adhere to the facts [?]—these, too, may well have their explanations. You students have long devoted yourselves wholeheartedly to reciting and taking it as your model. Set forth its merits fully and vigorously, investigate its foundations and trace its sources in your answers. Be neither diffident nor careless.
Question: Establishing virtue, accomplishing meritorious deeds, and leaving enduring words are the undertakings of a Confucian scholar. Yet some excel in virtue while their accomplishments fall short; others achieve great things, yet their words lack literary refinement. Truly, it is difficult to excel in all three! But if one first establishes what is greatest, may what comes next be given less attention? If not, is there indeed an essential method for attaining all three together? I have examined the circumstances of men of antiquity and found grounds for doubt. Let me raise some conspicuous examples for you to examine. Loyalty, uprightness, integrity, and frugality belong to virtue; orderly government, securing peace within, and repelling threats from without belong to accomplishment; literary composition and textual exegesis belong to enduring words. Yet the loyal and pure man who suffered slander in Chu was nevertheless considered excessive; the stern and upright man who was feared in the Han was constantly suspected of narrow-mindedness. The man who left a calf behind when departing from office was sometimes denounced as affected; the man who wore soiled clothes and ate poor food was sometimes exposed as deceitful…

The man who left a calf behind on departing from office has been denounced by some as affected; the man who wore soiled clothes and ate poor food has been exposed by some as treacherous.…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
若然者德將何據而脩耶睢陽之績未
免流俗之口澶淵之役擬於城下之盟
請伐高麗者或致病於腹心應變成務
者或致亂於天寶若然者功將何施而
可耶潜心大業災異之論可疵博極群
書美新之累非細頌聖德者而風雅不
類著僮約者以過舉自彰若然者立言
君子又將何所取正而後精且粹耶豈
數子有諸己者不能無弊抑後儒之評
===
之見互有得失也諸生脩於家也素矣
其德其業固未可知如以言取子即今
日之急也不可不對
問事變萬殊理無定在而人之智慮有所
及有所不及稽諸古人已行之迹其在
當時可否異同之議若持訟牒於公庭
有未易以口舌爭焉姑舉其可見者與
諸士評之夫矯命專師均一恤鄰也而
有是有非立國樹黨均一謀國也而有
punctuated:
若然者，德將何據而脩耶？睢陽之績，未免流俗之口；澶淵之役，擬於城下之盟；請伐高麗者，或致病於腹心；應變成務者，或致亂於天寶。若然者，功將何施而可耶？潜心大業，災異之論可疵；博極群書，美新之累非細；頌聖德者，而風雅不類；著僮約者，以過舉自彰。若然者，立言君子又將何所取正，而後精且粹耶？豈數子有諸己者不能無弊，抑後儒之評之見互有得失也？諸生脩於家也素矣，其德其業固未可知。如以言取子，即今日之急也，不可不對。
問：事變萬殊，理無定在，而人之智慮有所及，有所不及。稽諸古人已行之迹，其在當時可否異同之議，若持訟牒於公庭，有未易以口舌爭焉。姑舉其可見者，與諸士評之。夫矯命專師，均一恤鄰也，而有是有非；立國樹黨，均一謀國也，而有
translation_en:
If this is so, on what basis is virtue to be cultivated? The achievement at Suiyang did not escape the criticism of ordinary opinion; the campaign at Chanyuan was likened to a covenant imposed beneath the city walls. One who requested an expedition against Gaoli was accused of bringing sickness to the heart of the realm; one who responded to changing circumstances and accomplished affairs was accused of bringing about the disorder of the Tianbao era. If this is so, how can meritorious deeds be undertaken acceptably? One who devoted himself to a great scholarly undertaking could be faulted for his arguments concerning calamities and anomalies; one whose learning encompassed the whole range of books incurred no slight stain through his Praise of Xin. One who extolled sagely virtue failed to accord with the Airs and Odes; one who wrote the Servant’s Contract made his own misconduct conspicuous. If this is so, from what are gentlemen seeking to establish enduring words to take their standard, so that their writings may become refined and pure? Could it be that the qualities these men possessed were not without defects, or that the judgments and views of later scholars each had their merits and failings? You students have long cultivated yourselves at home. Your virtue and accomplishments cannot, of course, yet be known. But if we are to select you through your words, that is the urgent business of today. You must answer.
Question: Changes in affairs take myriad forms, and principle has no fixed locus; human understanding and deliberation comprehend some things but fail to comprehend others. When we examine the recorded actions of the ancients, the arguments in their own times over what was acceptable or unacceptable, and the agreements and disagreements concerning them, resemble litigants presenting their written pleas in a public court: there are matters not easily settled through verbal contention. Let us take some evident examples and assess them together with you scholars. Falsifying a ruler’s command and assuming sole command of an army were alike acts of concern for a neighboring state, yet one was judged right and the other wrong. Establishing a state and forming a faction were alike ways of planning for the state, yet there were…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
得有失逼水置陣其勢同也然一以之
勝一以之負空國出師其迹同也然一
由之成一由之敗矯制立功若非矣或
者又以為可封負罪受辟當刑矣或者
又以為不當刑忘君之讎者彼此同歸
議者乃判功罪為兩途復父之讎者彼
此無間斷者輒施輕重之二典靈州之
棄守聚議紛紛未必皆是也綏州之城
否衆口藉藉不能無非也凡此之類窮
===
理者所當精察而明辨諸士子格物致
知之學其有素矣請悉心剖析以為古
今一大斷案不亦可乎毋委曰我則不
暇
問言行君子之樞機也古稱吉人之辭寡
而病商俗之靡曰利口焉若是乎聖人
之不貴言也而語善專對言果不可以已
耶又曰亂世之人尚通而聖人著其教
也必危行焉若是乎君子之行果而已
punctuated:
得有失。逼水置陣，其勢同也，然一以之勝，一以之負；空國出師，其迹同也，然一由之成，一由之敗。矯制立功，若非矣，或者又以為可封；負罪受辟，當刑矣，或者又以為不當刑。忘君之讎者，彼此同歸，議者乃判功罪為兩途；復父之讎者，彼此無間，斷者輒施輕重之二典。靈州之棄守，聚議紛紛，未必皆是也；綏州之城否，衆口藉藉，不能無非也。凡此之類，窮理者所當精察而明辨。諸士子格物致知之學，其有素矣，請悉心剖析，以為古今一大斷案，不亦可乎？毋委曰：「我則不暇。」

問：言行，君子之樞機也。古稱吉人之辭寡，而病商俗之靡，曰利口焉。若是乎聖人之不貴言也？而語善專對，言果不可以已耶？又曰亂世之人尚通，而聖人著其教也，必危行焉。若是乎君子之行果而已
translation_en:
…some succeeded and others failed. Deploying troops close against a river involved the same circumstances, yet one won thereby and another lost. Emptying a state to send out an army involved the same action, yet one thereby succeeded and another failed. Falsifying an imperial command to achieve merit would seem wrong, yet some have held that it deserved enfeoffment. Accepting a summons to office while burdened with guilt [?] ought to warrant punishment, yet some have held that punishment was unwarranted. Those who forgot the wrongs done to their rulers were alike in this respect, yet commentators assigned them to the separate categories of merit and guilt. Those who avenged their fathers were no different from one another, yet those judging them applied two different standards, one lenient and one severe. Opinions assembled concerning the abandonment or defense of Lingzhou were numerous and conflicting; they cannot all have been right. Voices clamored over whether to fortify Suizhou; some must have been wrong. All such cases require close examination and clear discrimination by those who investigate principle. You candidates have long cultivated the learning of investigating things and extending knowledge. Would it not be fitting to analyze these matters with your whole attention and produce a comprehensive adjudication spanning past and present? Do not evade the task by saying, “I have no time for this.”

Question: Words and deeds are the pivots of the gentleman’s conduct. The ancients said that an auspicious person speaks little, and, deploring the degeneracy of Shang customs, spoke of “glib tongues.” Did the sages thus place so little value on speech? Yet they spoke approvingly of the ability to respond independently on diplomatic missions. Can speech, then, really not be dispensed with? It is also said that people in disordered times prize accommodation, yet when the sage set forth his teaching, he insisted upon upright conduct. Is the gentleman’s conduct thus a matter of resolution alone…

得有失。逼水置陣，其勢同也，然一以之勝，一以之負；空國出師，其迹同也，然一由之成，一由之敗。矯制立功，若非矣，或者又以為可封；負罪受辟，當刑矣，或者又以為不當刑。忘君之讎者，彼此同歸，議者乃判功罪為兩途；復父之讎者，彼此無間，斷者輒施輕重之二典。靈州之棄守，聚議紛紛，未必皆是也；綏州之城否，衆口籍籍，不能無非也。凡此之類，窮理者所當精察而明辨。諸士子格物致知之學，其有素矣。請悉心剖析，以為古今一大斷案，不亦可乎？毋委曰：「我則不暇。」

問：言行，君子之樞機也。古稱吉人之辭寡，而病商俗之靡，曰利口焉。若是乎聖人之不貴言也！而語善專對，言果不可以已耶？又曰：「亂世之人尚通。」而聖人著其教也，必危行焉。若是乎君子之行果而已
translation_en:
…gains and losses. Deploying troops with their backs against water involved the same strategic circumstances, yet one army won thereby and another lost. Emptying the state to send out an army involved the same course of action, yet one succeeded thereby and another failed. Falsely invoking an imperial decree to achieve merit would seem wrong, yet some consider it deserving of enfeoffment. Someone guilty of an offense and subjected to punishment would seem deserving of that penalty, yet some consider that he should not have been punished. Those who forgot the wrong done to their ruler were alike in this respect, yet commentators assigned merit to one and guilt to another. Those who avenged their fathers differed in no such respect, yet those judging their cases applied two different standards, one lenient and one severe. Regarding whether to abandon or hold Lingzhou, the assembled opinions were numerous and conflicting, and not necessarily all correct. Regarding whether to fortify Suizhou, voices clamored in dispute, and some were inevitably mistaken. All such matters require close scrutiny and clear discrimination by those who investigate principles. You candidates have long pursued the learning of investigating things and extending knowledge. Would it not be fitting to analyze these matters with your utmost care and arrive at a definitive judgment encompassing past and present? Do not evade the task by saying, “I have no time for this.”

Question: Speech and conduct are the pivots of the gentleman’s activity. The ancients praised the good man’s sparing use of words, while criticizing the frivolity of Shang customs, describing it as glibness. Such was the sages’ low estimation of speech! Yet they also spoke of being skilled at responding independently on diplomatic missions. Can speech, then, truly not be dispensed with? It is also said, “People in disordered times prize adaptability.” Yet when the sages set forth their teachings, they invariably required upright conduct. Is the gentleman’s conduct, then, simply a matter of resoluteness…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中庸乃譏行怪又安在其不尚通耶後
世賢者語默之間通檢之迹或應對辨
給或言若不出或詞甚清辨或終日恂
恂或輕肆直言或不答國事或束身自
脩或任心獨詣或候見不顧或惟事造
謁或恥與俗交或自同傭人是其語者
默者檢者通者後世蓋嘗仰而觀之不
知其言也於事何所述其默也於道何
所營其通也何以周務而其檢也何以
===
育德耶抑不知於聖人言動之度果有
合乎否也茲欲言罔口過而行鮮怨惡
焉何道而可
問養民與兵政之紀也蓋不袪其患而厚
其生天下無安民不裕其食而節其力
天下無良兵此有識者所共知也巖栖
露宿老稚沿江而行丐廣西之民困矣
健逃老死單弱隨籍而紀錄廣西之卒
耗矣民困而供億且繁卒耗而饋餉不
punctuated:
中庸乃譏行怪，又安在其不尚通耶？後世賢者，語默之間，通檢之迹，或應對辨給，或言若不出，或詞甚清辨，或終日恂恂，或輕肆直言，或不答國事，或束身自脩，或任心獨詣，或候見不顧，或惟事造謁，或恥與俗交，或自同傭人。是其語者、默者、檢者、通者，後世蓋嘗仰而觀之。不知其言也，於事何所述？其默也，於道何所營？其通也，何以周務？而其檢也，何以育德耶？抑不知於聖人言動之度，果有合乎否也？茲欲言罔口過，而行鮮怨惡焉，何道而可？

問：養民與兵，政之紀也。蓋不袪其患而厚其生，天下無安民；不裕其食而節其力，天下無良兵。此有識者所共知也。巖栖露宿，老稚沿江而行丐，廣西之民困矣；健逃老死，單弱隨籍而紀錄，廣西之卒耗矣。民困而供億且繁，卒耗而饋餉不
translation_en:
…Yet the Doctrine of the Mean censures eccentric conduct. How, then, can it be said that it does not esteem adaptability? Among worthy men of later ages, in their speech and silence and in the manifestations of their adaptability or restraint, some answered readily and eloquently, while others seemed scarcely able to speak; some spoke with great clarity and eloquence, while others remained deferential throughout the day; some spoke frankly with heedless abandon, while others would not answer questions about affairs of state; some disciplined themselves and cultivated their persons, while others followed their own inclinations and pursued understanding independently. Some disregarded those waiting to see them [?], while others occupied themselves solely with paying visits; some were ashamed to associate with ordinary people, while others placed themselves on a level with hired laborers. These men—whether speaking or silent, restrained or adaptable—have been regarded with admiration by later generations. Yet we do not know: when they spoke, what did they expound concerning affairs? When they remained silent, what did they pursue concerning the Way? Through their adaptability, how did they attend comprehensively to practical affairs? Through their restraint, how did they nurture virtue? Nor do we know whether they truly conformed to the sages’ standards for speech and action. If we now wish to speak without verbal faults and to act so as seldom to incur resentment or hatred, by what way can this be achieved?

Question: Sustaining the people and the troops is a guiding principle of government. Unless their afflictions are removed and their livelihoods enriched, there will be no settled populace in the realm; unless their food supplies are made ample and their strength husbanded, there will be no good soldiers in the realm. This is something all discerning men recognize. Dwelling among rocks and sleeping exposed to the dew, the old and young travel along the rivers begging: the people of Guangxi are in distress. The able-bodied flee and the old die, while the frail and weak are entered in the registers: the ranks of Guangxi’s soldiers are depleted. The people are distressed, yet the demands for supplies are numerous; the troops are depleted, yet their provisions and pay do not…

知其言也於事何所述其默也於道何

punctuated:

translation_en:
…Yet the Doctrine of the Mean criticizes eccentric conduct: how, then, can it be said not to esteem accommodation? Among worthy men of later ages, in their speaking and remaining silent, and in their conduct marked by accommodation or restraint, some were fluent and quick in their replies; some spoke as though unable to get their words out; some expressed themselves with great clarity and eloquence; some remained modest and deferential all day. Some spoke frankly and without restraint; some declined to answer questions about affairs of state. Some disciplined themselves and cultivated their persons; some followed their own inclinations and pursued their own understanding. Some disregarded those waiting to see them; some concerned themselves solely with paying visits. Some were ashamed to associate with ordinary people; some placed themselves on the same footing as hired laborers. Later generations have looked up to these men, whether they spoke or remained silent, practiced restraint or accommodation. Yet what matters did they expound when they spoke? What did they pursue concerning the Way when they remained silent? How did their accommodation enable them to attend comprehensively to affairs, and how did their restraint nurture virtue? Nor do we know whether they truly conformed to the sages’ standards of speech and action. If we now wish to speak without verbal fault and act so as to incur little resentment or hatred, by what way can this be achieved?

Question: Nourishing the people and administering the troops are fundamental concerns of government. Unless the people’s troubles are removed and their livelihoods improved, there can be no settled populace in the realm; unless the troops’ food supplies are made ample and their strength conserved, there can be no good soldiers in the realm. This is something all discerning people recognize. Dwelling among rocks and sleeping in the open, the old and young travel along the rivers begging: the people of Guangxi are impoverished. The able-bodied flee and the old die; only the frail and weak remain recorded on the registers: the ranks of Guangxi’s troops are depleted. Yet, although the people are impoverished, demands for supplies and services remain heavy; although the troops are depleted, their provision of rations and pay does not…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
減此又有識者所共憂也振而處之曷
為其方乎蓋嘗聞之柴中行之為幹官
而減苗斛應孟明之為經略而除抑配
至我
朝或停逃亡之租或節無經之費養民之術
可謂要矣而不救於逋負者何耶許仲
宣為轉運而罷征交之士謝麟知桂州
而全近郡之兵至我
朝或借戍於湖廣或仰給於廣東養兵之術
===
亦謂備矣而無補於脫耗者何耶昔人
有言臨政論治不若退而更化今必公
私俱贍而民始裕戰守有備而兵始精
不知更其化而後可以赴吾民之急乎
抑其舊政者可脩而舉也諸生皆明當
世之務而於鄉邦之故計之必審幸盡
言之以告在位者
punctuated: 減，此又有識者所共憂也。振而處之，曷為其方乎？蓋嘗聞之，柴中行之為幹官而減苗斛，應孟明之為經略而除抑配。至我朝，或停逃亡之租，或節無經之費，養民之術可謂要矣，而不救於逋負者何耶？許仲宣為轉運而罷征交之士，謝麟知桂州而全近郡之兵。至我朝，或借戍於湖廣，或仰給於廣東，養兵之術亦謂備矣，而無補於脫耗者何耶？昔人有言：「臨政論治，不若退而更化。」今必公私俱贍而民始裕，戰守有備而兵始精。不知更其化而後可以赴吾民之急乎？抑其舊政者可脩而舉也？諸生皆明當世之務，而於鄉邦之故，計之必審，幸盡言之以告在位者。
translation_en:
…are not reduced. This, too, is a matter of shared concern among discerning people. What means should be adopted to remedy and manage this situation? We have heard that Chai Zhongxing, while serving as an administrative assistant, reduced the grain-tax levy, and that Ying Mengming, while serving as Military Commissioner, abolished compulsory allocations. Under our own dynasty, measures have included suspending taxes owed by those who had fled and curbing expenditures lacking an established basis. These methods of sustaining the people may be called essential; why, then, have they failed to relieve tax arrears? Xu Zhongxuan, as Transport Commissioner, stood down the troops assigned to campaign against Jiaozhi, and Xie Lin, as Prefect of Guizhou, preserved the troops of nearby prefectures. Under our own dynasty, measures have included borrowing troops from Huguang for garrison service and relying on Guangdong for supplies. These methods of sustaining the army may likewise be called comprehensive; why, then, have they done nothing to remedy desertion and depletion?

Someone in antiquity said: “Discussing good government while administering affairs is less effective than stepping back and reforming the system.” Now, only when both public and private resources are sufficient will the people attain prosperity; only when preparations for both battle and defense are in place will the troops become effective. Must we first reform the system before we can meet our people’s urgent needs? Or can the existing policies be repaired and put into effect? You candidates all understand the affairs of the present age, and you must surely have carefully considered the circumstances of your home province. Please express your views fully, so as to inform those in office.

We have heard that Chai Zhongxing, serving as an administrative assistant, reduced the measure used to collect the grain tax, and that Ying Mengming, serving as military commissioner, abolished compulsory apportionments. Under our dynasty, taxes owed by those who had fled have sometimes been suspended, and expenditures without established warrant have sometimes been curtailed. These methods of sustaining the people may be called well directed; why, then, have they failed to remedy tax arrears? We hope you will set forth your views fully, to inform those in office.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
三十而立四十而不惑
楊琇
同考試官教諭常批論語一題士子類騁浮
辭讀之令人可厭是作獨能融會傳註成文且筆
勢整整未嘗苟下一語蓋有所得者也是宜錄
出以式後學
考試官教諭周批論語義如此作良是
===
考試官教諭方批集註意正如此
旣壯而有定守旣強而有定見聖人自言其所
進然也夫聖雖無所不通非可以不學而至者
也苟不求諸所示之學抑何由而知其然哉想
昔吾夫子之意若曰理具於心皆吾之所當知
心見於事皆吾之所當為吾十有五嘗志於學
矣由十五而三十追惟斯時道蓋有所得耶以
心御氣而不為氣所御雖紛紜舛錯之集吾則

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所移雖紛華盛麗之來吾則居安操約而略無
苟動焉確乎其操而非疆制也卓乎其守而非
力勝也其自立有如此者由三十而四十追惟
斯時道蓋無所疑耶凡事所當然者事至則理
形介石之固足以決萬變之幾微而理欲其判
然矣凡物所當然者物來則順應一致之理有
以通吾心之百慮而得失其較然矣剖析不患
其弗詳也辨別不患其弗盡也其不惑有如此
者是則三十而立則無所事志也可知四十不
===
惑則無所事守也可知聖人進德固亦有序也
哉雖然夫子生知安行豈嘗若是其積累歟特
因其近似以自名見其亦由學而至所以勉進
後人耳後世乃謂聖本生知非學可至是又自
棄已噫典謨何病乎芻蕘途人豈乖於堯舜有
志於大學者其潛心焉
人莫不飲食也鮮能知味也
劉存仁
同考試官教諭林批或問之義甚明場中士子
punctuated:
所移，雖紛華盛麗之來，吾則居安操約，而略無苟動焉。確乎其操，而非疆制也；卓乎其守，而非力勝也。其自立有如此者。由三十而四十，追惟斯時，道蓋無所疑耶？凡事所當然者，事至則理形，介石之固足以決萬變之幾微，而理欲其判然矣。凡物所當然者，物來則順應，一致之理有以通吾心之百慮，而得失其較然矣。剖析不患其弗詳也，辨別不患其弗盡也。其不惑有如此者。是則三十而立，則無所事志也可知；四十不惑，則無所事守也可知。聖人進德，固亦有序也哉！雖然，夫子生知安行，豈嘗若是其積累歟？特因其近似以自名，見其亦由學而至，所以勉進後人耳。後世乃謂聖本生知，非學可至，是又自棄已。噫！典謨何病乎芻蕘？途人豈乖於堯舜？有志於大學者，其潛心焉！

人莫不飲食也，鮮能知味也。
劉存仁
同考試官教諭林批：或問之義甚明，場中士子
translation_en:
…moved by it. Though dazzling splendor and magnificence present themselves, I remain at ease and hold to simplicity, without the slightest rash impulse. Firm is my resolve, yet it does not depend on forcible restraint; steadfast is my adherence, yet it does not depend on overcoming myself through effort. Such was my establishment of myself. From thirty to forty, looking back upon that time, had I perhaps come to have no doubts concerning the Way? In everything that ought to be done, principle becomes manifest as affairs arise. A firmness like rock suffices to discern the subtle beginnings of myriad changes, and principle and desire are clearly distinguished. As each thing presents itself, I respond in accordance with what is proper to it. The single, unifying principle links the hundred deliberations of my mind, and right and wrong become clearly evident. In analysis, I need not fear insufficient detail; in discrimination, I need not fear a failure to distinguish fully. Such was my freedom from perplexity. Thus we can understand that, once established at thirty, I no longer needed to exert myself in fixing my aspiration; once free from perplexity at forty, I no longer needed to exert myself in maintaining my adherence. Surely even a sage advances in virtue in an orderly sequence!

Yet the Master possessed knowledge from birth and practiced the Way with ease. Did he ever really accumulate learning in this fashion? He merely described himself through stages approximating his own experience, showing that he too had arrived through learning, so as to encourage later generations to advance. Later people instead claim that sages are inherently born knowing, and that their attainment cannot be reached through study. This is simply to abandon oneself. Alas! What obstacle do the Canons and Counsels present to grass-cutters and wood-gatherers? How could an ordinary passerby be fundamentally at odds with Yao and Shun? Let those who aspire to the Great Learning devote their minds to this!

“Everyone eats and drinks, but few can discern the flavor.”
By Liu Cunren.

translation_en:
…swayed. Though dazzling splendor and magnificence present themselves, I remain at ease and hold to simplicity, without the slightest rash impulse. Firm is my resolve, without forcible restraint; lofty is what I uphold, without overcoming temptation by sheer effort. Such was his establishment of himself. As for what ought to be done in every affair, when an affair arises its principle becomes manifest. Firm as a rock, he could discern the subtlest beginnings amid myriad changes, clearly distinguishing principle from desire. As for the proper response to every thing, when things present themselves he responds accordingly. The principle that unites all things brings coherence to his mind’s hundred deliberations, making right and wrong clear. title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
類為所窘殊不通暢惟此作詞理兼到是宜錄出
考試官教諭周批詞氣純厚自是中庸文
字樣宜錄以式
考試官教諭方批體貼詳明句句皆本色
語非性理之學不能有此
中庸明人同具乎道之中自失乎道之中夫道
以中為至也人皆有之而自不察此所以有過
不及之弊歟中庸引夫子之言以釋首章之義
如此且道之所謂中者乃天命人心之正當然
===
不易之理固不外乎民生日用之間也試言諸
飲食彼夫冬而湯夏而水人莫不飲也飲有正
味必察之而後知人或飲以濟渴未之能察也
則飲焉而得其正味者幾何朝而饔夕而飧人
莫不食也食有正味必察之而後得人或食以
濟饑未之能察也則食焉而識其正味者幾何
是故若知若愚不能外此道而為知則道常在
人而人何可離道乎今則知者知之過愚者不
及知其在知者之揣摩也猶夫愚者之昏昧也
punctuated:
類為所窘，殊不通暢，惟此作詞理兼到，是宜錄出。
考試官教諭周批：詞氣純厚，自是中庸文字樣，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭方批：體貼詳明，句句皆本色語，非性理之學不能有此。
中庸明人同具乎道之中，自失乎道之中。夫道以中為至也，人皆有之而自不察，此所以有過不及之弊歟？中庸引夫子之言，以釋首章之義如此。且道之所謂中者，乃天命人心之正，當然不易之理，固不外乎民生日用之間也。試言諸飲食：彼夫冬而湯，夏而水，人莫不飲也。飲有正味，必察之而後知。人或飲以濟渴，未之能察也，則飲焉而得其正味者幾何？朝而饔，夕而飧，人莫不食也。食有正味，必察之而後得。人或食以濟饑，未之能察也，則食焉而識其正味者幾何？是故若知若愚，不能外此道而為知，則道常在人，而人何可離道乎？今則知者知之過，愚者不及知，其在知者之揣摩也，猶夫愚者之昏昧也。
translation_en:
…most were stymied by it, and their writing was far from clear and fluent. This composition alone succeeds in both expression and reasoning; it therefore deserves inclusion.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The diction and tone are pure and substantial. This is indeed a model of writing on the Doctrine of the Mean and should be included as an example.”
Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “The interpretation is attentive, detailed, and clear; every sentence speaks in terms true to the subject. Such writing could only come from a grounding in the learning of human nature and principle.”
The Doctrine of the Mean makes clear that all people alike possess the Mean of the Way, yet themselves lose hold of it. The Way takes the Mean as its highest attainment. Everyone possesses it, yet fails to examine it: is this not why the failings of excess and deficiency arise? This is how the Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Master’s words to explain the meaning of its opening chapter. Moreover, what is called the Mean of the Way is the rectitude of the human heart ordained by Heaven—the principle of what ought to be, which does not change. It is certainly not apart from the everyday activities of human life.
Consider eating and drinking. In winter people drink hot water, and in summer cool water; everyone drinks. What one drinks has its proper flavor, which one must attend to before one can recognize it. Some people drink merely to relieve thirst and fail to attend to it. How many, then, obtain its proper flavor when they drink? People eat their morning meal and their evening meal; everyone eats. Food has its proper flavor, which one must attend to before one can apprehend it. Some people eat merely to relieve hunger and fail to attend to it. How many, then, recognize its proper flavor when they eat?
Thus, whether wise or foolish, people cannot exercise understanding apart from this Way. The Way is therefore always within people: how could people depart from it? Yet the wise now go too far in their understanding of it, while the foolish fall short of understanding it. The conjectures of the wise are just like the benightedness of the foolish. …

What one drinks has its proper flavor, which can be known only through attentive discernment. Some people drink merely to quench their thirst and cannot discern it. How many, then, drink and apprehend its proper flavor? A morning meal and an evening supper: everyone eats. Food has its proper flavor, which can be apprehended only through attentive discernment. Some people eat merely to relieve their hunger and cannot discern it. How many, then, eat and recognize its proper flavor?
Thus, whether wise or foolish, people cannot attain knowledge outside this Way. The Way is therefore always within people; how could they depart from it? Yet the wise go too far in their understanding, while the foolish fall short of understanding. The conjectural probing of the wise is just like the benighted incomprehension of the foolish.

When did he personally strap on bow case and quiver, indulge greed and anger, and vaunt his martial prowess…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
功耶列爵惟五分土惟三諸侯也其守雖不同
度突然夙夜所謹則王命焉蓋天子之所有越
志而衡行者兵固當加也於焉竭股肱之力整
卒乘之雄聲其不率之罪陳之原而肆之市同
兄弟之邦受馳驅之役歸以不恪之曲誅其君
而弔其民將見奉辭而往惟武服之是共曷敢
不稟於王假義以干國紀耶銜命而行惟師律
之是正曷敢不由其上矯制以亂天綱耶是則
天子專討則畿兵不外出而威已行諸侯致伐
===
則敵國不相征而分自定五霸之師顧不出此
其僭侈之罪大矣抑嘗觀夫子之言曰天下有
道則禮樂征伐自天子出故羲和之征史臣善
之桓公伐楚春秋譏焉聖賢傳心之法如此夫
何淮北之師美宣王之自將彤弓之錫許臣子
之專征哉噫是又可以觀聖人立教之經馭世
之權矣蓋非姬運之中衰夷狄之篡弑則淮北
幾何而不為勤遠略而彤弓不至於竊主威耶
此有天下者所以當守經而行權也
punctuated:
功耶？列爵惟五，分土惟三，諸侯也。其守雖不同度突，然夙夜所謹則王命焉。蓋天子之所有越志而衡行者，兵固當加也。於焉竭股肱之力，整卒乘之雄，聲其不率之罪，陳之原而肆之市；同兄弟之邦，受馳驅之役，歸以不恪之曲，誅其君而弔其民。將見奉辭而往，惟武服之是共，曷敢不稟於王，假義以干國紀耶？銜命而行，惟師律之是正，曷敢不由其上，矯制以亂天綱耶？是則天子專討，則畿兵不外出而威已行；諸侯致伐，則敵國不相征而分自定。五霸之師，顧不出此，其僭侈之罪大矣！
抑嘗觀夫子之言曰：「天下有道，則禮樂征伐自天子出。」故羲和之征，史臣善之；桓公伐楚，《春秋》譏焉。聖賢傳心之法如此，夫何淮北之師美宣王之自將，彤弓之錫許臣子之專征哉？噫！是又可以觀聖人立教之經、馭世之權矣。蓋非姬運之中衰、夷狄之篡弑，則淮北幾何而不為勤遠略，而彤弓不至於竊主威耶？此有天下者所以當守經而行權也。
translation_en:
…military achievements? Those whose ranks number five and whose territorial allotments fall into three classes are the feudal lords. Although the territories in their charge differ in extent [?], what they scrupulously heed day and night is the king’s command. For when, within the Son of Heaven’s dominions, there are those who exceed their proper ambitions and act wantonly, armed force must indeed be brought against them. The lords then exert all their strength as his supporting limbs, marshal their formidable soldiers and chariots, proclaim the offenders’ crime of disobedience, and expose them on the plain and display their bodies in the marketplace. Together with their brother states, they undertake the service of campaigning, lay the blame for irreverence upon the offenders, execute their rulers, and console their people. Going forth under an authoritative declaration, they attend solely to securing submission by arms. How would they dare fail to seek the king’s instructions and, under a pretext of righteousness, violate the order of the realm? Proceeding with his command, they attend solely to maintaining military discipline. How would they dare bypass their superior and falsify his decrees to disrupt Heaven’s order? Thus, when the Son of Heaven alone holds the authority to punish, his might is exercised even without the troops of the royal domain marching abroad; when the feudal lords carry out punitive campaigns, states of equal standing do not attack one another, and their respective stations are duly settled. Yet the armies of the Five Hegemons did not follow this principle. Great indeed was the guilt of their presumptuous excess!
I have also considered the Master’s words: “When the Way prevails in the world, rites, music, and punitive expeditions proceed from the Son of Heaven.” Thus the court historian approved the campaign against Xi and He, whereas the Spring and Autumn Annals censured Duke Huan’s attack on Chu. Such is the teaching through which sages and worthies transmit their understanding. Why, then, does the account of the campaign north of the Huai praise King Xuan for commanding in person, while the bestowal of the vermilion bow permits a subject to conduct campaigns on his own authority? Ah! Here too we may discern the sages’ enduring principles for establishing instruction and their discretionary measures for governing the world. Had it not been for the decline of the house of Ji and the usurpations and regicides of the Yi and Di peoples, how close would the campaign north of the Huai have come to being an exhausting pursuit of distant conquests, and would the vermilion bow not have amounted to appropriating the ruler’s authority? This is why those who possess the realm must uphold enduring principles while exercising discretion.

translation_en:
…merit? Those ranked in the five grades of nobility and allotted territory in three sizes are the feudal lords. Although their responsibilities … standards [?], what they scrupulously observe day and night is the king’s command. For all belongs to the Son of Heaven, and those who overstep his will and act perversely must surely face armed force. The lords then exert their strength as his supporting limbs, marshal their mighty troops and chariots, proclaim the offenders’ crime of disobedience, array their forces on the plain, and expose the offenders’ bodies in the marketplace. Joining with brother states, they undertake the service of campaigning, lay the blame for irreverence upon the offenders, execute their ruler, and console their people. Thus, when they go forth bearing the royal charge, they attend only to their military duties. How could they dare to proceed without reporting to the king, using righteousness as a pretext to violate the order of the realm? When they march bearing his command, they attend only to maintaining military discipline. How could they dare to bypass their superior and falsify a royal decree, disrupting Heaven’s order? Thus, when punitive authority rests exclusively with the Son of Heaven, his might is exercised even without troops leaving the royal domain; when the feudal lords carry out an attack, states of equal standing do not wage war upon one another, and their respective stations are settled of themselves. Ah! Here too we may discern the enduring principles by which the sages establish their teachings and the discretionary judgment by which they govern the world. Had the fortunes of the house of Ji not declined midway, and had the Yi and Di not committed usurpation and regicide, how close would the campaign north of the Huai have come to being an exhausting pursuit of distant conquests, and would the red bow not have amounted to appropriating the sovereign’s authority? This is why one who possesses all under Heaven must uphold enduring principles while exercising discretion.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
本然之誠是立樞機謹擇而固有之真是存則
見於事者有不自知其積而廣大之境可入矣
夫忠信固所以進德然何如而見其德之進耶
蓋理得於心至善而无惡者謂之至至乃幾之
所在也真知為吾所當止之處內主忠信以至
之是行雖未至而知有所先則於至之所在而
為幾之所在者可與知之而不昧矣德有不進
者歟脩辭立誠固所以居業抑何如而見其業
之居耶蓋理見於事至當而歸一者謂之終終
===
乃義之所在也灼見為吾所終止之方脩辭立
誠以終之是知已在先而行復克副則於終之
所在而為義之所在者可與存之而不失矣業
有不居者歟是則進德者心也內也脩業者事
也外也九三君子之學內外兩進此所以終日
乾乾而无咎者豈易得哉大抵憂所當憂而卒
於无憂懼所當懼而卒於无懼此理之必然者
九三君子聖人之德備矣今一處乎危地且進
脩惕厲以求无過若是其勤也世有一善不聞
punctuated: 本然之誠是立，樞機謹擇，而固有之真是存，則見於事者有不自知其積，而廣大之境可入矣。夫忠信固所以進德，然何如而見其德之進耶？蓋理得於心，至善而无惡者謂之至，至乃幾之所在也。真知為吾所當止之處，內主忠信以至之，是行雖未至而知有所先，則於至之所在而為幾之所在者，可與知之而不昧矣。德有不進者歟？脩辭立誠固所以居業，抑何如而見其業之居耶？蓋理見於事，至當而歸一者謂之終，終乃義之所在也。灼見為吾所終止之方，脩辭立誠以終之，是知已在先而行復克副，則於終之所在而為義之所在者，可與存之而不失矣。業有不居者歟？是則進德者，心也，內也；脩業者，事也，外也。九三君子之學，內外兩進，此所以終日乾乾而无咎者，豈易得哉！大抵憂所當憂而卒於无憂，懼所當懼而卒於无懼，此理之必然者。九三君子，聖人之德備矣。今一處乎危地，且進脩惕厲以求无過，若是其勤也。世有一善不聞
translation_en:
…inherent sincerity is thereby established; the pivotal workings of speech are carefully considered, and one’s innate genuineness is preserved. Then, in what is manifested in affairs, achievements accumulate without one’s even being aware of them, and the realm of breadth and greatness becomes accessible. Truly recognizing it as the place where one ought to abide, one inwardly takes loyalty and trustworthiness as one’s guiding principles in order to reach it. title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
本然之誠是立樞機謹擇而固有之真是存則
見於事者有不自知其積而廣大之境可入矣
夫忠信固所以進德然何如而見其德之進耶
蓋理得於心至善而无惡者謂之至至乃幾之
所在也真知為吾所當止之處内主忠信以至
之是行雖未至而知有所先則於至之所在而
為幾之所在者可與知之而不昧矣德有不進
者歟脩辭立誠固所以居業抑何如而見其業
之居耶蓋理見於事至當而歸一者謂之終終
===
乃義之所在也灼見為吾所終止之方脩辭立
誠以終之是知已在先而行復克副則於終之
所在而為義之所在者可與存之而不失矣業
有不居者歟是則進德者心也内也脩業者事
也外也九三君子之學内外兩進此所以終日
乾乾而无咎者豈易得哉大抵憂所當憂而卒
於无憂懼所當懼而卒於无懼此理之必然者
九三君子聖人之德備矣今一處乎危地且進
脩惕厲以求无過若是其勤也世有一善不聞

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄

而冥行无忌者欲其不陷於危難矣哉噫其亦
不占者也
歸竒於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後

===

間歸之蓋有定在焉歸竒於扐如此蓋掛一揲

This is gathered and lodged between the second and third fingers of the left hand; there is a fixed place for putting it. Such is the procedure for placing the remainder between the fingers. For hanging one stalk and counting off…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
左扐左象夫三歲積盈虛之餘日分而為一閏
也揲右扐右象夫五歲積盈虛之餘日合而為
再閏也所謂歸餘有所合者如此然筮法再扐
後掛者何耶蓋曆法五歲之間既積餘以一閏
復積餘以再閏矣然後別起積分故揲蓍之法
左右之策既各一揲而一扐矣于是別起掛一
以為後變之始求卦之方既四揲左右之策而
歸奇矣于焉別起一掛以為後變之端九變而
成三畫雖曰得乎內卦也其間凡有再扐者莫
===
不皆然否則蓍策无窮其變未終何以前萬民
之用哉十有八變成卦雖曰得乎全體也其中
凡有再扐者罔不皆爾否則蓍數无端其變未
竟何以决斯世之疑哉所謂再變有所始者如
此是則曆法難知也而策法與之合筮法至妙
也而曆法與之準大傳聖人闡之以告人得无
意歟抑論之聖人幽贊於神明而生蓍參天兩
地而倚數筮法之立豈但象閏而已耶觀其分
二以象兩儀掛一以象三才揲四以象四時何
punctuated:
左，扐左，象夫三歲積盈虛之餘日，分而為一閏也；揲右，扐右，象夫五歲積盈虛之餘日，合而為再閏也。所謂歸餘有所合者如此。然筮法再扐後掛者何耶？蓋曆法五歲之間，既積餘以一閏，復積餘以再閏矣，然後別起積分。故揲蓍之法，左右之策既各一揲而一扐矣，于是別起掛一，以為後變之始。求卦之方，既四揲左右之策而歸奇矣，于焉別起一掛，以為後變之端。九變而成三畫，雖曰得乎內卦也，其間凡有再扐者，莫不皆然。否則蓍策无窮，其變未終，何以前萬民之用哉？十有八變成卦，雖曰得乎全體也，其中凡有再扐者，罔不皆爾。否則蓍數无端，其變未竟，何以决斯世之疑哉？所謂再變有所始者如此。
是則曆法難知也，而策法與之合；筮法至妙也，而曆法與之準。《大傳》聖人闡之以告人，得无意歟？抑論之，聖人幽贊於神明而生蓍，參天兩地而倚數，筮法之立，豈但象閏而已耶？觀其分二以象兩儀，掛一以象三才，揲四以象四時，何
translation_en:
…counting the left-hand stalks and placing their remainder between the fingers symbolizes how, over three years, the surplus days arising from the discrepancy between the solar and lunar cycles accumulate, their fractions making up one intercalary month. Counting the right-hand stalks and placing their remainder between the fingers symbolizes how, over five years, those surplus days accumulate and combine to produce a second intercalary month. This is what is meant by saying that gathering the remainders has its corresponding significance. But why does the divination procedure prescribe setting aside a stalk after placing the remainders between the fingers twice? In calendrical reckoning, within five years the surplus is accumulated to make one intercalary month, and then accumulated again to make a second. Only then does a new accumulation of fractions begin. Thus, in the method of counting milfoil stalks, once the stalks on both left and right have each been counted and their remainders placed between the fingers, one begins anew by setting aside a single stalk to initiate the next transformation. In the procedure for obtaining a hexagram, once the stalks on the left and right have been counted in fours and the remainders gathered, one again sets aside a single stalk to begin the next transformation. Nine transformations produce three lines. Although this yields the inner trigram, every instance of placing the remainders between the fingers twice within that process follows this same rule. Otherwise, the manipulation of the milfoil stalks would continue endlessly and the transformations would never reach completion: how could they guide the undertakings of the myriad people? Eighteen transformations produce a hexagram. Although this yields the complete figure, every instance of placing the remainders between the fingers twice within it follows this same rule. Otherwise, the reckoning of the milfoil stalks would have no bounds and the transformations would remain unfinished: how could they resolve the doubts of the world? This is what is meant by saying that a further transformation has its prescribed beginning.
Thus, although calendrical reckoning is difficult to understand, the method of manipulating the stalks accords with it; although the divination procedure is supremely subtle, calendrical reckoning provides its counterpart. Could the sage have had no purpose in elucidating this for people in the Great Commentary (Dazhuan)? To discuss it further, the sage mysteriously assisted the spiritual powers and brought forth the milfoil, assigning three to Heaven and two to Earth and basing the numbers upon them. Could the establishment of the divination procedure have been intended merely to symbolize intercalation? Consider how dividing the stalks into two symbolizes the Two Modes, Heaven and Earth; setting aside one symbolizes the Three Powers, Heaven, Earth, and humanity; and counting in fours symbolizes the four seasons. How…

Counting the right-hand stalks and lodging their remainder between the fingers represents the surplus days accumulated over five years from those excesses and shortfalls, combined to constitute a second intercalary month. This is what is meant by saying that setting aside the remainders has its correspondence.

But why does the divination procedure call for suspending a stalk after lodging the remainders twice? In calendrical reckoning, within five years the surplus is accumulated to produce one intercalary month, and then accumulated again to produce a second. Only afterward does the accumulation of fractional days begin anew. Thus, in the method of counting milfoil stalks, once the stalks on the left and right have each been counted and their remainders lodged between the fingers, one stalk is suspended anew to begin the next transformation. In the procedure for obtaining a hexagram, once the stalks on the left and right have been counted in groups of four and their remainders set aside, a fresh suspension of one stalk initiates the next transformation. Nine transformations produce three lines. Although this may be called obtaining the inner trigram, every instance within it of lodging the remainders twice follows this same procedure. Otherwise, the counting of milfoil stalks would go on without limit and its transformations would never end: how could it enable the myriad people to undertake their affairs?

Eighteen transformations complete a hexagram. Although this may be called obtaining the whole figure, every instance within it of lodging the remainders twice follows this same procedure. Otherwise, the reckoning of milfoil stalks would have no endpoint and its transformations would remain unfinished: how could it resolve the doubts of this world? This is what is meant by saying that renewed transformation has a starting point. Thus, although calendrical reckoning is difficult to understand, the method of counting stalks accords with it; although the method of divination is supremely subtle, calendrical reckoning corresponds to it. Could the sage have expounded this in the Great Commentary to instruct people without an intention?

To consider the matter further: the sage mysteriously assisted the spiritual powers and brought forth milfoil, assigning three to Heaven and two to Earth and basing the numbers upon them. Could the establishment of the divination procedure have been intended merely to represent intercalation? Observe how dividing the stalks into two represents the Two Modes, suspending one represents the Three Powers, and counting in groups of four represents the four seasons—how…

正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
苗而贊之以此若曰今茲師舉三旬而苗猶未
服意者威武不足恃而德化有未至乎夫德者
人心同然之善天人感應之機人惟無德耳德
則發乎邇見乎遠自升聞於亭毒之表誠於此
形於彼自旁達乎沖漠之虛然則還兵而脩德
者此其時也況乎忽持盈之戒而充然自足不
期損而必損守撝謙之行而卑以自牧不求益
而受益是乃天道之自然而非人力之所能違
也曷亦觀諸帝乎帝初於歷山之下往于畒畝
===
之時于旻天于父母日以號泣惟怨慕之不已
負其罪引其慝痛自克責一懟尤之不存于焉
敬其為子之職以往見之而惟恐少違其志竭
其事親之敬以承順之而惟恐不得其心帝之
誠孝如此瞽瞍亦信而順之也然豈惟是哉神
明之幽視之有弗見也至誠之馨香有以感之
亦且為之來格況蕞爾有苗矣乎聽之有弗聞
也誠意之精華有以格之亦且為之時歆況蠢
茲有苗矣乎是則感化之理遠而天愚而瞽瞍
punctuated: 苗，而贊之以此，若曰：「今茲師舉三旬，而苗猶未服，意者威武不足恃，而德化有未至乎？夫德者，人心同然之善，天人感應之機。人惟無德耳，德則發乎邇，見乎遠，自升聞於亭毒之表；誠於此，形於彼，自旁達乎沖漠之虛。然則還兵而脩德者，此其時也。況乎忽持盈之戒，而充然自足，不期損而必損；守撝謙之行，而卑以自牧，不求益而受益。是乃天道之自然，而非人力之所能違也。曷亦觀諸帝乎？帝初於歷山之下，往于畒畝之時，于旻天，于父母，日以號泣，惟怨慕之不已；負其罪，引其慝，痛自克責，一懟尤之不存。于焉敬其為子之職，以往見之，而惟恐少違其志；竭其事親之敬，以承順之，而惟恐不得其心。帝之誠孝如此，瞽瞍亦信而順之也。然豈惟是哉？神明之幽，視之有弗見也，至誠之馨香有以感之，亦且為之來格，況蕞爾有苗矣乎？聽之有弗聞也，誠意之精華有以格之，亦且為之時歆，況蠢茲有苗矣乎？是則感化之理，遠而天，愚而瞽瞍
translation_en:
…the Miao, and encouraged him with these words, as if to say: “Now the army has been in the field for thirty days, yet the Miao have still not submitted. Might it be that military might cannot be relied upon, and that the transforming influence of virtue has not yet reached them? Virtue is the goodness shared alike by human hearts, the mainspring of sympathetic response between Heaven and humanity. The only difficulty is that people lack virtue. When virtue is present, it issues forth nearby and becomes manifest afar; of itself its renown rises beyond the realm of Heaven’s nurturing care. Sincerity here takes visible form there; of itself it reaches throughout the vast, formless void. Thus, now is the time to recall the troops and cultivate virtue. Moreover, one who neglects the warning to take care when holding a full vessel, and becomes complacently self-satisfied, will certainly suffer loss, though he does not expect it. One who maintains the practice of manifesting humility and disciplines himself through modesty receives increase without seeking it. This is the natural course of Heaven’s Way, which human strength cannot contravene.

“Why not also consider the Emperor [Shun]? In his early days, when he went out into the fields below Mount Li, he cried and wept daily to merciful Heaven and to his parents, unceasing in his sorrow and yearning for their affection. He took the blame upon himself and acknowledged faults as his own, painfully restraining and reproaching himself, without harboring the slightest resentment or impulse to blame others. Thus he conscientiously fulfilled his duties as a son, going to see his parents with only the fear that he might depart even slightly from their wishes. He exhausted his reverence in serving them and complied with them, fearing only that he might fail to win their hearts. Such was the Emperor’s sincere filial devotion that Gusou, too, trusted him and became well disposed toward him.

“Yet was this all? The spirits are hidden: one may look for them and fail to see them. Yet the fragrance of perfect sincerity can move them, so that even they come into one’s presence. How much more, then, those insignificant Youmiao! One may listen for the spirits and fail to hear them. Yet the pure essence of sincere intent can reach them, so that even they duly come to savor the offerings. How much more, then, these benighted Youmiao! Thus, the principle of transformation through moral influence extends to what is as distant as Heaven and as obtuse as Gusou…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
幽而鬼神皆不出乎德之外也由是而增脩其
德焉何患乎有苗大抵莫強於人心而可以義
動可以仁感莫柔於人心而不可以威劫不可
以力屈苗亦人耳而豈威武之可服哉伯益有
見於此而歷言以賛之禹即班師而不以為屈
舜即敷德而不以為嫌卒之有苗之格無不中
吾意料之所及者則苗也可謂無負於舜而舜
禹無負於伯益也所謂一乃心力其克有勳者
信夫
===
不作無益害有益功乃成不貴異物賤用
物民乃足
唐脩
同考試官教諭李批通篇無陳言無俗氣
讀之令人洒然
考試官教諭周批說召公進戒之意明
白通暢諸作不及
考試官教諭方批體認親切筆力清健
殆有識之士也允宜高薦
punctuated:
幽而鬼神，皆不出乎德之外也。由是而增脩其德焉，何患乎有苗？大抵莫強於人心，而可以義動，可以仁感；莫柔於人心，而不可以威劫，不可以力屈。苗亦人耳，而豈威武之可服哉？伯益有見於此，而歷言以賛之。禹即班師而不以為屈，舜即敷德而不以為嫌。卒之有苗之格，無不中吾意料之所及者。則苗也，可謂無負於舜，而舜禹無負於伯益也。所謂「一乃心力，其克有勳」者，信夫！

不作無益害有益，功乃成；不貴異物賤用物，民乃足。

唐脩

同考試官教諭李批：通篇無陳言，無俗氣，讀之令人洒然。

考試官教諭周批：說召公進戒之意，明白通暢，諸作不及。

考試官教諭方批：體認親切，筆力清健，殆有識之士也。允宜高薦。
translation_en:
…and even spirits in their hidden realm—all lie within the reach of virtue. By further cultivating his virtue on this basis, what need had he to worry about the Youmiao? In general, nothing is stronger than the human heart, yet righteousness can move it and benevolence can touch it; nothing is more yielding than the human heart, yet threats cannot compel it and force cannot subdue it. The Miao, too, are human: how could military might secure their submission? Boyi understood this and explained it point by point to support his counsel. Yu thereupon withdrew his troops without regarding this as a humiliation; Shun thereupon spread his virtue without misgivings. In the end, the submission of the Youmiao fell entirely within what we could have anticipated. Thus it may be said that the Miao did not fail Shun, and that Shun and Yu did not fail Boyi. How true are the words: “Unite your minds and strength, and you will achieve merit”!

“Do not undertake useless things to the detriment of useful ones, and your work will be accomplished; do not prize exotic objects while slighting useful goods, and the people will have enough.”

Tang Xiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Throughout the piece there are neither hackneyed expressions nor vulgarity. Reading it leaves one refreshed.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The explanation of the Duke of Shao’s purpose in offering admonition is clear and fluent. The other compositions do not equal it.

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: His understanding is intimate and precise, and his writing lucid and vigorous. He is surely a man of discernment and fully deserves recommendation for a high place.

text:
詩
既見君子錫我百朋
陳汝謨
同考試官教諭楊批菁莪一題場中多為所
窘清麗可愛者僅見此篇
考試官教諭周批辭味雋永善說詩者
考試官教諭方批明暢可錄
詩人於所見之賓必狀其至悅之情也甚矣詩
人之好賢也今於所見之賓而必狀其至悅之
===
情焉宜其燕飲之際而咏歌之也歟菁莪詩人
之意蓋謂好賢之誠既通見賢之樂斯盛凡爾
君子皆我良翰鴻漸之儀昔蓋可望而不可即
矣今也萃止於鐘鼓既設之餘龍光之德昔嘗
可聞而不可覩矣今也既覯於承筐是將之頃
中而和順外而英華咸奉我以周旋傾戴散而
為笑語矣音為金玉質為圭璋舉接我以宴好
歆慕轉而為獻酬矣是君子之既見其喜幸之
何如彼世之所嗜者貨也茲焉見彼君子喜樂
punctuated:
詩

既見君子，錫我百朋。

陳汝謨

同考試官教諭楊批：「菁莪一題，場中多為所窘，清麗可愛者僅見此篇。」

考試官教諭周批：「辭味雋永，善說詩者。」

考試官教諭方批：「明暢可錄。」

詩人於所見之賓，必狀其至悅之情也。甚矣，詩人之好賢也！今於所見之賓，而必狀其至悅之情焉，宜其燕飲之際而咏歌之也歟！菁莪詩人之意，蓋謂好賢之誠既通，見賢之樂斯盛。凡爾君子，皆我良翰。鴻漸之儀，昔蓋可望而不可即矣，今也萃止於鐘鼓既設之餘；龍光之德，昔嘗可聞而不可覩矣，今也既覯於承筐是將之頃。中而和順，外而英華，咸奉我以周旋，傾戴散而為笑語矣；音為金玉，質為圭璋，舉接我以宴好，歆慕轉而為獻酬矣。是君子之既見，其喜幸之何如！彼世之所嗜者貨也，茲焉見彼君子，喜樂
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Having seen the gentleman, he bestows on me a hundred strings of cowries.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “The topic ‘Luxuriant Southernwood’ (Jing e) troubled many candidates in the examination hall. This is the only essay I have seen that is lucid, elegant, and pleasing.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The language has a lasting savor: here is someone skilled at interpreting the Odes.”

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: “Clear and fluent; worthy of inclusion.”

When the poet sees his guests, he invariably depicts his utmost delight. How profound is the poet’s love of worthy men! Since he must express his utmost delight in the guests he sees, is it not fitting that he should chant and sing of it while feasting and drinking? The intention of the poet of ‘Luxuriant Southernwood’ is presumably this: once his sincere love of worthy men has been communicated, his joy in seeing them becomes abundant. All you gentlemen are my excellent supports. Your bearing, like wild geese advancing in flight, could formerly be admired from afar but could not be approached; now you have gathered here after the bells and drums have been set out. Your virtue, radiant with glorious favor, could formerly be heard of but could not be seen; now it has come into view as the baskets are presented.

Harmonious and gentle within, splendid and refined without, you all favor me with your gracious company, and wholehearted reverence unfolds into laughter and conversation. Your voices are like gold and jade, your character like the ceremonial jade tablets gui and zhang; you all meet me in festive friendship, and admiration turns into the offering and returning of wine cups. Now that these gentlemen have been seen, how great the joy and good fortune! What the world covets is wealth; here, on seeing these gentlemen, the joy…

旣見君子錫我百朋
陳汝謨
同考試官教諭楊批菁莪一題場中多為所
窘清麗可愛者僅見此篇
考試官教諭周批辭味雋永善說詩者
考試官教諭方批明暢可錄
詩人於所見之賓必狀其至悅之情也甚矣詩
人之好賢也今於所見之賓而必狀其至悅之
===
情焉宜其燕飲之際而咏歌之也歟菁莪詩人
之意蓋謂好賢之誠旣通見賢之樂斯盛凡爾
君子皆我良翰鴻漸之儀昔蓋可望而不可即
矣今也萃止於鐘鼓旣設之餘龍光之德昔嘗
可聞而不可覩矣今也旣覯於承筐是將之頃
中而和順外而英華咸奉我以周旋傾戴散而
為笑語矣音為金玉質為圭璋舉接我以宴好
歆慕轉而為獻酬矣是君子之旣見其喜幸之
何如彼世之所嗜者貨也茲焉見彼君子喜樂
punctuated:
詩
旣見君子，錫我百朋。
陳汝謨

同考試官教諭楊批：「菁莪一題，場中多為所窘，清麗可愛者僅見此篇。」
考試官教諭周批：「辭味雋永，善說詩者。」
考試官教諭方批：「明暢可錄。」

詩人於所見之賓，必狀其至悅之情也。甚矣，詩人之好賢也！今於所見之賓，而必狀其至悅之情焉，宜其燕飲之際而咏歌之也歟！菁莪詩人之意，蓋謂好賢之誠旣通，見賢之樂斯盛。凡爾君子，皆我良翰。鴻漸之儀，昔蓋可望而不可即矣，今也萃止於鐘鼓旣設之餘；龍光之德，昔嘗可聞而不可覩矣，今也旣覯於承筐是將之頃。中而和順，外而英華，咸奉我以周旋，傾戴散而為笑語矣；音為金玉，質為圭璋，舉接我以宴好，歆慕轉而為獻酬矣。是君子之旣見，其喜幸之何如！彼世之所嗜者，貨也；茲焉見彼君子，喜樂
translation_en:
Book of Odes
“Having seen the gentlemen, it is as though I had been bestowed a hundred strings of cowries.”
Chen Rumo

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “The topic from ‘Luxuriant Southernwood’ (Jing’e) left many candidates at a loss. This is the only essay I have seen that is limpid, elegant, and delightful.”
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The language has a rich and lasting savor: here is someone skilled at expounding the Odes.”
Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: “Clear and fluent; worthy of inclusion.”

In speaking of the guests he has met, the poet unfailingly depicts his feelings of utmost delight. How profound is the poet’s love of worthy men! Since he must depict his utmost delight in the guests he has met, is it not fitting that he should sing of it at the banquet? The intention of the poet of ‘Luxuriant Southernwood’ is, surely, that once his sincere love of worthy men has found expression and response, his joy in meeting them flourishes. All you gentlemen are my trusty supports. Your bearing, like wild geese advancing in flight, could formerly be admired from afar but not approached; now you have gathered here after the bells and drums have been set out. Your virtue, radiant with glory, could formerly be heard of but not witnessed; now it is seen as the baskets are presented in offering. Harmonious and compliant within, splendid and refined without, you all honor me with your gracious company, and heartfelt devotion flows forth in laughter and conversation. Your voices are like gold and jade, your substance like the gui and zhang ceremonial jades; all of you meet me in convivial friendship, and admiration becomes the offering and returning of wine cups. Having now met these gentlemen, how great are my joy and good fortune! What the world covets is wealth; here, on seeing these gentlemen, joy and delight …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之心生如重貨之多於我乎予也人之所欲者
利也茲焉見此君子愛悅之情至如竒貨之溢
於我乎居也初筵之間人徒見其溫溫之恭而
已抑不知上下胥悅周行所示若披寶藏之府
而觀其富有方以百朋之貺何過乎几席之上
人徒見其衎衎之樂而已抑不知君臣交會忠
告所益若發良賈之積而見其深藏儗以多貝
之獲何泰乎噫周王於燕飲之歌而極道其見
賢之喜如此盛時君臣相與氣象豈不於是而
===
見歟大抵上下之交豈可以聲音笑貌為哉蓋
必有真德實意潛孚默運乎其間然後可以感
人心而成德業也周之王者有知乎此因其飲
食而制為禮法鹿鳴之歌菁莪之咏其所以交
上下而感人心者如此故得人之效至為天子
使而媚于庶人焉嗚呼盛矣君人者其尚鑒茲
哉
在彼無惡在此無斁庶幾夙夜以永終譽
費順
punctuated:
之心生，如重貨之多於我乎予也。人之所欲者利也，茲焉見此君子，愛悅之情至，如竒貨之溢於我乎居也。初筵之間，人徒見其溫溫之恭而已，抑不知上下胥悅，周行所示，若披寶藏之府而觀其富有，方以百朋之貺，何過乎？几席之上，人徒見其衎衎之樂而已，抑不知君臣交會，忠告所益，若發良賈之積而見其深藏，儗以多貝之獲，何泰乎？噫！周王於燕飲之歌，而極道其見賢之喜如此，盛時君臣相與氣象，豈不於是而見歟？大抵上下之交，豈可以聲音笑貌為哉？蓋必有真德實意潛孚默運乎其間，然後可以感人心而成德業也。周之王者有知乎此，因其飲食而制為禮法。《鹿鳴》之歌，《菁莪》之咏，其所以交上下而感人心者如此。故得人之效，至為天子使而媚于庶人焉。嗚呼，盛矣！君人者其尚鑒茲哉！

在彼無惡，在此無斁，庶幾夙夜，以永終譽。

費順
translation_en:
…a feeling of joy arises, as though precious goods had been bestowed upon me in abundance. What people desire is profit; here, upon seeing this gentleman, feelings of affection and delight reach their height, as though rare treasures filled my dwelling to overflowing.

At the opening of the banquet, people see only his gentle reverence. They do not realize that those above and below delight in one another, and that what the ranks of worthy men reveal is like opening a treasury and beholding its abundance. How could comparing this to a gift of a hundred strings of cowries be excessive? Among the tables and mats, people see only his cheerful pleasure. They do not realize that ruler and ministers meet in fellowship, and that the benefit of loyal counsel is like opening a skilled merchant’s stores and seeing his deeply hoarded wealth. How could comparing this to acquiring many cowries be extravagant?

Ah! In this song of feasting, the king of Zhou expresses to the utmost his joy at meeting worthy men. Does not the spirit of fellowship between ruler and ministers in a flourishing age become visible here? Generally speaking, how could relations between those above and below be sustained merely by tones of voice, smiles, and outward expressions? Genuine virtue and sincere intent must inspire unspoken trust and work silently between them; only then can they move people’s hearts and bring virtuous achievements to fruition.

The kings of Zhou understood this, and established ritual rules around their eating and drinking. Such was the means by which the song “The Deer Call” (Lu ming) and the ode “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing e) united those above and below and moved people’s hearts. Thus, the results of securing worthy men extended to their serving as the Son of Heaven’s envoys and winning the affection of the common people. Ah, how flourishing it was! May those who rule others take this as their mirror!

“Over there, let there be no hatred; here, let there be no weariness. May you, morning and night, forever preserve your good name to the end.”

Fei Shun

translation_en:
…such a feeling arises, as though abundant precious goods had been bestowed upon me [?]. What people desire is benefit. Now, on seeing this gentleman, the affection and delight felt are as though rare goods filled my dwelling [?]. At the beginning of the banquet, people see only his gentle reverence. They do not realize that those above and below delight in one another, and that the perfect way shown to him is like opening a treasury and beholding its riches. How could comparing this to a gift of a hundred strings of cowries be excessive? At the banquet tables, people see only his joyful ease.
