I was once perplexed by these judgments. Only upon considering the events of protecting and preserving half the realm [?] and personally supporting the imperial chariot did I understand that the Duke of Wen's judgment arose entirely from impartiality, and that Qinruo's slander could still serve as a check upon men of learning, while…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
逢君之惡者亦不容已於譏且病耳若夫
董仲舒潜心大業而真氏論其流於災異
楊子雲博極群書而程子貶其首撰美新
王褒著僮約而顏氏示戒韓愈頌聖德而
子由鄙焉夫以仲舒承秦滅學之後六經
離析之餘賢良之策度越諸子其推陰陽
錯行之故蓋有得乎春秋災異之變視雄
承諛之語可並觀耶昌黎文起八代之衰
道濟天下之溺泰山北斗學者依歸其警
藩鎮叛逆之意蓋脗合乎風雅勸懲之旨
楊雄王褒之文可例論耶執此以往則先
正之取舍後賢之定論可具見矣雖然有
三義焉蓋自其一者而論之必德盛者業
可大而言可法也自其分者而言之蘊之
為德發之為功為言也自其脩於人者言
之天質之美固不足以勝其涵養之力也
是以原之忠黯之直張之烈冠之斷董之
學得本原韓之佐佑六經皆有端厚以為
punctuated:
逢君之惡者，亦不容已於譏且病耳。若夫董仲舒潜心大業，而真氏論其流於災異；楊子雲博極群書，而程子貶其首撰《美新》；王褒著《僮約》，而顏氏示戒；韓愈頌聖德，而子由鄙焉。夫以仲舒承秦滅學之後、六經離析之餘，賢良之策度越諸子，其推陰陽錯行之故，蓋有得乎《春秋》災異之變，視雄承諛之語，可並觀耶？昌黎文起八代之衰，道濟天下之溺，泰山北斗，學者依歸；其警藩鎮叛逆之意，蓋脗合乎風雅勸懲之旨，楊雄、王褒之文，可例論耶？執此以往，則先正之取舍、後賢之定論，可具見矣。
雖然，有三義焉。蓋自其一者而論之，必德盛者，業可大而言可法也；自其分者而言之，蘊之為德，發之為功、為言也；自其脩於人者言之，天質之美，固不足以勝其涵養之力也。是以原之忠、黯之直、張之烈、冠之斷、董之學得本原、韓之佐佑六經，皆有端厚以為
translation_en:
…those who accommodate their ruler’s wickedness likewise cannot be spared criticism and censure. As for Dong Zhongshu, he devoted himself to the great undertaking, yet Master Zhen argued that he strayed into the study of calamities and anomalies. Yang Ziyun read widely through the whole range of books, yet Master Cheng disparaged him for taking the lead in composing In Praise of Xin. Wang Bao wrote the Contract with a Bondservant, and Master Yan held it up as a warning. Han Yu praised imperial virtue, yet Ziyou scorned him. Zhongshu lived after the Qin destruction of learning, when the Six Classics had been fragmented and scattered. His policy essays for the examination of Worthy and Good candidates surpassed the writings of the various masters. His investigation of why yin and yang operate out of order surely grasped something of the changes manifested in the calamities and anomalies recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Can this be placed on a par with Yang Xiong’s flattering words? Han Yu of Changli revived literature after eight dynasties of decline, and his Way rescued the world from drowning. Like Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper, he was a guide to whom scholars turned. His intention to warn against rebellion by the regional military commands surely accorded with the purpose of encouragement and admonition in the Airs and Odes. Can the writings of Yang Xiong and Wang Bao be judged in the same category? Applying this principle further, we can fully discern the grounds on which earlier worthies accepted or rejected these men, and the settled judgments of later sages.
Even so, there are three meanings here. Considered in their unity, only someone whose virtue is abundant can achieve great things and utter words worthy of emulation. Considered in their distinct aspects, what is stored within is virtue; what issues forth is achievement and speech. Considered in terms of human cultivation, the excellence of one’s natural endowment certainly cannot outweigh the power of sustained moral nurture. Thus, the loyalty of Qu Yuan, the uprightness of Ji An, the staunchness of Zhang Xun, the decisiveness of Guan [?], Dong Zhongshu’s learning that grasped the fundamental source, and Han Yu’s support of the Six Classics all had integrity and generosity of character to serve as…

translation_en:
…those who abet their ruler’s wrongdoing likewise cannot escape criticism and censure. Dong Zhongshu devoted himself to the great undertaking of learning, yet Master Zhen criticized him for straying into the study of calamities and anomalies. Yang Ziyun ranged broadly through all the books, yet Master Cheng disparaged him for taking the lead in composing In Praise of the Xin Dynasty. Wang Bao wrote the Contract with a Servant, and Master Yan held it up as a warning. Han Yu praised sagely virtue, yet Ziyou disdained his work.

Now Zhongshu lived after the Qin destruction of learning, when the Six Classics had been scattered and fragmented. His policy responses in the examination for the Worthy and Good surpassed the writings of the various masters. His investigation of why yin and yang operate out of order surely grasped something of the changes manifested in the calamities and anomalies recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Can this be considered on a par with Yang Xiong’s words of ingratiating flattery? Han Yu of Changli revived literary writing after eight dynasties of decline, and through the Way rescued the world from drowning. Like Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper, he was the guide to whom scholars turned. His intention to warn against rebellion by the regional military commands surely accorded with the purpose of encouragement and admonition in the Airs and Odes. Can his work be discussed in the same category as Wang Bao’s useless writing? Following this reasoning, we can fully discern both the choices of earlier worthies and the settled judgments of later sages.

Nevertheless, there are three principles here. Considered in their unity, only one whose virtue is abundant can accomplish great deeds and utter words worthy of emulation. Considered separately, what is stored within is virtue; what issues forth becomes achievement and expression. Considered in terms of personal cultivation, the excellence of one’s natural endowment certainly cannot surpass the power of sustained self-cultivation. Thus Yuan’s loyalty, An’s uprightness, Zhang’s staunchness, Kou’s decisiveness, Dong’s learning that reached the fundamental source, and Han’s support of the Six Classics all possessed uprightness and integrity to serve as…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之質剛大以為之氣而濟之以雄偉不常
之才考其所立德雖未合乎中庸功則高
視乎一世而其言又有聖人之道賴之以
復明者多矣後之論者猶復云爾何哉蓋
聖賢之學體用一原而存養之密內外兼
致故其德足以動高玄功足以周物務而
其言又足以宣人文而憲萬世自夫道學
不明而人才之成就大抵不能無可論者
要亦非數子之責也然愚竊有憾焉原之
===
怨黜之忿寇之不學韓之好進此君子所
以喜其天質之美而惜其涵養之力也嗚
呼孰謂千載而下而有仲舒之醇正睢陽
之忠義者哉謹對
第三問
楊琇
同考試官教諭常批評論古人行事得失乃
學者一項窮理工夫所不可缺然非博極群書不能也
今子於此條答無遺豈非尚友者耶
punctuated:
之質，剛大以為之氣，而濟之以雄偉不常之才。考其所立，德雖未合乎中庸，功則高視乎一世，而其言又有聖人之道賴之以復明者多矣。後之論者猶復云爾，何哉？蓋聖賢之學，體用一原，而存養之密，內外兼致，故其德足以動高玄，功足以周物務，而其言又足以宣人文而憲萬世。自夫道學不明，而人才之成就，大抵不能無可論者，要亦非數子之責也。然愚竊有憾焉：原之怨，黜之忿，寇之不學，韓之好進，此君子所以喜其天質之美而惜其涵養之力也。嗚呼！孰謂千載而下，而有仲舒之醇正、睢陽之忠義者哉？謹對。

第三問
楊琇

同考試官教諭常批：評論古人行事得失，乃學者一項窮理工夫所不可缺，然非博極群書不能也。今子於此條答無遺，豈非尚友者耶？
translation_en:
…as their substance, with firmness and greatness as their vital force, supplemented by outstanding and extraordinary talent. Examining what they established, although their virtue did not fully accord with the Mean, their achievements towered above their age; and in many instances their words enabled the Way of the sages to shine forth anew. Why, then, do later critics still speak thus? In the learning of sages and worthies, substance and function share a single source. Their meticulous preservation and cultivation of the mind extend fully to both the inner and the outer. Thus their virtue can move the lofty heavens, their achievements can encompass worldly affairs, and their words can give expression to human culture and serve as a model for ten thousand generations. Since the learning of the Way became obscure, the attainments of talented men have generally been open to criticism. Ultimately, this is not the responsibility of these few men alone. Yet I venture to harbor some regrets: Qu Yuan’s resentment, Ji An’s indignation [黜, probably a garbled name, ?], Kou Zhun’s lack of learning, and Han Yu’s eagerness for advancement. These are why the gentleman delights in the beauty of their innate qualities but regrets the inadequacy of their efforts at self-cultivation. Alas! Who would say that, a thousand years later, there would be men possessing Zhongshu’s purity and rectitude or Suiyang’s loyalty and righteousness? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Third Question
Yang Xiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chang, Instructor: To assess the merits and faults of the ancients’ conduct is an indispensable part of a scholar’s work of investigating principle. Yet one cannot accomplish it without reading widely and thoroughly among the books. Now you have answered this question point by point, omitting nothing. Are you not one who seeks friendship with the worthies of antiquity?

translation_en:
…in their native disposition, with firmness and greatness constituting their vital force, supplemented by extraordinary talents of heroic stature. Examining their accomplishments, although their virtue did not fully accord with the Mean, their achievements towered above their age; and in many instances their words enabled the Way of the sages to shine forth again. Third Policy Question
Yang Xiu
Associate Examiner Chang, Instructor, comments: Assessing the merits and faults of the actions of men of antiquity is an indispensable part of a scholar’s work of investigating principle. Are you not one who seeks friendship with the worthy men of the past?

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭周批觀此一策蓋博學宏辭
之流也健羨健羨
考試官敎諭方批叙事詳盡而斷制精明
非若左氏專以成敗論事者矣佳士佳士
不患乎疑事之難決而貴存至公之心不
畏乎眾論之難折而貴操大中之矩蓋公
則不私而天下之猶豫自定中則不偏而
天下之議論自明不私不偏其於眾言之
混淆吾折以本然之則而有餘力尚何狐
===
疑之患哉請因明問而陳之事之交於前
者雖無常形理之具於心者自有定則理
同而事異不害其為同理異而事同適所
以為異慨自嬴秦黷武邯鄲幾傾無忌襲
擊晉鄙以赴平原之急雖非大義而勇於
救患猶或可嘉項籍何為者顧以偏裨之
職矯殺宋義以救新趙而又戕害主帥大
義乖矣陳勝舉事尺土未階張耳勸立六
國以為自固之計雖非公謀而外假虛名
punctuated:
考試官敎諭周批：觀此一策，蓋博學宏辭之流也。健羨，健羨！

考試官敎諭方批：叙事詳盡，而斷制精明，非若左氏專以成敗論事者矣。佳士，佳士！

不患乎疑事之難決，而貴存至公之心；不畏乎眾論之難折，而貴操大中之矩。蓋公則不私，而天下之猶豫自定；中則不偏，而天下之議論自明。不私不偏，其於眾言之混淆，吾折以本然之則而有餘力，尚何狐疑之患哉？請因明問而陳之。事之交於前者雖無常形，理之具於心者自有定則。理同而事異，不害其為同；理異而事同，適所以為異。慨自嬴秦黷武，邯鄲幾傾，無忌襲擊晉鄙，以赴平原之急，雖非大義，而勇於救患，猶或可嘉。項籍何為者？顧以偏裨之職，矯殺宋義，以救新趙，而又戕害主帥，大義乖矣。陳勝舉事，尺土未階，張耳勸立六國，以為自固之計，雖非公謀，而外假虛名，
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Judging by this policy essay, he belongs among those of broad learning and ample literary talent. How admirable, how admirable!

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: His account of events is thorough, and his judgments are incisive and clear. He is unlike Master Zuo, who judges events solely by success or failure. A worthy scholar, a worthy scholar!

One should not worry that doubtful matters are difficult to decide, but prize the preservation of a wholly impartial mind; one should not fear that competing opinions are difficult to adjudicate, but prize adherence to the standard of perfect balance. Impartiality excludes self-interest, and the world’s uncertainties thereby resolve themselves; balance excludes bias, and the world’s debates thereby become clear. Free of self-interest and bias, I can readily adjudicate the confusion of competing claims by the inherent standard of principle. What cause, then, remains to fear indecision? Allow me to explain in response to your discerning question. Although the affairs confronting us have no constant form, the principles inherent in the mind have fixed standards. When the principle is the same but the circumstances differ, this does not prevent their being alike; when the principles differ but the circumstances are alike, this is precisely what makes them different.

Alas, when Qin under the Ying house recklessly resorted to arms and Handan was on the verge of falling, Wuji attacked Jin Bi to come to the aid of the Lord of Pingyuan in his emergency. Although this did not accord with the higher demands of righteousness, his courage in relieving distress might still merit praise. But what was Xiang Ji doing? Holding merely the post of a subordinate commander, he invoked a false order to kill Song Yi in order to rescue the newly restored Zhao; in murdering his commanding general, he violated the higher demands of righteousness. When Chen Sheng rose in revolt and had not yet secured a foot of territory [?], Zhang Er urged him to reestablish the six states as a means of securing his own position. Although this was no public-spirited plan, outwardly he borrowed their nominal prestige…

translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Judging from this policy essay, its author belongs among those of broad learning and splendid literary expression. How admirable, how admirable!

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: The account of events is exhaustive, and the judgments are penetrating and clear. This is unlike Master Zuo, who assesses events solely by success or failure. An excellent scholar, an excellent scholar!

One should not worry that doubtful matters are difficult to decide, but value preserving a wholly impartial mind; one should not fear that competing opinions are difficult to adjudicate, but value holding to the standard of perfect balance. For impartiality excludes selfishness, and thus the uncertainties of the world resolve themselves; balance excludes bias, and thus the debates of the world become clear of themselves. Free of selfishness and bias, I can adjudicate the confusion of competing statements by their inherent standard, with strength to spare. What cause remains to worry about doubt and hesitation? Allow me to set this forth in response to your illuminating question.

Although the events that confront us have no constant form, the principles inherent in the mind have their fixed standards. When the principle is the same but the events differ, this does not prevent their being alike; when the principles differ but the events are alike, this is precisely what makes them different. Alas, when Qin under the Ying house wantonly resorted to warfare, Handan nearly fell. Wuji launched a surprise attack on Jin Bi to hasten to the aid of the Lord of Pingyuan in his emergency. Although this did not accord with the highest righteousness, his courage in coming to the rescue might still deserve praise. But what was Xiang Ji doing? Holding merely a subordinate command, he killed Song Yi under a falsely claimed order to rescue the newly restored state of Zhao. In doing so, he murdered his commander and violated the highest righteousness.

When Chen Sheng rose in revolt and had not yet gained even a foot of territory [?], Zhang Er urged him to establish the Six States as a means of securing his own position. Although this was no plan for the common good, outwardly borrowing their nominal prestige…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
或能樹黨酈食其何為者乃於垂成之漢
賛立六國以撓楚權是為割地資敵淺謀
甚矣韓信伐趙置背水陣而士卒有死之
心其致勝宜也漢王以惰卒而當强大之
楚於睢水非納侮而何王翦伐楚將六十
萬衆而函谷為虛其成功幸也符堅舉大
衆而冦安輯之晉於淮淝非取敗而何甘
陳矯詔以斬郅支匡衡以為不當封者義
也劉向謂其排妬不免於計利之言薄昭
===
恃勢而殺漢使李德裕以為殺之當者正
也温公謂其未然不免於公義之損管仲
不死子糾蓋桓公當立而子糾不當立耳
故孔子與其功若王魏之苟難殊於仲矣
子程子謂其先有罪而後有功不亦當歟
梁悅為父復讎蓋知義不共天而法令不
暇顧耳故昌黎薄其罪元慶之復父讎等
於悅矣陳子昂乃欲誅其人而表其閭不
亦過歟靈州為宋人保障之境不可棄者
punctuated: 或能樹黨。酈食其何為者？乃於垂成之漢，賛立六國以撓楚權，是為割地資敵，淺謀甚矣。韓信伐趙，置背水陣，而士卒有死之心，其致勝宜也。漢王以惰卒而當强大之楚於睢水，非納侮而何？王翦伐楚，將六十萬衆，而函谷為虛，其成功幸也。符堅舉大衆而冦安輯之晉於淮淝，非取敗而何？甘陳矯詔以斬郅支，匡衡以為不當封者，義也。劉向謂其排妬，不免於計利之言。薄昭恃勢而殺漢使，李德裕以為殺之當者，正也。温公謂其未然，不免於公義之損。管仲不死子糾，蓋桓公當立而子糾不當立耳，故孔子與其功。若王魏之苟難，殊於仲矣。子程子謂其先有罪而後有功，不亦當歟？梁悅為父復讎，蓋知義不共天，而法令不暇顧耳，故昌黎薄其罪。元慶之復父讎，等於悅矣。陳子昂乃欲誅其人而表其閭，不亦過歟？靈州為宋人保障之境，不可棄者
translation_en:
…might perhaps build a following. But what was Li Yiji doing? Just as Han was on the verge of success, he advocated restoring the Six States to undermine Chu’s power. This amounted to ceding territory to assist the enemy: a very shortsighted plan indeed. When Han Xin attacked Zhao, he drew up his troops with their backs to the river, and his soldiers resolved to fight to the death. His victory was fitting. When the King of Han confronted mighty Chu at the Sui River with indolent troops, what was this but inviting humiliation? When Wang Jian attacked Chu, he commanded six hundred thousand men, leaving Hangu Pass empty of defenders. His success was fortunate. When Fu Jian led a vast host to invade the peaceful and well-ordered Jin at the Huai and Fei rivers, what was this but courting defeat?

Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang falsified an imperial edict to execute Zhizhi. Kuang Heng’s judgment that they should not be enfeoffed was righteous. Liu Xiang’s claim that he was excluding them out of jealousy could not escape the charge of arguing from calculations of advantage. Bo Zhao relied on his influence and killed a Han envoy. Li Deyu’s judgment that putting him to death was proper was correct. Duke Wen, Sima Guang, disputed this, but his position could not escape the charge of impairing public righteousness.

Guan Zhong did not die for Prince Jiu simply because Duke Huan ought to have succeeded to the throne, whereas Prince Jiu ought not. Confucius therefore approved his achievement. As for Wang Gui and Wei Zheng’s conduct in evading danger [?], it differed from Guan Zhong’s. Master Cheng said that they were guilty at first but later rendered meritorious service. Was this not an apt judgment?

Liang Yue avenged his father because he understood the righteous principle that one cannot live under the same heaven as one’s father’s killer, and had no leisure to consider laws and statutes. Thus Han Yu of Changli judged his culpability to be slight. Xu Yuanqing’s vengeance for his father was equivalent to Liang Yue’s. Yet Chen Zi’ang wished to execute the man while erecting an honorific marker at the gate of his neighborhood. Was this not mistaken? Lingzhou was a territory that served as a defensive bulwark for the people of Song and could not be abandoned…

punctuated: 或能樹黨。酈食其何為者，乃於垂成之漢，賛立六國以撓楚權，是為割地資敵，淺謀甚矣！韓信伐趙，置背水陣，而士卒有死之心，其致勝宜也。漢王以惰卒而當强大之楚於睢水，非納侮而何？王翦伐楚，將六十萬衆，而函谷為虚，其成功幸也。符堅舉大衆而冦安輯之晉於淮淝，非取敗而何？甘陳矯詔以斬郅支，匡衡以為不當封者，義也。劉向謂其排妬，不免於計利之言。薄昭恃勢而殺漢使，李德裕以為殺之當者，正也。温公謂其未然，不免於公義之損。管仲不死子糾，蓋桓公當立，而子糾不當立耳。故孔子與其功。若王魏之苟難，殊於仲矣。子程子謂其先有罪而後有功，不亦當歟？梁悅為父復讎，蓋知義不共天，而法令不暇顧耳。故昌黎薄其罪。元慶之復父讎，等於悅矣。陳子昂乃欲誅其人而表其閭，不亦過歟？靈州為宋人保障之境，不可棄者
translation_en:
…might be able to build a faction. What was Li Yiji about, that, when Han was on the verge of success, he advocated reestablishing the Six States to undermine Chu’s power? This amounted to ceding territory to aid the enemy: a most shortsighted scheme! When Han Xin attacked Zhao, he arrayed his troops with their backs to the water, and the soldiers were resolved to fight to the death. His victory was therefore to be expected. When the King of Han took indolent troops to confront mighty Chu at the Sui River, what was this but inviting humiliation? When Wang Jian attacked Chu, he commanded a force of six hundred thousand, leaving Hangu Pass undefended. His success was fortunate. When Fu Jian raised a vast army and invaded the peaceful and settled Jin realm in the region of the Huai and Fei rivers, what was this but courting defeat?

Gan and Chen falsified an imperial edict to execute Zhizhi. Kuang Heng’s view that they should not receive enfeoffment accorded with righteousness. Liu Xiang’s claim that this was exclusion born of jealousy could not escape being an argument calculated in terms of advantage. Bo Zhao relied on his influence and killed a Han envoy. Li Deyu’s view that executing him was appropriate was correct. Duke Wen’s view that this was not so could not escape impairing public justice.

Guan Zhong did not die for Prince Jiu, surely because Duke Huan was the rightful ruler and Prince Jiu was not. Thus Confucius approved his achievement. The conduct of Wang and Wei in seeking to escape danger [?] was quite different from Guan Zhong’s. Was Master Cheng not right to say that they first incurred guilt and later rendered meritorious service?

Liang Yue avenged his father because he understood the moral duty not to share the same heaven with his father’s killer and had no time to consider the statutes. Thus Han Yu of Changli judged his offense lightly. Yuanqing’s vengeance for his father was equivalent to Liang Yue’s. Yet Chen Zi’ang wished to execute the man while honoring his neighborhood gate. Was this not mistaken? Lingzhou was territory that served as a defensive bulwark for the people of Song and could not be abandoned…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也輔臣之言爲是楊億李沆以爲可棄其
殆未之思乎綏州乃敵人戎馬之塲不可
城者也洪湛之言爲非孫全照以爲宜緩
其亦計之熟乎吁群疑滿腹判之在於一
心衆難塞胸折之憑乎一理傳曰權然後
知輕重度然後知長短舍至公之鑑其何
以决天下之疑昧大中之矩又何以斷天
下之務哉雖然評古人之得失將以驗吾
身之得失較往行之是非期以審吾行之
===
是非苟徒觀人而昧反觀察人而忘自察
則亦何益於身心哉末學管窺未知是否
幸執事進而教之
第四問
拱廷臣
同考試官教諭陳批聽言信行孔門自有故
步此篇貫串經史品量人物而不失權衡况議論辯
博辭氣莊整若德人儼雅色不可犯察子所存殆
非無之而工言者也將信子爲端士矣薦之以華科目
punctuated:
也。輔臣之言爲是，楊億、李沆以爲可棄，其殆未之思乎？綏州乃敵人戎馬之塲，不可城者也。洪湛之言爲非，孫全照以爲宜緩，其亦計之熟乎？吁！群疑滿腹，判之在於一心；衆難塞胸，折之憑乎一理。傳曰：「權然後知輕重，度然後知長短。」舍至公之鑑，其何以决天下之疑？昧大中之矩，又何以斷天下之務哉？雖然，評古人之得失，將以驗吾身之得失；較往行之是非，期以審吾行之是非。苟徒觀人而昧反觀，察人而忘自察，則亦何益於身心哉？末學管窺，未知是否，幸執事進而教之。
第四問
拱廷臣
同考試官教諭陳批：聽言信行，孔門自有故步。此篇貫串經史，品量人物，而不失權衡。况議論辯博，辭氣莊整，若德人儼雅，色不可犯。察子所存，殆非無之而工言者也。將信子爲端士矣，薦之以華科目。
translation_en:
… indeed. The chief minister’s advice was correct. When Yang Yi and Li Hang considered it expendable, had they perhaps failed to think the matter through? Suizhou was a battleground for enemy cavalry, a place that should not be fortified. Hong Zhan’s advice was wrong. When Sun Quanzhao considered that the work should be deferred, had he not weighed the matter thoroughly?

Ah! When doubts fill the mind, their resolution rests with a single heart; when difficulties crowd the breast, their settlement depends upon a single principle. The classic says: “Only after weighing do we know lightness and heaviness; only after measuring do we know length and shortness.” If we abandon the mirror of perfect impartiality, how can we resolve the world’s doubts? If we fail to understand the standard of the great mean, how can we adjudicate the world’s affairs? Nevertheless, in judging the successes and failures of the ancients, we seek to test our own successes and failures; in comparing the right and wrong of past conduct, we aim to scrutinize the right and wrong of our own conduct. If we merely observe others without turning our gaze upon ourselves, and scrutinize others while forgetting to scrutinize ourselves, what benefit can this bring to our persons and minds? These are the narrow views of an unseasoned student; I do not know whether they are correct. I hope that you, sir, will guide and instruct me.

Fourth Policy Question
Gong Tingchen

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor:
“In listening to words and trusting conduct, the school of Confucius has its established procedure. This essay connects the classics and histories, assessing individuals without losing the proper balance. Moreover, its arguments are discriminating and wide-ranging, its language dignified and orderly, like a virtuous man whose solemn elegance and demeanor command respect. Examining what you hold within, I judge that you are surely not someone who speaks skillfully without possessing the substance of his words. I am inclined to trust that you are an upright scholar. I recommend you to bring distinction to the examination.”

Fourth Question
Gong Tingchen
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: In listening to words and trusting conduct, the school of Confucius has its established methods. This essay draws together the classics and histories, weighing historical figures without losing the proper balance. Moreover, its arguments are penetrating and wide-ranging, its language and tone dignified and orderly, like a virtuous man whose grave and refined bearing commands respect. Examining what you hold within, I judge that you are hardly someone who lacks substance yet excels at words. I am inclined to trust that you are an upright scholar. I recommend you to bring distinction to the examinations.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭周批言行一策正關士習此篇
斂華就實黜通尚儉辭氣舂容而剸制有據世有如
此才宜其穎脫而出矣
考試官教諭方批五策皆無可疵而言行
一篇尤敻出諸士之右錄之將以喻浮誕者云
對道術正士之言行初無可擇氣習異士
之言行始有所偏天下之事以言而傳將
亦以言而廢以行而立將亦以行而荒蓋
言有切謾而行有夷險也今夫叩鐘皷而
===
聽其鏗訇天下無異聲由道路而騁夫康
莊天下無異徑人之於言行也亦然節而
後言志而後動則鏗訇之聲徹於外而康
莊之馳將達於天下矣夫惟言必簡而節
始中行至中而志始堅不中乎節不堅乎
志則言固苟言而行亦詖行耳善乎宋儒
之論曰先道而言故無不信之言先義而
行故無不果之行知此然後可與論言行
矣是故聖賢者萬世言行之準也觀夫賛
punctuated:
考試官教諭周批：言行一策，正關士習。此篇斂華就實，黜通尚儉，辭氣舂容，而剸制有據。世有如此才，宜其穎脫而出矣。

考試官教諭方批：五策皆無可疵，而言行一篇尤敻出諸士之右。錄之，將以喻浮誕者云。

對：道術正，士之言行初無可擇；氣習異，士之言行始有所偏。天下之事，以言而傳，將亦以言而廢；以行而立，將亦以行而荒。蓋言有切謾，而行有夷險也。今夫叩鐘皷而聽其鏗訇，天下無異聲；由道路而騁夫康莊，天下無異徑。人之於言行也亦然。節而後言，志而後動，則鏗訇之聲徹於外，而康莊之馳將達於天下矣。夫惟言必簡而節始中，行至中而志始堅。不中乎節，不堅乎志，則言固苟言，而行亦詖行耳。善乎宋儒之論曰：「先道而言，故無不信之言；先義而行，故無不果之行。」知此，然後可與論言行矣。是故聖賢者，萬世言行之準也。觀夫賛
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: This policy essay on words and conduct bears directly upon the habits of scholars. It restrains ornament and attends to substance, rejects fluency [?] and esteems restraint. Its language is measured and ample, and its judgments are well grounded. A talent such as this should indeed distinguish itself and emerge from the crowd.

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: None of the five policy essays has anything to fault, but the essay on words and conduct stands especially far above those of the other candidates. I select it to offer instruction to those given to frivolity and extravagance.

Response: When learning of the Way is correct, scholars’ words and conduct initially offer nothing to choose between; only when their temperaments and acquired habits differ do their words and conduct begin to become partial. Affairs throughout the world are transmitted through words, yet through words they may also be abandoned; they are established through conduct, yet through conduct they may also fall into neglect. For words may be pertinent or deceptive, and conduct may be straightforward or devious. Now, when one strikes bells and drums and listens to their resounding tones, nowhere under Heaven is their sound different; when one follows the roads and speeds along the broad thoroughfares, nowhere under Heaven is the path different. So it is with people’s words and conduct. Speak only after exercising restraint, and act only after establishing one’s resolve: then the resounding tones will carry outward, and travel along the broad thoroughfares will reach throughout the world. Only when words are concise does restraint attain its proper measure; only when conduct attains the mean does resolve become firm. Without proper restraint or firmness of resolve, words are merely careless words, and conduct merely distorted conduct. Well put is the judgment of the Song Confucians: “Put the Way first when speaking, and no word will fail to be trustworthy; put righteousness first when acting, and no action will fail to be resolute.” Only with this understanding can one discuss words and conduct. Thus sages and worthies are the standard for words and conduct for all ages. Consider the praise …

When the world has talent like this, it is fitting that it should stand out.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
吉人而稱寡辭叙敝俗而病利口語世變
而薄尚通敦操已而重危行至於四方之
使則未嘗以有言棄中庸之道又未嘗以
怪異求何也夫言慎者德崇而誕者風靡
行果者德久而通者詭隨此固言行之大
端也若夫子員無私叔向所召子產有辭
諸侯賴之柴愚參魯著在髙業而狷者不
為亦惟所取焉是言果不可已而通果不
必尚也審爾雖然君子豈樂為是費辭者
===
哉誠以道術不可以不明人心不可以不
正故也大道旣隱民訛寖彰柔巽流而為
諛佞貞實散而為夸毗其言行之可觀者
亦其習俗之近古者也蓋嘗求之古人語
默之間而有得乎宇文融之應對辯給周
勃乏言若不出王夷甫之詞甚清辯李廣
之終日恂恂嵇康之輕肆直言徐穉之不
荅國事矣又嘗稽之古人通檢之迹而有
得乎卓茂之束身自修郗超之任心獨詣
punctuated: 吉人而稱寡辭，叙敝俗而病利口，語世變而薄尚通，敦操已而重危行。至於四方之使，則未嘗以有言棄中庸之道，又未嘗以怪異求。何也？夫言慎者德崇，而誕者風靡；行果者德久，而通者詭隨。此固言行之大端也。若夫子員無私，叔向所召；子產有辭，諸侯賴之；柴愚參魯，著在髙業；而狷者不為，亦惟所取焉。是言果不可已，而通果不必尚也，審爾。雖然，君子豈樂為是費辭者哉？誠以道術不可以不明，人心不可以不正故也。大道旣隱，民訛寖彰，柔巽流而為諛佞，貞實散而為夸毗。其言行之可觀者，亦其習俗之近古者也。蓋嘗求之古人語默之間，而有得乎宇文融之應對辯給、周勃乏言若不出、王夷甫之詞甚清辯、李廣之終日恂恂、嵇康之輕肆直言、徐穉之不荅國事矣。又嘗稽之古人通檢之迹，而有得乎卓茂之束身自修、郗超之任心獨詣
translation_en:
…good men, they commend their sparing speech; in describing corrupt customs, they deplore glib tongues; in speaking of changes in the world, they disparage the esteem for accommodation; and in encouraging disciplined personal conduct [?], they value upright action. As for those sent on missions to the four quarters, they never abandon the Way of the Mean merely because they have something to say, nor do they seek through strange and eccentric behavior [?]. Why is this? Those cautious in speech possess lofty virtue, whereas those given to extravagant talk bend with the wind; those resolute in action possess enduring virtue, whereas those given to accommodation follow others unscrupulously. These are indeed the cardinal principles of speech and conduct. Thus Zi Yuan [?] was impartial and was summoned by Shuxiang; Zichan was eloquent, and the feudal lords relied upon him. Chai was simple and Shen was slow, yet both were distinguished for high attainment; and the scrupulous, who refrain from certain actions, were likewise approved for precisely this quality. Thus speech truly cannot be dispensed with, while accommodation truly need not be esteemed: this is certain. Nevertheless, could the gentleman take pleasure in expending so many words on this? He does so because the principles of the Way must be clarified and people’s hearts must be set right.

Once the Great Way became obscured, popular error gradually grew manifest. Gentleness and compliance degenerated into flattery and sycophancy; integrity and sincerity dissolved into fawning obsequiousness. Those whose speech and conduct remain worthy of regard are also those whose customary practices approach those of antiquity. I have sought understanding in the speech and silence of men of old, and have gained insight from Yuwen Rong’s fluent and ready replies; Zhou Bo’s paucity of speech, as though unable to utter a word; Wang Yifu’s exceptionally lucid and eloquent diction; Li Guang’s quiet modesty throughout the day; Ji Kang’s uninhibited, forthright speech; and Xu Zhi’s refusal to answer questions about affairs of state. I have also examined the traces of openness and restraint in the conduct of men of old, and have gained insight from Zhuo Mao’s self-restraint and self-cultivation, and Xi Chao’s following his own inclinations toward independent attainments…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
吉人而稱寡辭叙敝俗而病利口語世變
而薄尚通敦操已而重危行至於四方之
使則未嘗以有言棄中庸之道又未嘗以
怪異求何也夫言慎者德崇而誕者風靡
行果者德久而通者詭隨此固言行之大
端也若夫子貢無私叔向所召子產有辭
諸侯頼之柴愚參魯著在髙業而狷者不
為亦惟所取焉是言果不可已而通果不
必尚也審爾雖然君子豈樂為是費辭者
===
哉誠以道術不可以不明人心不可以不
正故也大道旣隱民訛寖彰柔巽流而為
諛佞貞實散而為夸毗其言行之可觀者
亦其習俗之近古者也蓋嘗求之古人語
默之間而有得乎宇文融之應對辯給周
勃之言若不出王夷甫之詞甚清辯李廣
之終日恂恂嵇康之輕肆直言徐穉之不
荅國事矣又嘗稽之古人通檢之迹而有
得乎卓茂之束身自修郗超之任心獨詣
punctuated: 吉人而稱寡辭，叙敝俗而病利口，語世變而薄尚通，敦操已而重危行。至於四方之使，則未嘗以有言棄，中庸之道又未嘗以怪異求，何也？夫言慎者德崇，而誕者風靡；行果者德久，而通者詭隨。此固言行之大端也。若夫子貢無私，叔向所召；子產有辭，諸侯頼之；柴愚參魯，著在髙業，而狷者不為，亦惟所取焉。是言果不可已，而通果不必尚也，審爾。雖然，君子豈樂為是費辭者哉？誠以道術不可以不明，人心不可以不正故也。大道旣隱，民訛寖彰，柔巽流而為諛佞，貞實散而為夸毗。其言行之可觀者，亦其習俗之近古者也。蓋嘗求之古人語默之間，而有得乎宇文融之應對辯給、周勃之言若不出、王夷甫之詞甚清辯、李廣之終日恂恂、嵇康之輕肆直言、徐穉之不荅國事矣。又嘗稽之古人通檢之迹，而有得乎卓茂之束身自修、郗超之任心獨詣
translation_en:
…praises the good man for speaking sparingly, describes corrupt customs and deplores glib tongues, discusses changes in the world and disparages the esteem for accommodation, and urges firm personal discipline and values upright conduct. Yet those sent as envoys to the four quarters were never rejected for their eloquence, nor was the Way of the Mean ever sought through strange and extraordinary behavior. Why is this? Those cautious in speech possess lofty virtue, whereas those whose words are extravagant bend with the prevailing wind; those resolute in conduct possess enduring virtue, whereas those given to accommodation follow others unscrupulously. These are indeed the main principles governing speech and conduct. As for Zigong’s impartiality, it was this that Shuxiang commended [?]; Zichan possessed eloquence, and the feudal lords relied upon him. Chai’s simplicity and Shen’s dullness figured among their lofty achievements; and the scrupulous, who refuse to do certain things, were likewise approved for that quality. Thus speech truly cannot be dispensed with, while accommodation need not be esteemed. This is assuredly so. Nevertheless, does the gentleman take pleasure in expending so many words on this? It is truly because the teachings of the Way must be clarified and people’s hearts must be set right.

Once the Great Way had become hidden, falsehood among the people gradually became manifest. Gentleness and deference degenerated into flattery and obsequiousness; steadfastness and sincerity dissolved into fawning servility. Those whose speech and conduct remained worthy of regard were also those whose customary ways remained close to antiquity. I have sought understanding in the speech and silence of the ancients, and have gained insight from Yuwen Rong’s fluent and ready replies, Zhou Bo’s seeming inability to get his words out, Wang Yifu’s exceptionally lucid and eloquent language, Li Guang’s quiet modesty throughout the day, Ji Kang’s unrestrained frank speech, and Xu Zhi’s refusal to answer questions about affairs of state. I have also examined the traces of the ancients’ accommodating or restrained conduct, and have gained insight from Zhuo Mao’s self-discipline and self-cultivation, and Xi Chao’s following his own inclinations toward an independent attainment…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
關康之之候見不顧何思澄之惟事造謁
陸龜蒙之耻與俗交申屠蟠之自同傭人
矣蓋求之而不辯稽之而不察果能有以
盡夫人乎否耶故曰言有切謾而行有夷
險者也夫以聚斂禍唐者孰與厚重之安
劉廢事亂晉者孰與簡易之効績直遂戕
生者孰與明哲之自容曠世不羈者孰與
恭愛之被聘俗方婁護者又孰與人不敢
干之高尚及乎樂開入學之賢見幾而作
===
之智或者殆未可以醇疵判矣由是觀之
誕者不必述事而謹者然後可以營道通
者不必周務而果者然後可以育德噫聖
人之言動又豈有舍道德而為之度者哉
而執事者下詢又欲求以去夫口過怨惡
之道焉蓋有以見開示承學之盛心矣夫
言由中出行由心制者也君子先立其誠
於是乎有易心之語比義之行矣韓愈儒
者也其著言行之箴顧不推本於此何耶
punctuated:
關康之之候見不顧，何思澄之惟事造謁，陸龜蒙之耻與俗交，申屠蟠之自同傭人矣。蓋求之而不辯，稽之而不察，果能有以盡夫人乎？否耶？故曰：言有切謾，而行有夷險者也。夫以聚斂禍唐者，孰與厚重之安劉？廢事亂晉者，孰與簡易之効績？直遂戕生者，孰與明哲之自容？曠世不羈者，孰與恭愛之被聘？俗方婁護者，又孰與人不敢干之高尚？及乎樂開入學之賢、見幾而作之智，或者殆未可以醇疵判矣。由是觀之，誕者不必述事，而謹者然後可以營道；通者不必周務，而果者然後可以育德。噫！聖人之言動，又豈有舍道德而為之度者哉？
而執事者下詢，又欲求以去夫口過怨惡之道焉，蓋有以見開示承學之盛心矣。夫言由中出，行由心制者也。君子先立其誠，於是乎有易心之語、比義之行矣。韓愈，儒者也，其著言行之箴，顧不推本於此，何耶？
translation_en:
…Guan Kangzhi’s disregard for those awaiting an audience, He Sicheng’s exclusive devotion to paying visits, Lu Guimeng’s shame at associating with commonplace people, and Shentu Pan’s placing himself on the same footing as hired laborers. Yet if we seek understanding without making distinctions, and examine precedents without scrutinizing them, can we truly understand these men fully, or not? Thus it is said: speech may be earnest or deceitful, while conduct may be straightforward or devious. How does one who brought disaster upon the Tang through rapacious exactions compare with one whose gravity and substantial character secured the house of Liu? How does one who neglected affairs and threw the Jin into disorder compare with one who achieved results through simplicity and ease? How does one whose unrestrained directness cost him his life compare with one who preserved himself through clear understanding and wisdom? How does one who stood aloof from his age, acknowledging no restraints, compare with one whose reverence and affection brought him an invitation to serve? And how does one whom popular opinion likened to Lou Hu compare with one whose lofty integrity no one dared encroach upon? As for the worthiness of ‘Le Kai entering the school’ [?] and the wisdom of acting upon perceiving the first signs of change, perhaps these cannot readily be judged in terms of purity and defect. Viewed in this light, the extravagant in speech do not necessarily accomplish affairs; only the circumspect can cultivate the Way. Those who move freely among others do not necessarily attend fully to their duties; only the resolute can nurture virtue. Ah! In their speech and actions, could the sages ever set aside the Way and virtue as their measure?
You who preside over this examination have condescended to inquire further, seeking a way to eliminate faults of speech, resentment, and hatred. This reveals your generous intention to enlighten those engaged in learning. Speech proceeds from within, and conduct is governed by the heart. The gentleman first establishes his sincerity; from this come words expressing an untroubled heart and actions conforming to righteousness. Han Yu was a Confucian scholar. Yet in composing his admonitions on speech and conduct, why did he not trace their foundations back to this?

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
噫誠豈易言哉昔顏淵問仁而請其目夫
子曰非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言非禮
勿動程子嗣而為之四箴誠之一語蓋三
致意焉退之之學非心學也無惑乎其未
之前聞也雖然何以知要曰言忠信行篤
敬雖蠻貊之邦行矣此孔氏家法也請敬
事斯語
第五問
蔣識
===
同考試官教諭林 批 民事敝而不脩軍政渙
而無緒廣西之恒患也此策首言任人任法已得
其要而叙事精確初無浮冗不根之談見於施行
當亦有濟如子者宣亦先天下之憂者歟吾將卜
子於用矣
考試官教諭周 批 士子適用之學類於時
務一策見之此篇辭醇事覈諒非能言而不能行者
考試官教諭方 批 士子叙時政者不激即
迂此篇酌古準今言利害處尤明白痛切而文復渾
punctuated:
噫！誠豈易言哉？昔顏淵問仁而請其目，夫子曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」程子嗣而為之四箴，誠之一語，蓋三致意焉。退之之學，非心學也，無惑乎其未之前聞也。雖然，何以知要？曰：「言忠信，行篤敬，雖蠻貊之邦行矣。」此孔氏家法也，請敬事斯語。
第五問
蔣識
同考試官教諭林批：民事敝而不脩，軍政渙而無緒，廣西之恒患也。此策首言任人任法，已得其要，而叙事精確，初無浮冗不根之談。見於施行，當亦有濟。如子者，宣亦先天下之憂者歟？吾將卜子於用矣。
考試官教諭周批：士子適用之學，類於時務一策見之。此篇辭醇事覈，諒非能言而不能行者。
考試官教諭方批：士子叙時政者，不激即迂。此篇酌古準今，言利害處尤明白痛切，而文復渾
translation_en:
Ah! Can sincerity be spoken of so easily? Formerly, when Yan Yuan asked about benevolence and requested its particulars, the Master said: “Look at nothing contrary to ritual propriety; listen to nothing contrary to ritual propriety; say nothing contrary to ritual propriety; make no movement contrary to ritual propriety.” Master Cheng subsequently composed his Four Admonitions on these precepts, repeatedly emphasizing the single word “sincerity.” Tuizhi’s learning was not the learning of the mind; no wonder he had not previously heard this teaching. Nevertheless, how can one grasp the essentials? The answer is: “Be loyal and trustworthy in speech, earnest and reverent in conduct, and even in the lands of the Man and Mo peoples you will get along.” This is the teaching handed down in the school of Confucius. Let me reverently put these words into practice.
Fifth Question
Jiang Shi
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: Civil affairs fall into disrepair and remain neglected; military administration is disorganized and lacks order. These are Guangxi’s perennial troubles. This policy essay begins by discussing the employment of men and the application of laws, thus already grasping the essentials. Its account of affairs is precise, entirely free of empty, redundant, or groundless talk. Put into practice, its proposals should also prove beneficial. Might someone like you be one who worries before all others under Heaven [?]? I shall judge your promise by your performance in office.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: A candidate’s practical learning can generally be seen in a single policy essay on current affairs. This essay’s language is sound and its treatment of affairs exact. Surely its author is no mere talker incapable of action.
Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: Candidates who discuss contemporary governance are either intemperate or impractical. This essay weighs antiquity against the present; its discussion of benefits and harms is especially clear, incisive, and compelling, while its prose is also rounded…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
罷征交屯近郡歟今也冦則在門庭兵則
不出境而廣東之餉且歳至湖廣遞戍之
軍日接踵於道矣必欲滅四郊之盜蠲兩
稅之征逐侵漁之吏編户之民非不足以
刷積歲之忿而快其心吾恐十室九空緩
急之宜吾民不能以懸俟矣必欲正投附
之罰完脫漏之伍節貧懦之差尺籍之衆
非不足以申號令之重而作其氣吾恐十
羊九牧施為之方吾人不得以專制矣夫
===
惟至困之民而守之以不能懸俟之勢枯
魚之肆不其多乎且歲入不登於舊經費
遂踰於初官之所急即民之所需也為民
計者惟廣豐殖之利而已昔羊祜之始鎮
襄陽也軍無百日之儲祜乃墾田八百餘
頃及其季年遂有十年之積蓋古人已試
之效也廣西之野原田久於蕪穢水泉廢
於荒窒列郡蓋相望也必若募逃逋之徒
給墾闢之具分疆刋石使有定分再歲而
punctuated:
罷征交，屯近郡歟？今也，冦則在門庭，兵則不出境，而廣東之餉且歳至，湖廣遞戍之軍日接踵於道矣。必欲滅四郊之盜，蠲兩稅之征，逐侵漁之吏，編户之民非不足以刷積歲之忿而快其心，吾恐十室九空，緩急之宜，吾民不能以懸俟矣。必欲正投附之罰，完脫漏之伍，節貧懦之差，尺籍之衆非不足以申號令之重而作其氣，吾恐十羊九牧，施為之方，吾人不得以專制矣。
夫惟至困之民，而守之以不能懸俟之勢，枯魚之肆不其多乎？且歲入不登於舊，經費遂踰於初，官之所急，即民之所需也。為民計者，惟廣豐殖之利而已。昔羊祜之始鎮襄陽也，軍無百日之儲，祜乃墾田八百餘頃，及其季年，遂有十年之積，蓋古人已試之效也。廣西之野，原田久於蕪穢，水泉廢於荒窒，列郡蓋相望也。必若募逃逋之徒，給墾闢之具，分疆刋石，使有定分，再歲而
translation_en:
…halt the campaign against Jiao and station troops in nearby prefectures [?]? Now the bandits are at our very doors, yet the troops do not leave the territory; military supplies from Guangdong arrive yearly, and soldiers from Huguang coming in rotation for garrison duty follow one another along the roads day after day. If we insist on exterminating the bandits throughout the surrounding countryside, remitting the two seasonal taxes, and expelling officials who prey upon the people, these measures would indeed suffice to wash away the accumulated resentment of the registered households and gladden their hearts. Yet I fear that nine households out of ten stand empty: our people cannot wait indefinitely for measures suited to the urgency of their circumstances. If we insist on enforcing penalties for placing oneself under another’s protection, restoring military units depleted by desertions and omissions from the rolls, and moderating the service obligations of the poor and weak, these measures would indeed suffice to reaffirm the authority of commands and raise the spirits of the men on the military registers. Yet I fear there are nine shepherds for every ten sheep: we cannot exercise independent authority over how to act.
When people already in the utmost distress are held in circumstances in which they cannot wait indefinitely, will there not be many stalls of dried fish—a fate awaiting those whose relief comes too late? Moreover, annual receipts fall short of their former level, while regular expenditures exceed their initial amount. What the authorities urgently require is precisely what the people need. Those planning for the people have only to expand the benefits of abundant production. Formerly, when Yang Hu first took up his military command at Xiangyang, the army did not have provisions for even a hundred days. Hu therefore brought more than eight hundred qing of land under cultivation; by his final years, there were reserves sufficient for ten years. This was an effective measure already tested by a man of antiquity. In the countryside of Guangxi, fields have long lain overgrown, and watercourses and springs have fallen into disuse through neglect and obstruction. Such conditions are found in prefecture after prefecture. If we were to recruit fugitives, supply them with tools for clearing and cultivating land, demarcate boundaries and engrave them on stone so that their allotments were fixed, then after two years…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
熟民知所趨矣由是於常賦則放貱納而
徵土著於公田則給傭直而收贏餘雖微
叔子之效公私其或少贍乎夫惟極耗之
卒而振之以不能專制之威枘鑿之用可
相入乎且衛乏而需於所所乏而需於軍
下之所惡即上之所欲也為軍計者惟均
撫馭之政而已昔雍子之為謀主於晉也
彭城之役歸老幼返孤疾二人役歸一人
陣楚次而降彭城又古人已成之績也廣
===
西之兵丁壯役之樵蘇孱幼沒之奴隸宿
弊蓋相緣也必若嚴貴精之法廣營屯之
田招亡察隱俾無欺蔽踰時而定軍實可
閱矣由是精練者則執干戈而衛社稷羸
弱者則負耒耜而助餱糧雖無雍子之績
什伍其或少復乎振飭之務此其梗槩耳
夫民無定情而政且繋守令不擇則苟且
之意多而化不流軍有常局而弊易濫攉
禁不一則影占之私盛而法不統茍得其
punctuated:
熟，民知所趨矣。由是於常賦則放貱納而徵土著，於公田則給傭直而收贏餘。雖微叔子之效，公私其或少贍乎？

夫惟極耗之卒，而振之以不能專制之威，枘鑿之用可相入乎？且衛乏而需於所，所乏而需於軍，下之所惡即上之所欲也。為軍計者，惟均撫馭之政而已。昔雍子之為謀主於晉也，彭城之役，歸老幼，返孤疾，二人役歸一人，陣楚次而降彭城，又古人已成之績也。廣西之兵，丁壯役之樵蘇，孱幼沒之奴隸，宿弊蓋相緣也。必若嚴貴精之法，廣營屯之田，招亡察隱，俾無欺蔽，踰時而定，軍實可閱矣。由是精練者則執干戈而衛社稷，羸弱者則負耒耜而助餱糧。雖無雍子之績，什伍其或少復乎？振飭之務，此其梗槩耳。

夫民無定情，而政且繋守令；不擇則苟且之意多而化不流。軍有常局，而弊易濫攉；禁不一則影占之私盛而法不統。茍得其
translation_en:
…once the land becomes productive, the people will know what course to follow. Thereafter, in collecting the regular taxes, remit supplementary payments [?] and levy taxes on settled residents; on public fields, pay wages and take in the surplus. Even without results like those achieved by Shuzi [Yang Hu], might public and private resources not become somewhat more ample?

To take utterly depleted troops and try to reinvigorate them through an authority that cannot exercise independent command—is this a tenon that can fit its mortise? Moreover, when a guard lacks resources, it demands them from its battalions; when a battalion lacks resources, it demands them from the soldiers. What those below detest is precisely what those above desire. Planning for the army requires only an equitable administration of care and control. Formerly, when Yongzi served as chief adviser in Jin, during the campaign against Pengcheng he sent the old and young home, returned the orphaned and sick, and released one man wherever two were serving. He deployed against Chu’s encampment [?] and compelled Pengcheng to surrender. This, too, was an accomplishment already achieved by a man of antiquity. Among Guangxi’s soldiers, the able-bodied are made to gather firewood and fodder, while the weak and young are reduced to slavery. These longstanding abuses perpetuate one another. If regulations emphasizing quality were strictly enforced, the land under military agricultural colonies expanded, deserters recalled and concealed personnel investigated, so that there was no deception or concealment, then after a season matters would be settled and the army’s actual strength could be inspected. Thereafter, the well-trained would take up shields and spears to defend the altars of soil and grain, while the weak would shoulder ploughs and spades to supplement military provisions. Even without Yongzi’s achievements, might the ranks not be somewhat restored? These are merely the broad outlines of the work of revitalization and reform.

The people’s dispositions are not fixed, and government depends upon prefects and magistrates. If these are not carefully selected, a disposition to muddle through will prevail and moral transformation will not spread. The army has an established organization, but abuses readily proliferate [?]. If prohibitions are not uniform, the private appropriation of soldiers under protective pretexts will flourish, and the law will not be administered consistently. If one could obtain the…

Thus, in collecting regular taxes, one should discontinue the defective arrangements for payment [?] and levy taxes on the settled inhabitants; on public lands, one should pay wages for hired labor and collect the surplus. title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人則撓民者有所控制屈民者有所通融
蝕民者有所畏憚而凡豐殖之利將經久
而無遺矣苟一其權則投附者無所依憑
姦宄者無所竄匿征調者無所恣容而凡
撫馭之政將均齊而專一矣雖然豈特廣
西之患哉不恤緯而憂王室誠非嫠婦之
任也惟執事者教之
punctuated: 人，則撓民者有所控制，屈民者有所通融，蝕民者有所畏憚，而凡豐殖之利，將經久而無遺矣。苟一其權，則投附者無所依憑，姦宄者無所竄匿，征調者無所恣容，而凡撫馭之政，將均齊而專一矣。雖然，豈特廣西之患哉？不恤緯而憂王室，誠非嫠婦之任也。惟執事者教之。
translation_en: …the right men, then those who harass the people will be restrained, those who oppress them will be subject to adjustment and accommodation, and those who prey upon them will have something to fear. All the benefits of prosperity and growth will thus endure, with none neglected. If authority is unified, those who attach themselves to powerful protectors will have no support to rely upon, evildoers will have nowhere to hide, and those responsible for levies and mobilization will have no scope for unchecked license. All measures for governing and maintaining order will then be applied evenly and with unity of purpose. Yet are these troubles peculiar to Guangxi? To neglect one’s weaving and worry about the royal house is surely beyond a widow’s responsibilities. I ask only that you, who hold office, instruct me.

translation_en: …persons, then those who harass the people will be held in check, those who oppress the people will have scope to accommodate them, and those who prey upon the people will have something to fear. All the benefits of prosperity and growth will thus endure, with none left unrealized. If authority is unified, those who seek powerful patrons will have no one to rely upon, evildoers will have nowhere to hide, and those called up for service will have no cause for complaint. All measures for pacifying and governing will thus be consistent and unified. Yet are these troubles confined to Guangxi? To neglect the weft of one's weaving while worrying about the royal house is truly beyond a widow's proper charge. I ask only that you, the officials in charge, instruct me.

text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
正德已卯秋八月下澣廣西
鄉試錄就緒有日矣尚文等
七人實受幣聘來典文衡方
事之殷寢不妥席食不下咽
憂心忡忡惟恐其有負也撤
棘之前夕卷束于箱榜登于
===
堂待旦而出院尚文等暫憩
小集取館人嚮日所供酒殽
薄定禮飲獻酬有節雍雍愉
愉歡而不譁所以舒其和弛
其蘊節宣其勞而樂王事之
有成也旣而相與諗曰古者
列國卿大夫聘問宴饗必賦
punctuated:

正德已卯秋八月下澣，廣西鄉試錄就緒有日矣。尚文等七人實受幣聘，來典文衡。方事之殷，寢不妥席，食不下咽，憂心忡忡，惟恐其有負也。撤棘之前夕，卷束于箱，榜登于堂，待旦而出院。尚文等暫憩小集，取館人嚮日所供酒殽，薄定禮飲，獻酬有節，雍雍愉愉，歡而不譁，所以舒其和，弛其蘊，節宣其勞，而樂王事之有成也。旣而相與諗曰：「古者列國卿大夫聘問宴饗，必賦
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In autumn, during the last ten days of the eighth month of the jimao year of the Zhengde reign (1519; cyclical character transcribed as 已 [?]), the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination had been ready for some days. We seven, Shangwen and the others, had accepted invitations accompanied by ceremonial gifts and come to preside over the assessment of literary compositions. When our duties were most pressing, we could neither rest comfortably on our sleeping mats nor swallow our food. Our hearts were filled with anxiety, fearing only that we might fail in our trust.

On the evening before the thorn barriers were removed, the examination scripts were bundled into chests and the list of successful candidates was posted in the hall. We awaited dawn to leave the examination compound. Shangwen and the others briefly rested and gathered together, taking the wine and dishes that the attendants had provided earlier. We established a modest drinking ritual, offering and returning cups in due measure. In harmony and good cheer, we were merry without being boisterous. Thus we gave expression to our contentment, released our pent-up feelings, and found measured relief from our exertions, rejoicing that our service to the sovereign had been brought to completion. Then we reflected together, saying: “In antiquity, when ministers and grand masters of the various states exchanged diplomatic visits and held banquets, they invariably recited verse…”

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
正德已卯秋八月下澣廣西
鄉試錄就緒有日矣尚文等
七人實受幣聘來典文衡方
事之殷寢不妥席食不下咽
憂心忡忡惟恐其有負也撤
棘之前夕卷束于箱榜登于
===
堂待旦而出院尚文等暫憩
小集取館人嚮日所供酒殽
薄定禮飲獻酬有節雍雍愉
愉歡而不譁所以舒其和弛
其蘊節宣其勞而樂王事之
有成也旣而相與諗曰古者
列國卿大夫聘問宴饗必賦
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

正德已卯秋八月下澣，廣西鄉試錄就緒有日矣。尚文等七人，實受幣聘，來典文衡。方事之殷，寢不妥席，食不下咽，憂心忡忡，惟恐其有負也。撤棘之前夕，卷束于箱，榜登于堂，待旦而出院。尚文等暫憩小集，取館人嚮日所供酒殽，薄定禮飲，獻酬有節，雍雍愉愉，歡而不譁，所以舒其和，弛其蘊，節宣其勞，而樂王事之有成也。旣而相與諗曰：「古者列國卿大夫聘問宴饗，必賦
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In autumn, during the last ten days of the eighth month of the Zhengde reign’s jimao year [1519; transcribed 已卯, apparently for 己卯, ?], the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination was nearing completion. We seven, Shangwen and the others, had accepted ceremonial gifts of invitation and come to preside over the assessment of literary merit. When the work was most pressing, we could neither sleep comfortably nor swallow our food. Our hearts were filled with anxiety, fearing only that we might fail the trust placed in us. On the evening before the thorn barricades were removed, the examination scripts were bundled into boxes and the list of successful candidates was posted in the hall; we awaited dawn to leave the examination compound.

Shangwen and the others paused for a brief rest and gathered together. Taking the wine and dishes previously supplied by the attendants at our lodgings, we arranged a modest ceremonial drinking gathering. Cups were offered and returned with due restraint; all was harmonious and cheerful, joyful without clamour. Thus we gave expression to our fellow feeling, released our pent-up cares, and eased the strain of our labours, rejoicing that the king’s business had been successfully accomplished. Presently we said to one another: “In antiquity, when ministers and grandees of the various states exchanged diplomatic visits and attended banquets, they would invariably recite odes…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之矣吾徒此行得無内疚乎
好賢莫如緇衣杕杜近似之
矣誠之發於中心而敢有怠
於此乎淇澳之切磋琢磨求
其精而益致其精矣寧復有
遺材之憾乎菁莪棫樸雨露
之所濡也
===
國家作人造士之功莫大焉南
山之臺其德盛矣邦家之基
以人事君之謂也當軸諸君
子有焉雖然受賜不報豈只
尚文等之愆抑亦諸士之恥
也遂歌天保以祝
聖明坐者皆肅容拱而立御史曹
punctuated: 之矣。吾徒此行，得無内疚乎？好賢莫如《緇衣》，《杕杜》近似之矣。誠之發於中心，而敢有怠於此乎？《淇澳》之切磋琢磨，求其精而益致其精矣，寧復有遺材之憾乎？《菁莪》《棫樸》，雨露之所濡也。國家作人造士之功，莫大焉。《南山之臺》，其德盛矣；邦家之基，以人事君之謂也。當軸諸君子有焉。雖然，受賜不報，豈只尚文等之愆，抑亦諸士之恥也。」遂歌《天保》以祝聖明，坐者皆肅容拱而立。御史曹
translation_en:
…them. “On this journey of ours, can we be free of inward misgivings? For love of worthy men, nothing surpasses ‘Black Robes’ (Zi yi); ‘The Solitary Pear Tree’ (Di du) comes close to it. When sincerity issues from the heart, how could we dare be remiss in this? The cutting, filing, carving, and polishing of ‘The Bend of the Qi’ (Qi yu) mean seeking refinement and bringing it to still greater refinement. Could there then remain any regret over overlooked talent? ‘Luxuriant Mugwort’ (Jing e) and ‘The Oaks’ (Yu pu) tell of what rain and dew nourish. Nothing surpasses the state's achievement in nurturing men and forming scholars. In ‘The Terrace Grass on the Southern Mountain’ (Nan shan zhi tai), virtue flourishes: to be the foundation of the realm means serving one's ruler by providing worthy men. The gentlemen at the helm possess this virtue. Nevertheless, to receive such favors without repaying them would be not only a fault of Shangwen and the rest of us, but also a disgrace to all the scholars.”
They then sang ‘Heaven Protects You’ (Tian bao) to invoke blessings upon His Sagely Majesty. All those seated assumed solemn expressions, clasped their hands, and rose. Censor Cao…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之矣吾徒此行得無内疚乎
好賢莫如緇衣杕杜近似之
矣誠之發於中心而敢有怠
於此乎淇澳之切磋琢磨求
其精而益致其精矣寧復有
遺材之憾乎菁莪棫樸雨露
之所濡也
===
國家作人造士之功莫大焉南
山之臺其德盛矣邦家之基
以人事君之謂也當軸諸君
子有焉雖然受賜不報豈只
尚文等之愆抑亦諸士之耻
也遂歌天保以祝
聖明坐者皆肅容拱而立御史曹
punctuated:
之矣。吾徒此行，得無内疚乎？好賢莫如《緇衣》，《杕杜》近似之矣。誠之發於中心，而敢有怠於此乎？《淇澳》之切磋琢磨，求其精而益致其精矣，寧復有遺材之憾乎？《菁莪》《棫樸》，雨露之所濡也。
國家作人造士之功，莫大焉。南山之臺，其德盛矣；邦家之基，以人事君之謂也。當軸諸君子有焉。雖然，受賜不報，豈只尚文等之愆，抑亦諸士之耻也。遂歌《天保》以祝聖明，坐者皆肅容拱而立。御史曹
translation_en:
… so it is. Can we, on this journey, be free of inward misgivings? For cherishing worthy men, nothing surpasses “Black Robes” (Ziyi); “The Solitary Pear Tree” (D杜, D杜) approaches it. When sincerity springs from the heart, how could we dare to slacken in this? Through the cutting and polishing described in “The Bends of the Qi” (Qi Ao), we seek refinement and bring it to still greater perfection. Could there then remain any regret over overlooked talent? “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing E) and “The Oak and the Shrub” (Yu Pu) speak of nourishment by rain and dew.
Nothing surpasses the state's achievement in nurturing men and cultivating scholars. The sedge on the southern mountain signifies abundant virtue; being the foundation of the realm means serving one's ruler by bringing forward worthy men. The gentlemen at the helm possess these qualities. Nevertheless, to receive such favor without repaying it would be not merely the fault of Shangwen and his companions, but also a disgrace to all the scholars. We therefore sang “Heaven Protects You” (Tian Bao) to offer blessings to His Sagacious Majesty. All those seated assumed solemn expressions and stood with their hands clasped. Censor Cao …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
愚嘗端居而思致治之大典
惟賓興賢能亘古今而弗替
者曷故焉曰是三綱之所繫
也九疇之所屬也故自成周
以降至于後世雖正朔偏安
裔夷雲擾而猶知科舉取士
===
之為重際遇我
朝
列聖稽古右文其典益備耳目之
所睹記蓋蔑以加矣正德己
卯復當大比之期巡按廣西
監察御史曹珪祗奉
德音此為首務棘闈既拓士類爭
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

愚嘗端居而思致治之大典，惟賓興賢能亘古今而弗替者，曷故焉？曰：是三綱之所繫也，九疇之所屬也。故自成周以降，至于後世，雖正朔偏安、裔夷雲擾，而猶知科舉取士之為重。際遇我朝，列聖稽古右文，其典益備，耳目之所睹記，蓋蔑以加矣。正德己卯，復當大比之期，巡按廣西監察御史曹珪祗奉德音，此為首務。棘闈既拓，士類爭
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

I once sat quietly and reflected upon the great institutions by which good government is achieved. Why has the practice of honoring and advancing the worthy and capable endured from antiquity to the present without being abandoned? The answer is that upon it depend the Three Bonds, and to it relate the Nine Categories of the Great Plan. Thus, from the Zhou dynasty onward into later ages, even when the legitimate dynasty held sway only in a regional refuge and peoples of the distant frontiers rose in turmoil like gathering clouds, men still recognized the importance of selecting officials through the civil-service examinations. Under our dynasty, successive sage emperors have studied antiquity and esteemed literary learning, making these institutions ever more complete. Among all that eyes and ears have witnessed and recorded, surely nothing has surpassed them.

In the jimao year of Zhengde [1519], the time for the triennial examination came round again. Cao Gui, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Guangxi, reverently received the imperial pronouncement and made this his foremost duty. Once the examination compound had been opened, the scholars competed …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
先維時總督兩廣都御史楊
旦執經用武注意斯文而總
鎮太監王堂總兵官撫寧侯
朱麒鎮守太監傅倫副總兵
張祐皆預聞焉今致仕左布
政使何珊先事授畫旣即厥
緒於是合四道所簡之士鎖
===
院而三試之其在内提調則
右參政黃衷右參議梁億為
之監試則按察使宗璽僉事
俞緇為之至於監臨獨任其
責者御史曹珪也暨考校試
卷則教諭周尚文楊國本李
從龍林德振常儒甫陳錫賓
punctuated: 先。維時，總督兩廣都御史楊旦執經用武，注意斯文，而總鎮太監王堂、總兵官撫寧侯朱麒、鎮守太監傅倫、副總兵張祐皆預聞焉。今致仕左布政使何珊先事授畫，旣即厥緒，於是合四道所簡之士，鎖院而三試之。其在内提調，則右參政黃衷、右參議梁億為之；監試，則按察使宗璽、僉事俞緇為之。至於監臨獨任其責者，御史曹珪也。暨考校試卷，則教諭周尚文、楊國本、李從龍、林德振、常儒甫、陳錫賓
translation_en:
…to come forward first. At that time, Yang Dan, Censor-in-chief and Governor-general of Liangguang, upheld classical learning while exercising military command and devoted his attention to this literary undertaking. Wang Tang, the eunuch serving as Grand Defender; Zhu Qi, Marquis of Funing and Regional Commander; Fu Lun, the eunuch serving as Regional Defender; and Zhang You, Vice Regional Commander, were all consulted. He Shan, the now-retired Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, had provided plans in advance. Once preparations were under way, the candidates selected by the four circuits were assembled, the examination compound was sealed, and they were examined in three sessions.
Within the compound, Huang Zhong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, and Liang Yi, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner, served as Proctors. Zong Xi, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Yu Zi, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, monitored the examinations. Sole responsibility as Supervising Official rested with Censor Cao Gui. As for evaluating the examination scripts, the Instructors Zhou Shangwen, Yang Guoben, Li Conglong, Lin Dezhen, Chang Rufu, and Chen Xibin…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
應聘而來其在外襄理則右
布政使翁茂南左叅政彭夔
右叅政宋愷副使張祐劉潮
僉事姚鵬楊譽李淳都指揮
同知戴儀皆夙夜匪懈聿觀
厥成旣遵
制額取士刻文為錄以獻世讓
===
忝茲文柄其為自幸實多矣
惡能已於言乎惟昔先王之
世若井田若封建若賓興賢
能皆所謂大經大法也然彼
二者同塗殊歸不能保其不
變也是故井田之後變而為
稅畝徵租封建之後變而為
punctuated:
應聘而來。其在外襄理，則右布政使翁茂南、左叅政彭夔、右叅政宋愷、副使張祐、劉潮、僉事姚鵬、楊譽、李淳、都指揮同知戴儀，皆夙夜匪懈，聿觀厥成。旣遵制額取士，刻文為錄以獻。

世讓忝茲文柄，其為自幸實多矣，惡能已於言乎？惟昔先王之世，若井田，若封建，若賓興賢能，皆所謂大經大法也。然彼二者，同塗殊歸，不能保其不變也。是故井田之後，變而為稅畝徵租；封建之後，變而為
translation_en:
…came in response to the invitation. Assisting with arrangements outside the examination compound were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Weng Maonan, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Peng Kui, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Song Kai, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang You and Liu Chao, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Yao Peng, Yang Yu, and Li Chun, and Regional Military Vice Commissioner Dai Yi. All labored tirelessly morning and night and saw the undertaking through to completion. Having selected candidates according to the imperially prescribed quota, we had the examination compositions printed as a record for presentation.

I, Shirang, unworthily entrusted with authority over this literary selection, have much indeed to count as my good fortune. How could I refrain from saying something? In the age of the former kings, such institutions as the well-field system, the enfeoffment of lords, and the ceremonial reception and advancement of the worthy and capable were all what are called great guiding principles and fundamental laws. Yet the former two, though following the same path, reached different destinations; their preservation without change could not be assured. Thus, the well-field system subsequently changed into taxation by the mu and the collection of rents; the enfeoffment of lords subsequently changed into…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
罷侯置守獨賓興之典萬世
炳如日星嗚呼此可以觀世
道之所寄矣夫廣西古百粤
之區也當先王盛時井田封
建猶未嘗及猶不識不知而
况鄉舉里選之制乎以今日
人文之盛觀之可以知我
===
列聖化成天下之績矣諸士子生
逢
景運睹河洛而不思禹功可乎
或曰今之選舉賓興果如周
禮之三物而無變乎否也愚
應之曰學校以善其基明倫
以敦其本養之六經以造其
punctuated:
罷侯置守，獨賓興之典，萬世炳如日星。嗚呼！此可以觀世道之所寄矣。夫廣西，古百粤之區也。當先王盛時，井田、封建猶未嘗及，猶不識不知，而况鄉舉里選之制乎？以今日人文之盛觀之，可以知我列聖化成天下之績矣。諸士子生逢景運，睹河洛而不思禹功，可乎？
或曰：「今之選舉賓興，果如周禮之三物而無變乎？」否也。愚應之曰：「學校以善其基，明倫以敦其本，養之六經以造其
translation_en:
…abolishing the enfeoffed lords and appointing governors. Only the institution of honoring and recommending worthy men has shone through the ages like the sun and stars. Ah! Here we can see where the moral order of the world finds its support. Guangxi was anciently the territory of the Hundred Yue. Even in the flourishing age of the former kings, the well-field system and feudal enfeoffment had never reached it; its people remained unaware of them, much less of the system of recommending men from townships and selecting them from villages. Judging by the flourishing of culture today, we can recognize the achievements of our successive sage emperors in transforming and perfecting the realm. You scholars were born into this glorious age: could you look upon the Yellow and Luo Rivers without thinking of Yu’s accomplishments?
Someone asks: “Do today’s selection and recommendation of worthy men truly follow the three categories of instruction in the Rites of Zhou without change?” No. I humbly reply: “Schools make their foundation sound; clarification of human relationships strengthens their roots; nurturing them through the Six Classics develops their…”

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
道博之五策以試其能然則
三物固在是矣又何變焉雖
然吾所憂者吾人之變耳靜
言庸違嚮道中廢脩于家而
壞于
天子之庭者聖賢之罪人也又焉
得為三代之士乎世讓不敏
===
願諸士子幸更相勉圖之
直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒
學教諭方世讓謹序
punctuated:
道，博之五策以試其能。然則三物固在是矣，又何變焉？雖然，吾所憂者，吾人之變耳。靜言庸違，嚮道中廢，脩于家而壞于天子之庭者，聖賢之罪人也，又焉得為三代之士乎？世讓不敏，願諸士子幸更相勉圖之。
直隸鳳陽府潁州潁上縣儒學教諭方世讓謹序。
translation_en:
…the Way, and broaden their learning through five policy questions to test their abilities. Thus the three things are indeed present here; what, then, has changed? Nevertheless, what concerns me is change in ourselves. Those who speak well at leisure but act contrary to their words, who turn toward the Way but abandon it halfway, and who cultivate themselves at home but become corrupt at the Son of Heaven’s court are offenders against the sages and worthies. How could they qualify as scholars of the Three Dynasties? I, Shirang, am slow of understanding, but hope that you candidates will encourage one another and strive toward this.
This preface is respectfully written by Fang Shirang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yingshang County, Yingzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili).

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
正德十四年鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史曹珪〔廷獻湖廣黃岡縣人辛未進士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政黄衷〔子和廣東南海縣人丙辰進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參議梁億〔叔永廣東順德縣人辛未進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使宗璽〔朝用直隸建平縣人己未進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事俞緇〔子宜江西鄱陽縣人戊辰進士〕
===
考試官
直隸鳳陽府穎州穎上縣儒學教諭方世讓〔伯禮湖廣巴陵縣人庚午貢士〕
江西南昌府新建縣儒學教諭周尚文〔質夫福建閩縣人庚午貢士〕
同考試官
廣東惠州府博羅縣儒學教諭楊國本〔在培福建莆田縣人庚午貢士〕
江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭李從龍〔孔雨福建莆田縣人丁卯貢士〕
山東濟南府青城縣儒學教諭林德振〔如玉福建閩縣人丙子貢士〕
山東兗州府城武縣儒學教諭宋儒兩〔際學福建莆田縣人癸酉貢士〕
福建興化府仙遊縣儒學教諭陳錫〔元與廣東南海縣人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
正德十四年鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按廣西監察御史曹珪〔廷獻，湖廣黃岡縣人，辛未進士〕。

提調官：
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政黄衷〔子和，廣東南海縣人，丙辰進士〕。
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參議梁億〔叔永，廣東順德縣人，辛未進士〕。

監試官：
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使宗璽〔朝用，直隸建平縣人，己未進士〕。

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
三十而立四十而不惑
人莫不飲食也鮮能知味也
天子討而不伐諸侯伐而不討
易
忠信所以進德也脩辭立其誠所以居業
也知至至之可與幾也知終終之可與
存義也
===
聖人亨以享上帝而大亨以養聖賢
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛
陽卦奇陰卦耦
書
惟德動天無遠弗届滿招損謙受益時乃
天道帝初于歷山往于田日號泣于旻
天于父母負罪引慝祗載見瞽瞍夔夔
齊慄瞽亦允若至誠感神矧茲有苗
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
三十而立，四十而不惑。
人莫不飲食也，鮮能知味也。
天子討而不伐，諸侯伐而不討。

易
忠信所以進德也，脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。
聖人亨以享上帝，而大亨以養聖賢。
歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。
陽卦奇，陰卦耦。

書
惟德動天，無遠弗届。滿招損，謙受益，時乃天道。帝初于歷山，往于田，日號泣于旻天，于父母，負罪引慝，祗載見瞽瞍，夔夔齊慄，瞽亦允若。至誠感神，矧茲有苗！
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
“At thirty, I stood firm; at forty, I was free from doubts.”
“Everyone eats and drinks, but few can discern flavors.”
“The Son of Heaven punishes but does not wage punitive campaigns; the feudal lords wage punitive campaigns but do not pronounce punishment.”

Book of Changes
“Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue. Refining one's words and establishing one's sincerity are the means of abiding in one's work. Knowing where to arrive and arriving there, one may participate in discerning the first stirrings of things; knowing where to end and ending there, one may participate in preserving what is right.”
“The sage cooks offerings to present to the Lord on High, and prepares great feasts to nourish sages and worthies.”
“Place the remaining stalks between the fingers to represent an intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalary months; therefore, place the remainders between the fingers twice before setting a stalk apart again.”
“Yang trigrams are odd; yin trigrams are even.”

Book of Documents
“Virtue alone moves Heaven; there is no distance beyond its reach. Fullness invites loss; humility receives benefit: this is Heaven's way. In his early days at Mount Li, the emperor [Shun] went into the fields and daily cried out in tears to merciful Heaven and to his parents. Taking blame upon himself and acknowledging his faults, he respectfully served and attended upon Gusou. He was reverent, solemn, and trembling, and Gusou, too, became truly compliant. Utter sincerity moves the spirits—how much more, then, these people of Youmiao!”

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
佑賢輔德顯忠遂良
不作無益害有益功乃成不貴異物賤用
物民乃足
僕臣正厥后克正
詩
知子之來之雜佩以贈之知子之順之雜
佩以問之知子之好之雜佩以報之
旣見君子錫我百朋
受福無疆四方之綱
===
在彼無惡在此無斁庶幾夙夜以永終譽
春秋
初獻六羽隱公五年衛人來媵成公八年伯姬
歸于宋 季孫行父如宋致女 晉人
來媵俱成公九年齊人來媵成公十年

詩
知子之來之，雜佩以贈之；知子之順之，雜佩以問之；知子之好之，雜佩以報之。

初獻六羽，隱公五年；衛人來媵，成公八年。伯姬歸于宋；季孫行父如宋致女；晉人來媵，俱成公九年。齊人來媵，成公十年。

translation_en:
Assist the worthy and support the virtuous; give distinction to the loyal and advance the good.
Do not undertake useless things to the detriment of useful ones, and your work will succeed. Do not prize exotic objects and disparage useful goods, and the people will have enough.
When the attendant servants are upright, their sovereign can be upright.

Book of Odes
Knowing that you have come, I present you with assorted girdle pendants. Knowing your goodwill, I offer assorted girdle pendants as a greeting. Knowing your affection, I give assorted girdle pendants in return.
Having seen the noble lord, I have been granted a hundred strings of cowries.
He receives blessings without limit and serves as the guiding cord for the four quarters.
There he is not disliked; here no one tires of him. May he remain diligent morning and night, preserving his good name forever.

Spring and Autumn Annals

Bo Ji went to Song to marry; Jisun Hangfu went to Song to formally deliver the bride; men of Jin came escorting secondary brides: all in the ninth year of Duke Cheng. Men of Qi came escorting secondary brides: tenth year of Duke Cheng.
The army of Qi relocated the inhabitants of Ping, Zi, and Wu in Ji: first year of Duke Zhuang.
The royal daughter went to Qi to marry: eleventh year of Duke Zhuang. Bo Ji went to Qi 杞 to marry: twenty-fifth year of Duke Zhuang. The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the royal heir apparent at Shouzhi: fifth year of Duke Xi. … the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. Ninth year of Duke Xi.

Book of Rites
After three years of cultivation, there must be enough food stored for one year; after nine years of cultivation, there must be enough food stored for three years.
Heaven displays its signs, and the sage takes them as his model. The suburban sacrifice serves to make manifest the Way of Heaven.
Bring together the harmony of life-giving energies and guide the practice of the five constant virtues.
A ruler must not use small matters to plan great ones, speak of what is near on the basis of what is distant, or use what is within to devise plans for what is outside.

Second Session
Discourse
Censors and remonstrance officials should take the impartial judgment of all under Heaven as their guiding principle.

One topic from among imperial edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
