title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
判語〔五條〕
出使不復命
官馬不調習
告狀不受理
徒囚不應役
造作不如法
第叁場
策五道
問帝王之御極皆有典則垂訓而其後世
===
之君能守文繼志者亦或鮮矣若我
孝宗敬皇帝暨惟
今上大明會典之作誠所謂善繼善述而集一
代之大成者故其制作損益皆本於
聖祖高皇帝御製群書然其實有因事而類見
者有專主以立法者可得而詳言歟予
嘗伏讀而歎其大綱日麗萬目星羅體
統截然而名分不易也可指言其實歟
唐虞而下致治莫備於周不知會典之
punctuated:
判語〔五條〕
出使不復命。
官馬不調習。
告狀不受理。
徒囚不應役。
造作不如法。

第叁場
策五道

問：帝王之御極，皆有典則垂訓，而其後世之君能守文繼志者，亦或鮮矣。若我孝宗敬皇帝暨惟今上，《大明會典》之作，誠所謂善繼善述而集一代之大成者。故其制作損益，皆本於聖祖高皇帝御製群書。然其實有因事而類見者，有專主以立法者，可得而詳言歟？予嘗伏讀而歎其大綱日麗，萬目星羅，體統截然而名分不易也。可指言其實歟？唐虞而下，致治莫備於周，不知《會典》之
translation_en:
Legal judgments [five items]
Failure to report back upon completing an official mission.
Failure to train government horses.
Failure to accept and hear a complaint.
Failure of prisoners sentenced to penal servitude to perform their assigned labor.
Construction or manufacture that does not conform to regulations.

Third Session
Five policy questions

Question: When emperors and kings ascend the throne, they all leave authoritative rules and instructions for posterity. Yet among their successors, those able to uphold the established institutions and carry on their intentions have sometimes been few. In the case of our Emperor Xiaozong Jing and His present Majesty, the compilation of the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian) truly exemplifies skill in carrying on and elaborating the work of their predecessors, bringing together the consummate achievements of a dynasty. Thus its institutional arrangements, modifications, and additions all derive from the various works imperially composed by the Sagely Progenitor, Emperor Gao. Yet among these works, some present matters by category as particular affairs arise, while others concentrate on a particular subject to establish regulations. Can you explain these in detail?

I have reverently read them and marveled that their main principles shine like the sun, their myriad particulars are arrayed like stars, their institutional hierarchy is sharply defined, and their distinctions of status remain unaltered. Can you identify concrete instances and explain them? From the eras of Tang and Yu onward, no age surpassed the Zhou in the completeness of its arrangements for good government. I wonder whether the Collected Statutes’…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
規模大要有合於周制者果何在歟自
是而降若漢唐宋若胡元皆未嘗無一
代之作也叅之會典可同日而語乎至
於所謂制異曠典法殊紀傳事雖微而
必錄令已寢而亦書文務之載華去潤
色而務從實者又未必無其說也爾諸
生誦法傾心之日久矣願鋪張揚厲探
本遡源以對毋遜毋忽
問立德立功立言儒者之業也固有優於
===
德而功或不逮茂於功而言則不文信
乎其兼長之難矣抑不知先立乎其大
者則其次者可畧不然則交致之功果
亦有要乎否耶蓋嘗迹古人之故而疑
焉姑舉其著者質之夫忠直廉約德之
屬也理治安攘功之屬也詞章訓詁又
言之屬也然忠潔而負讒於楚顧以為
過嚴直而見憚於漢恒疑於褊去官留
犢者或斥其矯垢衣惡食者或辨其姦
punctuated:
規模大要有合於周制者，果何在歟？自是而降，若漢唐宋，若胡元，皆未嘗無一代之作也。叅之會典，可同日而語乎？至於所謂制異曠典，法殊紀傳，事雖微而必錄，令已寢而亦書，文務之載華，去潤色而務從實者，又未必無其說也。爾諸生誦法傾心之日久矣，願鋪張揚厲，探本遡源以對，毋遜毋忽。

問：立德、立功、立言，儒者之業也。固有優於德而功或不逮，茂於功而言則不文，信乎其兼長之難矣！抑不知先立乎其大者，則其次者可畧；不然，則交致之功，果亦有要乎否耶？蓋嘗迹古人之故而疑焉，姑舉其著者質之。夫忠直廉約，德之屬也；理治安攘，功之屬也；詞章訓詁，又言之屬也。然忠潔而負讒於楚，顧以為過；嚴直而見憚於漢，恒疑於褊；去官留犢者，或斥其矯；垢衣惡食者，或辨其姦。
translation_en:
…where, precisely, do its overall structure and principal features accord with the institutions of Zhou? In subsequent ages, the Han, Tang, and Song, as well as the non-Chinese Yuan, each produced works of their own dynasty. Compared with the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming, can these be spoken of in the same breath? As for the assertions that its arrangement differs from exceptional precedents [?], and its method from annals and biographies; that events, however minor, are invariably recorded, and ordinances, even when no longer in force, are also included; and that its writing seeks to record ornate language [?], yet discards embellishment and strives for factual accuracy—these, too, may have their explanations. You students have long devoted yourselves wholeheartedly to studying and taking it as your model. I hope you will expound its merits fully and vigorously, probe its foundations, and trace its origins in your answers. Neither hold back nor be careless.

Question: Establishing virtue, achieving meritorious deeds, and leaving enduring words are the undertakings of a Confucian scholar. Certainly, some excel in virtue yet fall short in achievement, while others have outstanding achievements yet lack literary refinement in their words. Truly, it is difficult to excel in all three! Yet might establishing the greater first allow the lesser to receive less attention? If not, is there indeed an essential method for attaining all three together? I have examined the circumstances of men of antiquity and found grounds for doubt. Let me select some prominent examples and put them to you. Loyalty, uprightness, integrity, and frugality belong to virtue; bringing orderly government, securing peace, and repelling threats belong to achievement; literary composition and textual exegesis belong to enduring words. Yet the man whose loyalty and purity brought slander upon him in Chu was nevertheless thought excessive; the man whose stern uprightness made him feared in Han was repeatedly suspected of narrow-mindedness. The man who left a calf behind when departing office was sometimes denounced as affected; the man who wore soiled clothes and ate poor food was sometimes exposed as treacherous…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
若然者德將何據而脩耶睢陽之績未
免流俗之口澶淵之役擬於城下之盟
請伐高麗者或致病於腹心應變成務
者或致亂於天寳若然者功將何施而
可耶潛心大業災異之論可疵博極群
書美新之累非細頌聖德者而風雅不
類著僮約者以過舉自彰若然者立言
君子又將何所取正而後精且粹耶豈
數子有諸己者不能無弊抑後儒之評
===
之見互有得失也諸生脩於家也素矣
其德其業固未可知如以言取子即今
日之急也不可不對
問事變萬殊理無定在而人之智慮有所
及有所不及稽諸古人已行之迹其在
當時可否異同之議若持訟牒於公庭
有未易以口舌争焉姑舉其可見者與
諸士評之夫矯命專師均一恤鄰也而
有是有非立國樹黨均一謀國也而有
punctuated:
若然者，德將何據而脩耶？睢陽之績，未免流俗之口；澶淵之役，擬於城下之盟；請伐高麗者，或致病於腹心；應變成務者，或致亂於天寳。若然者，功將何施而可耶？潛心大業，災異之論可疵；博極群書，美新之累非細；頌聖德者，而風雅不類；著僮約者，以過舉自彰。若然者，立言君子又將何所取正，而後精且粹耶？豈數子有諸己者不能無弊，抑後儒之評之見互有得失也？諸生脩於家也素矣，其德其業固未可知，如以言取子，即今日之急也，不可不對。

問：事變萬殊，理無定在，而人之智慮有所及，有所不及。稽諸古人已行之迹，其在當時可否異同之議，若持訟牒於公庭，有未易以口舌争焉。姑舉其可見者，與諸士評之。夫矯命專師，均一恤鄰也，而有是有非；立國樹黨，均一謀國也，而有
translation_en:
If this is so, on what basis should one cultivate virtue? The achievement at Suiyang did not escape the criticism of common opinion; the campaign at Chanyuan was likened to a covenant made beneath the city walls under duress. One who requested an expedition against Gaoli may have brought affliction upon the heartland; one who responded to changing circumstances and accomplished affairs may have brought about the disorder of the Tianbao era. If this is so, how can one perform meritorious deeds and meet with approval? One who devoted himself to the great undertaking of learning could be faulted for his discussions of calamities and anomalies; one whose learning encompassed the whole range of books incurred no slight disgrace through his Praise of Xin. One who extolled sagely virtue failed to accord with the Airs and Odes; one who wrote the Contract with a Servant made his own improper conduct manifest. If this is so, where should gentlemen who seek to establish enduring words find their standard, so that their writings may become refined and pure? Could it be that what these men possessed within themselves was not free of faults, or that the critical opinions of later scholars [?] were themselves partly sound and partly mistaken? You candidates have long cultivated yourselves at home. Your virtue and accomplishments cannot yet be known with certainty, but selecting you on the basis of your words is the urgent task of this day. You must give an answer.

Question: Events and changes take countless forms, and principle has no fixed locus; human intelligence and deliberation can encompass some things but not others. When we examine the deeds of the ancients, the debates in their own times over approval and disapproval, agreement and disagreement, resemble litigants presenting their pleadings in a court of law: some matters cannot readily be settled by verbal argument. Let us take some evident examples and assess them together with you gentlemen. Falsifying a command and taking sole control of an army were alike acts of solicitude for a neighboring state, yet one was judged right and another wrong. Establishing a state and building a faction were alike schemes undertaken for the state, yet there were…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
得有失逼水置陣其勢同也然一以之
勝一以之負空國出師其迹同也然一
由之成一由之敗矯制立功若非矣或
者又以為可封負罪受辟當刑矣或者
又以為不當刑忘君之讎者彼此同歸
議者乃判功罪為兩途復父之讎者彼
此無間斷者輒施輕重之二典靈州之
棄守聚議紛紛未必皆是也綏州之城
否衆口籍籍不能無非也凡此之類窮
===
理者所當精察而明辨諸士子格物致
知之學其有素矣請悉心剖析以為古
今一大斷案不亦可乎毋委曰我則不
暇
問言行君子之樞機也古稱吉人之辭寡
而病商俗之靡曰利口焉若是乎聖人
之不貴言也而語善專對言果不可以已
耶又曰亂世之人尚通而聖人著其教
也必危行焉若是乎君子之行果而已
punctuated:
得有失。逼水置陣，其勢同也，然一以之勝，一以之負；空國出師，其迹同也，然一由之成，一由之敗。矯制立功，若非矣，或者又以為可封；負罪受辟，當刑矣，或者又以為不當刑。忘君之讎者，彼此同歸，議者乃判功罪為兩途；復父之讎者，彼此無間，斷者輒施輕重之二典。靈州之棄守，聚議紛紛，未必皆是也；綏州之城否，衆口籍籍，不能無非也。凡此之類，窮理者所當精察而明辨。諸士子格物致知之學，其有素矣，請悉心剖析，以為古今一大斷案，不亦可乎？毋委曰：「我則不暇。」

問：言行，君子之樞機也。古稱吉人之辭寡，而病商俗之靡，曰利口焉。若是乎聖人之不貴言也，而語善專對，言果不可以已耶？又曰：「亂世之人尚通。」而聖人著其教也，必危行焉。若是乎君子之行果而已
translation_en:
…some gained and others lost. In deploying troops with water close behind them, the circumstances were the same; yet one thereby won and another lost. In emptying the state to send forth an army, the actions were the same; yet one thereby succeeded and another failed. To forge an imperial decree and achieve merit would seem wrong, yet some have held that it deserved enfeoffment. Those who incurred guilt and suffered punishment would seem to have deserved it, yet some have held that they should not have been punished. Those who forgot the vengeance owed for their lord were alike in this respect, yet commentators assigned merit to one and guilt to another. Those who avenged their fathers differed in no respect, yet those judging them applied two standards, one lenient and the other severe. Over whether to abandon or hold Lingzhou, assembled opinions were numerous and conflicting; they cannot all have been right. Over whether to fortify Suizhou, many voices clamored; some must have been wrong. All such cases require those who investigate principles to examine them closely and distinguish clearly. You candidates have long pursued the learning of investigating things and extending knowledge. Would it not be fitting for you to analyze these matters with your whole attention and render a definitive judgment encompassing past and present? Do not evade the task by saying, “I have no time for this.”

Question: Words and conduct are the hinges and springs of the gentleman’s actions. An ancient saying praises the good man for being sparing of words, while another deplores the degeneration of Shang customs, speaking of glib tongues. Such, then, is the sage’s low estimation of speech. Yet he speaks approvingly of the ability to respond independently as an envoy: can speech, after all, not be dispensed with? It is also said, “People in an age of disorder prize accommodation.” Yet when the sage sets forth his teaching, he insists on upright conduct. Does this mean that the gentleman’s conduct consists simply in being resolute…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中庸乃譏行怪又安在其不尚通耶後
世賢者語默之間通檢之迹或應對辨
給或言若不出或詞甚清辨或終日恂
恂或輕肆直言或不荅國事或束身自
脩或任心獨詣或候見不顧或惟事造
謁或恥與俗交或自同傭人是其語者
默者檢者通者後世蓋甞仰而觀之不
知其言也於事何所述其默也於道何
所營其通也何以周務而其檢也何以
===
育德耶抑不知於聖人言動之度果有
合乎否也茲欲言罔口過而行鮮怨惡
焉何道而可
問養民與兵政之紀也蓋不祛其患而厚
其生天下無安民不裕其食而節其力
天下無良兵此有識者所共知也巖栖
露宿老稚沿江而行丐廣西之民困矣
健逃老死單弱隨籍而紀錄廣西之卒
耗矣民困而供億且繁卒耗而饋餉不
punctuated:
中庸乃譏行怪，又安在其不尚通耶？後世賢者，語默之間，通檢之迹，或應對辨給，或言若不出，或詞甚清辨，或終日恂恂，或輕肆直言，或不荅國事，或束身自脩，或任心獨詣，或候見不顧，或惟事造謁，或恥與俗交，或自同傭人。是其語者、默者、檢者、通者，後世蓋甞仰而觀之。不知其言也，於事何所述？其默也，於道何所營？其通也，何以周務？而其檢也，何以育德耶？抑不知於聖人言動之度，果有合乎否也？茲欲言罔口過，而行鮮怨惡焉，何道而可？

問：養民與兵，政之紀也。蓋不祛其患而厚其生，天下無安民；不裕其食而節其力，天下無良兵。此有識者所共知也。巖栖露宿，老稚沿江而行丐，廣西之民困矣；健逃老死，單弱隨籍而紀錄，廣西之卒耗矣。民困而供億且繁，卒耗而饋餉不
translation_en:
…Yet the Doctrine of the Mean criticizes eccentric conduct: how, then, can it be said not to value accommodation? Among worthy men of later ages, in their speech and silence and in their conduct, whether accommodating or restrained, some were quick and eloquent in their replies, while others seemed scarcely able to speak; some expressed themselves with great clarity and eloquence, while others remained modest and deferential all day; some spoke frankly and without restraint, while others would not answer questions about affairs of state; some disciplined themselves and cultivated their character, while others followed their own inclinations and pursued an independent course; some disregarded those waiting for an audience [?], while others occupied themselves solely with making visits to persons of standing; some were ashamed to associate with ordinary people, while others placed themselves on a level with hired laborers. Those who spoke, those who remained silent, those who exercised restraint, and those who accommodated themselves to circumstances—all have been looked up to by later generations. Yet what did their speech set forth concerning affairs? What did their silence accomplish for the Way? How did their accommodation enable them to attend to practical duties, and how did their restraint nurture virtue? Indeed, did they truly conform to the sages’ standards of speech and action? If one now wishes to speak without verbal fault and act while incurring little resentment or hatred, by what way can this be achieved?

Question: Providing for the people and the troops is a fundamental principle of government. Unless their troubles are removed and their livelihoods enriched, there can be no contented people in the realm; unless their food supplies are made ample and their strength spared, there can be no good troops in the realm. This is common knowledge among discerning men. Dwelling among rocks and sleeping in the open, old and young wander along the rivers begging: the people of Guangxi are destitute. The able-bodied flee and the old die; the few and weak who remain are entered in the registers: Guangxi’s troops are depleted. Yet although the people are destitute, the demands for supplies remain numerous; although the troops are depleted, provisions and military pay are not…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
減此又有識者所共憂也振而處之曷
為其方乎蓋嘗聞之柴中行之為幹官
而減苗斛應孟明之為經略而除抑配
至我
朝或停逃亡之租或節無經之費養民之術
可謂要矣而不救於逋負者何耶許仲
宣為轉運而罷征交之士謝麟知桂州
而全近郡之兵至我
朝或借戍於湖廣或仰給於廣東養兵之術
===
亦謂備矣而無補於脫耗者何耶昔人
有言臨政論治不若退而更化今必公
私俱贍而民始裕戰守有備而兵始精
不知更其化而後可以赴吾民之急乎
抑其舊政者可脩而舉也諸生皆明當
世之務而於鄉邦之故計之必審幸盡
言之以告在位者
punctuated: 減，此又有識者所共憂也。振而處之，曷為其方乎？蓋嘗聞之，柴中行之為幹官而減苗斛，應孟明之為經略而除抑配。至我朝，或停逃亡之租，或節無經之費，養民之術可謂要矣，而不救於逋負者，何耶？許仲宣為轉運而罷征交之士，謝麟知桂州而全近郡之兵。至我朝，或借戍於湖廣，或仰給於廣東，養兵之術亦謂備矣，而無補於脫耗者，何耶？昔人有言：「臨政論治，不若退而更化。」今必公私俱贍而民始裕，戰守有備而兵始精。不知更其化而後可以赴吾民之急乎？抑其舊政者可脩而舉也？諸生皆明當世之務，而於鄉邦之故，計之必審，幸盡言之，以告在位者。
translation_en:
…are not reduced. This, too, is a shared concern of discerning men. By what means can relief be provided and the situation addressed? We have heard that Chai Zhongxing, while serving as an administrative officer, reduced the grain-tax assessments, and that Ying Mengming, while serving as Military Commissioner, abolished compulsory levies. Under our own dynasty, taxes owed by those who had fled have sometimes been suspended, and expenditures lacking established authorization have sometimes been curtailed. These methods of sustaining the people may be called essential; why, then, have they failed to remedy tax arrears? Xu Zhongxuan, as Transport Commissioner, withdrew the troops campaigning against Jiaozhi; Xie Lin, as Prefect of Guizhou, preserved the troops of the nearby prefectures. Under our own dynasty, troops have sometimes been borrowed from Huguang for garrison duty, and supplies obtained from Guangdong. These methods of sustaining the troops may likewise be called comprehensive; why, then, have they done nothing to remedy desertion and dwindling numbers?

A man of old said: “To discuss good government while administering affairs is less effective than stepping back and reforming the system.” Now, only when both public and private needs are amply supplied will the people enjoy sufficiency; only when preparations for both fighting and defense are complete will the troops become proficient. Must we reform the system before we can respond to our people's urgent needs? Or can the existing policies be repaired and put into effect? You candidates all understand the affairs of the present age, and you must have carefully considered the circumstances of your native province. Please set forth your views fully, so as to inform those in office.

同考試官教諭常批論語一題士子類騁浮
辭讀之令人可厭是作獨能融會傳註成文且筆

考試官教諭方批集註意正如此
旣壯而有定守旣強而有定見聖人自言其所
進然也夫聖雖無所不通非可以不學而至者
也苟不求諸所示之學抑何由而知其然哉想
昔吾夫子之意若曰理具於心皆吾之所當知
心見於事皆吾之所當為吾十有五嘗志於學
矣由十五而三十追惟斯時道蓋有所得耶以
心御氣而不為氣所御雖紛紜舛錯之集吾則
居貞守固而屹無所撓焉以心移氣而不為氣
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

三十而立，四十而不惑。

楊琇

同考試官教諭常批：論語一題，士子類騁浮辭，讀之令人可厭。是作獨能融會傳註成文，且筆勢整整，未嘗苟下一語，蓋有所得者也。是宜錄出，以式後學。

考試官教諭周批：論語義如此作，良是。

考試官教諭方批：集註意正如此。

旣壯而有定守，旣強而有定見，聖人自言其所進然也。夫聖雖無所不通，非可以不學而至者也。苟不求諸所示之學，抑何由而知其然哉？想昔吾夫子之意若曰：理具於心，皆吾之所當知；心見於事，皆吾之所當為。吾十有五嘗志於學矣。由十五而三十，追惟斯時，道蓋有所得耶？以心御氣，而不為氣所御，雖紛紜舛錯之集，吾則居貞守固，而屹無所撓焉；以心移氣，而不為氣
translation_en:

“At thirty, I stood firm; at forty, I was free from perplexity.”

Yang Xiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chang, Instructor: On this question from the Analects, candidates generally indulge in empty rhetoric, making their essays tiresome to read. This composition alone succeeds in integrating the commentaries into a coherent essay. Moreover, its writing is consistently well ordered, with not a single phrase carelessly set down. Its author evidently has attained some understanding. It deserves to be transcribed here as a model for later students.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: An exposition of the meaning of the Analects written like this is very sound.

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: This is precisely the meaning of the Collected Commentaries.

Having reached maturity, he had a firm adherence to principle; having reached his prime, he had settled discernment. Thus did the Sage himself describe his progress. Although there is nothing the Sage does not comprehend, this is no condition that can be attained without learning. If we do not seek understanding through the learning he indicated, how can we know why this was so? I imagine that our Master’s meaning then was as if he said: “The principles inherent in the mind are all things I ought to know; the mind’s manifestations in affairs are all things I ought to put into practice. At fifteen, I had already set my heart on learning. From fifteen to thirty—looking back upon that time, had I not gained some understanding of the Way? I used my mind to govern my vital force, rather than being governed by it. Even when confusion and disorder converged upon me, I remained steadfast in rectitude and firm in my resolve, standing unshaken. I used my mind to transform my vital force, rather than being, by that vital force …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所移雖紛華盛麗之來吾則居安操約而略無
苟動焉確乎其操而非疆制也卓乎其守而非
力勝也其自立有如此者由三十而四十迨惟
斯時道蓋無所疑耶凡事所當然者事至則理
形介石之固足以決萬變之幾微而理欲其判
然矣凡物所當然者物來則順應一致之理有
以通吾心之百慮而得失其較然矣剖析不患
其弗詳也辨別不患其弗盡也其不惑有如此
者是則三十而立則無所事志也可知四十不
===
惑則無所事守也可知聖人進德固亦有序也
哉雖然夫子生知安行豈嘗若是其積累歟特
因其近似以自名見其亦由學而至所以勉進
後人耳後世乃謂聖本生知非學可至是又自
棄已噫典謨何病乎芻蕘途人豈乖於堯舜有
志於大學者其潛心焉
人莫不飲食也鮮能知味也
劉存仁
同考試官教諭林 批 或問之義甚明場中上字
punctuated:
所移，雖紛華盛麗之來，吾則居安操約，而略無苟動焉。確乎其操，而非疆制也；卓乎其守，而非力勝也。其自立有如此者。由三十而四十，迨惟斯時，道蓋無所疑耶？凡事所當然者，事至則理形，介石之固，足以決萬變之幾微，而理欲其判然矣。凡物所當然者，物來則順應，一致之理，有以通吾心之百慮，而得失其較然矣。剖析不患其弗詳也，辨別不患其弗盡也。其不惑有如此者。是則三十而立，則無所事志也，可知；四十不惑，則無所事守也，可知。聖人進德，固亦有序也哉！雖然，夫子生知安行，豈嘗若是其積累歟？特因其近似以自名，見其亦由學而至，所以勉進後人耳。後世乃謂聖本生知，非學可至，是又自棄已。噫！典謨何病乎芻蕘？途人豈乖於堯舜？有志於大學者，其潛心焉。
人莫不飲食也，鮮能知味也。
劉存仁
同考試官教諭林批：或問之義甚明，場中上字
translation_en:
…moved by it. Even when dazzling splendor presents itself, I remain at ease and hold to simplicity, never acting rashly in the slightest. Firm indeed is my resolve, yet it is not forcibly imposed; lofty indeed is my steadfastness, yet it is not achieved through strenuous conquest. Such was my standing firm. From thirty to forty, reflecting upon that time, had I perhaps reached a point where I had no doubts about the Way? As for what ought to be done in every affair, when an affair arises, its principle becomes manifest. A firmness like rock suffices to discern the subtlest beginnings amid myriad changes, and principle and desire stand clearly distinguished. As for the proper response to every thing, when things present themselves, I respond accordingly. The principle of unity runs through my mind’s hundred deliberations, and right and wrong become clear. There is no fear that analysis will lack detail or that discrimination will be incomplete. Such was my freedom from perplexity. Thus we can understand that, once I stood firm at thirty, there was no further need to exert myself in fixing my aspiration; once I was free from perplexity at forty, there was no further need to exert myself in maintaining my resolve. Surely even a sage advances in virtue by stages!
Yet the Master knew from birth and acted with effortless ease: did he ever really have to accumulate learning in this fashion? He merely described himself through approximate comparisons, showing that he too had arrived through learning, in order to encourage later generations to advance. Yet people of later ages say that sages are inherently born knowing and that their attainment cannot be reached through learning. This is simply to abandon oneself. Alas! How could the Canons and Counsels disdain the words of grass-cutters and wood-gatherers? How could an ordinary passerby be fundamentally at odds with Yao and Shun? Let those who aspire to the Great Learning devote their minds to this.
There is no one who does not eat and drink, yet few can discern the flavor.
Liu Cunren
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The meaning of the Questions and Answers is very clearly understood. Among the candidates in the examination hall, the word above [?] …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
類為所窘殊不通暢惟此作詞理兼到是宜錄出
考試官教諭周批詞氣純厚自是中庸文
字樣宜錄以式
考試官教諭方批體貼詳明句句皆本色
語非性理之學不能有此
中庸明人同具乎道之中自失乎道之中夫道
以中為至也人皆有之而自不察此所以有過
不及之弊歟中庸引夫子之言以釋首章之義
如此且道之所謂中者乃天命人心之正當然
===
不易之理固不外乎民生日用之間也試言諸
飲食彼夫冬而湯夏而水人莫不飲也飲有正
味必察之而後知人或飲以濟渴未之能察也
則飲焉而得其正味者幾何朝而饔夕而飧人
莫不食也食有正味必察之而後得人或食以
濟饑未之能察也則食焉而識其正味者幾何
是故若知若愚不能外此道而為知則道常在
人而人何可離道乎今則知者知之過愚者不
及知其在知者之揣摩也猶夫愚者之昏昧也
punctuated:
類為所窘，殊不通暢，惟此作詞理兼到，是宜錄出。
考試官教諭周批：詞氣純厚，自是中庸文字樣，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭方批：體貼詳明，句句皆本色語，非性理之學不能有此。
中庸明人同具乎道之中，自失乎道之中。夫道以中為至也，人皆有之而自不察，此所以有過不及之弊歟？中庸引夫子之言以釋首章之義如此。且道之所謂中者，乃天命人心之正、當然不易之理，固不外乎民生日用之間也。試言諸飲食：彼夫冬而湯，夏而水，人莫不飲也。飲有正味，必察之而後知。人或飲以濟渴，未之能察也，則飲焉而得其正味者幾何？朝而饔，夕而飧，人莫不食也。食有正味，必察之而後得。人或食以濟饑，未之能察也，則食焉而識其正味者幾何？是故若知若愚，不能外此道而為知，則道常在人，而人何可離道乎？今則知者知之過，愚者不及知，其在知者之揣摩也，猶夫愚者之昏昧也。
translation_en:
…most were hampered by it, and their writing was far from fluent. This composition alone succeeds in both expression and reasoning, and therefore deserves inclusion.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: Its language and tenor are pure and substantial. This is truly an exemplar of writing on the Doctrine of the Mean and should be included as a model.
Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: Its close engagement with the meaning is detailed and clear; every sentence speaks in terms true to the subject. Such writing is impossible without learning in human nature and principle.
The Doctrine of the Mean makes clear that people all possess the Mean of the Way, yet themselves lose that Mean. The Way takes the Mean as its highest attainment. Everyone possesses it, yet fails to discern it: is this not the source of the faults of excess and deficiency? Such is the meaning conveyed when the Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Master's words to explain its opening chapter. Moreover, what is called the Mean of the Way is the rectitude Heaven ordains in the human heart, the principle of what ought to be, which does not change. It certainly does not lie outside the everyday activities of people's lives.
Consider drinking and eating. In winter people drink hot water, and in summer cool water: no one goes without drinking. Drink has its proper flavor, which must be discerned before it can be known. Some people drink merely to relieve thirst and cannot discern it; how many, then, drink and apprehend its proper flavor? People take their morning meal and their evening meal: no one goes without eating. Food has its proper flavor, which must be discerned before it can be apprehended. Some people eat merely to relieve hunger and cannot discern it; how many, then, eat and recognize its proper flavor?
Thus, whether wise or foolish, people cannot exercise their understanding outside this Way. The Way is therefore always within people: how could they depart from it? Yet the wise now go too far in their understanding, while the foolish fall short of understanding. The conjectures and calculations of the wise are just like the benightedness of the foolish.…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
然則知此道而察其中者何落落歟道之不行
有由也已若賢若不肖不能外此道而為行則
道常在人而人何可違道乎今則賢者行之過
不肖者不及行其在賢者之刻意也猶夫不肖
者之卑污也然則行斯道而察其中者何寥寥
歟道之不明有由也已吁道之得喪由於中之
存亡中之存亡係於人之察否然則中庸果不
可能也哉粤自先王迹熄教化廢而隄防壞士
學於異端之後言道德者務高遠而遺世用語
===
政理者務卑近而非師古當時號賢知者猶不
免於過中失正他尚何望焉子思懼夫愈久而
愈失其真也於是推本堯舜以來相傳之意揭
其體要於中庸之首章此以下又歷引言以發
厥旨可謂喫緊為人矣學者玩味而有得焉精
一執中之傳豈俟他求而後得哉
天子討而不伐諸侯伐而不討
陳汝謨
同考試官教諭楊 批 〔討伐二字說得透徹孟〕
punctuated:
然則知此道而察其中者何落落歟？道之不行有由也已。若賢若不肖，不能外此道而為行，則道常在人，而人何可違道乎？今則賢者行之過，不肖者不及行，其在賢者之刻意也，猶夫不肖者之卑污也。然則行斯道而察其中者何寥寥歟？道之不明有由也已。吁！道之得喪由於中之存亡，中之存亡係於人之察否。然則中庸果不可能也哉？粤自先王迹熄，教化廢而隄防壞，士學於異端之後，言道德者務高遠而遺世用，語政理者務卑近而非師古。當時號賢知者猶不免於過中失正，他尚何望焉？子思懼夫愈久而愈失其真也，於是推本堯舜以來相傳之意，揭其體要於《中庸》之首章。此以下又歷引言以發厥旨，可謂喫緊為人矣。學者玩味而有得焉，精一執中之傳豈俟他求而後得哉？

天子討而不伐，諸侯伐而不討。
陳汝謨
同考試官教諭楊批〔討伐二字說得透徹，孟〕
translation_en:
…Why, then, are those who understand this Way and discern its mean so few? There is indeed a reason why the Way is not practiced. Neither the worthy nor the unworthy can act outside this Way. Thus the Way is always present in people: how could they depart from it? Yet now the worthy go too far in practicing it, while the unworthy fall short. The strained effort of the worthy is like the baseness of the unworthy. Why, then, are those who practice this Way and discern its mean so rare? There is indeed a reason why the Way is not understood. Alas! Gaining or losing the Way depends on whether the mean is preserved or lost; preserving or losing the mean depends on whether people discern it. Is the practice of the mean truly impossible, then?

Ever since the traces of the former kings vanished, moral instruction has fallen into disuse and its safeguards have crumbled. Scholars have pursued learning in the wake of heterodox teachings. Those who speak of the Way and virtue strive for the lofty and remote, neglecting practical use in the world; those who discuss government strive for the low and immediate, rejecting the example of antiquity. Even those reputed worthy and wise in their time could not avoid overshooting the mean and losing what is right. What could one expect of the others? Zisi feared that, as time passed, the truth would be increasingly lost. He therefore traced back to its source the meaning transmitted since Yao and Shun, setting forth its essential substance in the opening chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean. In the chapters that follow, he repeatedly cited sayings to elucidate its purport. This may truly be called an earnest effort on behalf of others. If learners ponder these words and gain an understanding of them, why should they have to seek elsewhere to apprehend the transmitted teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean?

“The Son of Heaven condemns offenses but does not wage punitive campaigns; the feudal lords wage punitive campaigns but do not condemn offenses.”
By Chen Rumo.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: 〔The two terms ‘condemning offenses’ and ‘waging punitive campaigns’ are explained thoroughly. Meng…〕

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
子尊王黜伯底意溢於言表而文復峻整筆力學力亦
甚相副錄之非但見子之才也
考試官教諭周批辭嚴義正是孟子文字
錄之
考試官教諭方批理致到處辭氣亦到作
者作者
大君出用師之命列辟奉用師之命蓋治師邦
之大政也命出於上而奉於下焉尚何僭紊之
有哉昔孟子舉三王之事以律五霸之罪謂夫
===
古者王章克正侯度聿脩威福之柄不移征伐
之權亦異是故畿方千里提封萬國天子也其
勢雖有常尊矣然政典所專則天討焉蓋四方
之國有方命而不恭者刑固當脩也於焉發六
師之號申九伐之灋命彼方伯帥群后而底天
罰嚴簡書之譴重推轂之威詔彼連帥徵有眾
而致邦禁將見王威所向足以畏大而懷小何
嘗親用黃鉞御戎行而制攻取耶赫怒所震足
以推亡而固存何嘗躬屬櫜鞬濟貪忿而夸武
punctuated:
子尊王黜伯底意溢於言表，而文復峻整，筆力、學力亦甚相副。錄之，非但見子之才也。
考試官教諭周批：辭嚴義正，是孟子文字。錄之。
考試官教諭方批：理致到處，辭氣亦到。作者！作者！
大君出用師之命，列辟奉用師之命。蓋治師，邦之大政也。命出於上而奉於下焉，尚何僭紊之有哉？昔孟子舉三王之事，以律五霸之罪，謂夫古者王章克正，侯度聿脩，威福之柄不移，征伐之權亦異。是故畿方千里，提封萬國，天子也。其勢雖有常尊矣，然政典所專，則天討焉。蓋四方之國有方命而不恭者，刑固當脩也。於焉發六師之號，申九伐之灋，命彼方伯，帥群后而底天罰；嚴簡書之譴，重推轂之威，詔彼連帥，徵有眾而致邦禁。將見王威所向，足以畏大而懷小，何嘗親用黃鉞，御戎行而制攻取耶？赫怒所震，足以推亡而固存，何嘗躬屬櫜鞬，濟貪忿而夸武
translation_en:
…Mencius’s intent to honor true kings and disparage hegemons comes through beyond the words themselves. The composition is also forceful and orderly; strength of expression and depth of learning are very well matched. Its inclusion here does more than merely display your talent.
Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: “The language is stern and the principles correct: this is writing in the manner of Mencius. Include it.”
Examiner Fang, an Instructor, comments: “Wherever the reasoning reaches, the force of the language reaches too. A true writer! A true writer!”
The sovereign issues the command to employ armies; the assembled lords obey that command. For the direction of armies is a great affair of state. When commands issue from above and are obeyed below, what usurpation or disorder can there be? In former times Mencius cited the deeds of the Three Kings to judge the crimes of the Five Hegemons. His meaning was that, in antiquity, royal statutes were properly established and the rules governing the feudal lords duly observed. The power to punish and reward did not pass into other hands, and authority over military expeditions was likewise differentiated.
Thus, the one whose royal domain extended a thousand li on each side and whose territorial bounds encompassed the myriad states was the Son of Heaven. Although his position possessed an enduring supremacy, what the institutions of government reserved exclusively to him was punishment on Heaven’s behalf. If any state in the four quarters defied his commands and failed in respect, punitive measures certainly had to be enforced. He would therefore issue orders to the Six Armies and proclaim the statutes governing the nine grounds for punitive expeditions, commanding the regional chief to lead the assembled lords in inflicting Heaven’s punishment. He would make stern the reprimands conveyed in written commands and lend weight to the authority conferred when dispatching a commander, ordering the chief of a league of states to levy troops and enforce the realm’s prohibitions. Wherever royal authority was directed, it would suffice to overawe the great states and win over the small. When did he ever personally wield the yellow battle-axe, lead the ranks, and direct assaults and conquests? The shock of his blazing anger would suffice to overthrow those destined to perish and secure those entitled to survive. When did he ever personally strap on bow-case and quiver, indulge greed and wrath, and boast of martial…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
功耶列爵惟五分土惟三諸侯也其守雖有常
度矣然夙夜所謹則王命焉蓋天子之所有越
志而衡行者兵固當加也於焉竭股肱之力整
卒乗之雄聲其不率之罪陳之原而肆之市同
兄弟之邦受馳驅之役歸以不恪之曲誅其君
而弔其民將見奉辭而往惟武服之是共曷敢
不稟於王假義以干國紀耶銜命而行惟師律
之是正曷敢不由其上矯制以亂天綱耶是則
天子專討則畿兵不外出而威已行諸侯致伐
===
則敵國不相征而分自定五霸之師顧不出此
其僭侈之罪大矣抑嘗觀夫子之言曰天下有
道則禮樂征伐自天子出故羲和之征史臣善
之桓公伐楚春秋譏焉聖賢傳心之法如此夫
何淮北之師美宣王之自將彤弓之錫許臣子
之專征哉噫是又可以觀聖人立教之經馭世
之權矣蓋非姬運之中衰夷狄之篡弑則淮北
幾何而不為勤遠略而彤弓不至於竊主威耶
此有天下者所以當守經而行權也
punctuated:
功耶？列爵惟五，分土惟三，諸侯也。其守雖有常度矣，然夙夜所謹則王命焉。蓋天子之所有越志而衡行者，兵固當加也。於焉竭股肱之力，整卒乗之雄，聲其不率之罪，陳之原而肆之市；同兄弟之邦，受馳驅之役，歸以不恪之曲，誅其君而弔其民。將見奉辭而往，惟武服之是共，曷敢不稟於王，假義以干國紀耶？銜命而行，惟師律之是正，曷敢不由其上，矯制以亂天綱耶？是則天子專討，則畿兵不外出而威已行；諸侯致伐，則敵國不相征而分自定。五霸之師顧不出此，其僭侈之罪大矣！

抑嘗觀夫子之言曰：「天下有道，則禮樂征伐自天子出。」故羲和之征，史臣善之；桓公伐楚，春秋譏焉。聖賢傳心之法如此，夫何淮北之師美宣王之自將，彤弓之錫許臣子之專征哉？噫！是又可以觀聖人立教之經、馭世之權矣。蓋非姬運之中衰、夷狄之篡弑，則淮北幾何而不為勤遠略，而彤弓不至於竊主威耶？此有天下者所以當守經而行權也。
translation_en:
…military achievements? Those whose ranks number five and whose territorial allotments fall into three grades are the feudal lords. Although their responsibilities have fixed bounds, what they must heed morning and night is the king’s command. For when, within the Son of Heaven’s domain, there are those whose ambitions overstep their station and whose conduct is lawless, armed force must indeed be brought against them. The lords then exert their strength as his supporting limbs, marshal their formidable troops and chariots, proclaim the offenders’ crime of disobedience, array them on the plain and expose their bodies in the marketplace. Together with their brother states, they undertake the service of campaigning, lay the blame for irreverence upon the offenders, execute their rulers, and console their people. Thus, proceeding under an express charge, they devote themselves solely to performing their military duties. How would they dare act without reporting to the king, invoking righteousness as a pretext for violating the order of the realm? Bearing his command, they concern themselves solely with maintaining military discipline. How would they dare bypass their superior and falsify royal commands to disrupt Heaven’s order? Thus, when the Son of Heaven holds sole authority for punitive expeditions, his authority takes effect even without troops leaving the royal domain; when the feudal lords carry out those expeditions, states of equal standing do not attack one another, and their respective stations are settled of themselves. Yet the armies of the Five Hegemons did not proceed on this basis: grave indeed was their offense of usurpation and presumption!

Moreover, I have considered the Master’s words: “When the Way prevails under Heaven, rites, music, and punitive expeditions issue from the Son of Heaven.” Thus the historian approved the expedition against Xi and He, whereas the Spring and Autumn Annals censured Duke Huan’s attack on Chu. Such is the method by which sages and worthies transmit their understanding. Why, then, does the account of the campaign north of the Huai praise King Xuan for commanding in person, while the bestowal of the vermilion bow permits a subject to conduct expeditions on his own authority? Ah! Here too we may discern the constant principles by which the sages establish their teachings and the discretionary measures by which they govern the world. Had it not been for the decline of the Ji royal house and the usurpations and regicides of the Yi and Di peoples, how could the campaign north of the Huai have escaped being an exertion for distant conquest, and the vermilion bow have avoided becoming a means of appropriating the sovereign’s authority? This is why one who possesses all under Heaven must uphold constant principles while exercising discretion.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
易
忠信所以進德也脩辭立其誠所以居業
也知至至之可與幾也知終終之可與
存義也
楊琇
同考試官教諭常批此題士子類能言之到幾
義處便鶻突可厭此作挑剔明白錄之
考試官教諭周批易義明暢宜錄
考試官教諭方批詞不費而意盡佳作
===
文言詳君子進脩之學所以發其憂勤之故也
蓋進德脩業九三為學之事也則夫終日乾乾
者非以此耶想其意謂夫九三君子身雖處乎
危地心惟務乎進脩是故內焉不誠則德无途
而可進忠信其進德之基也必其主於心者念
念誠一而天命之懿以全肫肫真實而无妄之
本以立則得於心者有不自知其益而高明之
域可造矣外焉不誠則業无地而可居脩辭立
誠其居業之地也必其見於事者言辭脩省而
punctuated:
易

忠信所以進德也，脩辭立其誠所以居業也。知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。

楊琇

同考試官教諭常批：「此題士子類能言之，到幾義處便鶻突可厭。此作挑剔明白，錄之。」

考試官教諭周批：「易義明暢，宜錄。」

考試官教諭方批：「詞不費而意盡，佳作。」

文言詳君子進脩之學，所以發其憂勤之故也。蓋進德脩業，九三為學之事也，則夫終日乾乾者，非以此耶？想其意謂夫九三君子，身雖處乎危地，心惟務乎進脩。是故內焉不誠，則德无途而可進，忠信其進德之基也。必其主於心者，念念誠一，而天命之懿以全；肫肫真實，而无妄之本以立。則得於心者，有不自知其益，而高明之域可造矣。外焉不誠，則業无地而可居，脩辭立誠其居業之地也。必其見於事者，言辭脩省而

Book of Changes

“Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue; refining one’s words and establishing one’s sincerity are the means of abiding in one’s work. Knowing where to arrive and arriving there, one may participate in the incipient workings of things; knowing where to end and ending there, one may preserve righteousness.”

Yang Xiu

Associate Examiner Chang, Instructor, comments: “Candidates generally can discuss this topic, but when they reach the points concerning incipient workings and righteousness, they become muddled to an irritating degree. This composition distinguishes and elucidates them clearly. Include it.”

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of the Changes is explained clearly and fluently. It deserves inclusion.”

Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “Without wasting words, it fully conveys its meaning. An excellent composition.”

The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the noble man’s learning in moral advancement and cultivation, thereby revealing the reason for his concern and diligence. Advancing virtue and cultivating one’s work are the tasks of learning at the third yang line. Is this not why he is ‘actively striving throughout the day’? We may understand its meaning thus: although the noble man at the third yang line occupies a perilous position, his heart is devoted solely to advancement and cultivation. Thus, if there is no sincerity within, virtue has no path by which to advance: loyalty and trustworthiness are the foundation for advancing virtue. What governs his heart must be sincere and undivided in every thought, so that the excellence conferred by Heaven’s mandate is preserved intact; it must be earnest and true, so that the foundation of freedom from falsehood is established. Then what he has attained in his heart will increase without his being aware of it, and he can reach the realm of loftiness and illumination. If there is no sincerity in outward conduct, his work has no ground on which to rest: refining words and establishing sincerity provide the ground for abiding in his work. In what is manifested in affairs, he must refine and examine his words, and …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
本然之誠是立樞機謹擇而固有之真是存則
見於事者有不自知其積而廣大之境可入矣
夫忠信固所以進德然何如而見其德之進耶
蓋理得於心至善而无惡者謂之至至乃幾之
所在也真知為吾所當止之處內主忠信以至
之是行雖未至而知有所先則於至之所在而
為幾之所在者可與知之而不昧矣德有不進
者歟脩辭立誠固所以居業抑何如而見其業
之居耶蓋理見於事至當而歸一者謂之終終
===
乃義之所在也灼見為吾所終止之方脩辭立
誠以終之是知已在先而行復克副則於終之
所在而為義之所在者可與存之而不失矣業
有不居者歟是則進德者心也內也脩業者事
也外也九三君子之學內外兩進此所以終日
乾乾而无咎者豈易得哉大抵憂所當憂而卒
於无憂懼所當懼而卒於无懼此理之必然者
九三君子聖人之德備矣今一處乎危地且進
脩惕厲以求无過若是其勤也世有一善不聞
punctuated:
本然之誠是立，樞機謹擇而固有之真是存，則見於事者有不自知其積，而廣大之境可入矣。夫忠信固所以進德，然何如而見其德之進耶？蓋理得於心，至善而无惡者謂之至，至乃幾之所在也。真知為吾所當止之處，內主忠信以至之，是行雖未至而知有所先，則於至之所在而為幾之所在者，可與知之而不昧矣。德有不進者歟？脩辭立誠固所以居業，抑何如而見其業之居耶？蓋理見於事，至當而歸一者謂之終，終乃義之所在也。灼見為吾所終止之方，脩辭立誠以終之，是知已在先而行復克副，則於終之所在而為義之所在者，可與存之而不失矣。業有不居者歟？是則進德者，心也，內也；脩業者，事也，外也。九三君子之學，內外兩進，此所以終日乾乾而无咎者，豈易得哉！
大抵憂所當憂而卒於无憂，懼所當懼而卒於无懼，此理之必然者。九三君子，聖人之德備矣。今一處乎危地，且進脩惕厲以求无過，若是其勤也。世有一善不聞
translation_en:
…innate sincerity is thereby established; through careful discrimination in speech, the pivot of action, one’s inherent genuineness is preserved. Thus what manifests in affairs accumulates without one’s being aware of it, and the realm of breadth and greatness can be entered. Loyalty and trustworthiness are certainly the means of advancing virtue; but how does one see that virtue has advanced? Principle apprehended in the heart, supremely good and without evil, is called the utmost attainment. This attainment is where the incipient springs of action lie. Truly recognizing it as the place where one ought to abide, one inwardly makes loyalty and trustworthiness one’s guide in reaching it. Although practice has not yet arrived there, understanding has gone ahead. Thus one can discern without obscurity those incipient springs of action that lie at the point of utmost attainment. How could virtue fail to advance? Refining one’s words and establishing sincerity are certainly the means of securing one’s achievements; but how does one see that those achievements are secure? Principle manifested in affairs, perfectly fitting and converging upon unity, is called completion. Completion is where rightness lies. Clearly discerning it as the direction in which one must ultimately come to rest, one refines one’s words and establishes sincerity to bring it to completion. Understanding has already gone ahead, and practice can in turn measure up to it. Thus one can preserve without loss the rightness that lies at the point of completion. How could one’s achievements fail to be secure? Advancing virtue, then, concerns the heart and what is internal; cultivating one’s achievements concerns affairs and what is external. In the learning of the gentleman represented by the Nine in the Third Place, the internal and external advance together. This is how he remains unceasingly diligent throughout the day and incurs no blame. How could this be easily attained!
In general, by worrying about what ought to cause worry, one ultimately becomes free of worry; by fearing what ought to cause fear, one ultimately becomes free of fear. This necessarily follows from principle. The gentleman of the Nine in the Third Place possesses the virtues of a sage in full. Yet once placed in dangerous circumstances, he advances his virtue and cultivates his achievements, remaining vigilant and wary in his effort to avoid error. Such is his diligence. There are those in the world who have not heard a single good teaching…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而冥行无忌者欲其不陷於危難矣哉噫其亦
不占者也
歸竒於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛
劉廷叙
同考試官教諭常批此題上閏字已兼兩閏言
五歲再閏不過明再扐後掛之義是篇體認親切錄之
考試官教諭周批潔淨精微可與言易矣
考試官教諭方批說理之文煞有珎潤理學也
===
大傳論筮法歸餘有所合再變有所始也甚矣
筮法之妙也歸餘所合再變所始非大傳指而
言之抑何以知其然哉昔聖人之意謂夫大衍
之數出於河圖然其為用各有所合是故虚一
分二之餘掛一揲四之後左手之策不能无竒
也或一二或三四歸而扐於左手第三第四指
之間扐之蓋有定所焉右手之策不能不餘也
或一二或三四歸而扐於左手第二第三指之
間歸之蓋有定在焉歸竒於扐如此蓋掛一揲
punctuated:
而冥行无忌者，欲其不陷於危難矣哉？噫，其亦不占者也！

歸竒於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。

劉廷叙

同考試官教諭常批：此題上「閏」字已兼兩閏言，「五歲再閏」不過明再扐後掛之義。是篇體認親切，錄之。

考試官教諭周批：潔淨精微，可與言易矣。

考試官教諭方批：說理之文，煞有珎潤，理學也。

大傳論筮法，歸餘有所合，再變有所始也。甚矣，筮法之妙也！歸餘所合，再變所始，非大傳指而言之，抑何以知其然哉？昔聖人之意，謂夫大衍之數出於河圖，然其為用，各有所合。是故虚一分二之餘，掛一揲四之後，左手之策不能无竒也，或一二，或三四，歸而扐於左手第三第四指之間，扐之蓋有定所焉。右手之策不能不餘也，或一二，或三四，歸而扐於左手第二第三指之間，歸之蓋有定在焉。歸竒於扐如此，蓋掛一揲

…yet those who proceed blindly, without restraint—can one expect them not to fall into peril and distress? Alas, they too are people who do not consult the Changes!

“Place the remainder between the fingers to represent an intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalations; therefore, place remainders between the fingers twice before hanging a stalk again.”

Liu Tingxu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chang, Instructor: The first occurrence of “intercalation” in this topic already encompasses both intercalations. “In five years there are two intercalations” merely explains why one places remainders between the fingers twice before hanging a stalk again. This essay shows an intimate grasp of the meaning; I have selected it for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Pure and lucid, subtle and precise: this is someone with whom one can discuss the Changes.

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: An essay that expounds principle, with considerable precious lustre [?]; this is the learning of principle.

In discussing the method of milfoil divination, the Great Commentary explains that putting aside the remainders has its correspondence, and that a renewed transformation has its starting point. How wondrous is the method of milfoil divination! Had the Great Commentary not explicitly explained what putting aside the remainders corresponds to, and where a renewed transformation begins, how could we know why these procedures are so?

The intention of the sages of old was that the number of the Great Expansion derives from the River Chart, but that each operation in its use has its correspondence. Thus, after setting one stalk aside and dividing the rest into two groups, then hanging one stalk and counting by fours, the stalks in the left hand necessarily have a remainder: either one or two, or three or four. These are gathered and lodged between the third and fourth fingers of the left hand; there is a fixed place for lodging them. The stalks in the right hand likewise necessarily have a remainder: either one or two, or three or four. These are gathered and lodged between the second and third fingers of the left hand; there is a fixed place for putting them. Such is the procedure for placing the remainder between the fingers. For hanging one stalk and counting…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
左扐左象夫三歲積盈虛之餘日分而為一閏
也揲右扐右象夫五歲積盈虛之餘日合而為
再閏也所謂歸餘有所合者如此然筮法再扐
後掛者何耶蓋曆法五歲之間旣積餘以一閏
復積餘以再閏矣然後别起積分故揲蓍之法
左右之策旣各一揲而一扐矣于是别起掛一
以為後變之始求卦之方旣四揲左右之策而
歸竒矣于焉别起一掛以為後變之端九變而
成三畫雖曰得乎內卦也其間凡有再扐者莫
===
不皆然否則蓍策无窮其變未終何以前萬民
之用哉十有八變成卦雖曰得乎全體也其中
凡有再扐者罔不皆爾否則蓍數无端其變未
竟何以决斯世之疑哉所謂再變有所始者如
此是則曆法難知也而策法與之合筮法至妙
也而曆法與之準大傳聖人闡之以告人得无
意歟抑論之聖人幽贊於神明而生蓍參天兩
地而倚數筮法之立豈但象閏而已耶觀其分
二以象兩儀掛一以象三才揲四以象四時何
punctuated: 左扐左，象夫三歲積盈虛之餘日，分而為一閏也；揲右扐右，象夫五歲積盈虛之餘日，合而為再閏也。所謂歸餘有所合者如此。然筮法再扐後掛者何耶？蓋曆法五歲之間，旣積餘以一閏，復積餘以再閏矣，然後别起積分。故揲蓍之法，左右之策旣各一揲而一扐矣，于是别起掛一，以為後變之始。求卦之方，旣四揲左右之策而歸竒矣，于焉别起一掛，以為後變之端。九變而成三畫，雖曰得乎內卦也，其間凡有再扐者，莫不皆然。否則蓍策无窮，其變未終，何以前萬民之用哉？十有八變成卦，雖曰得乎全體也，其中凡有再扐者，罔不皆爾。否則蓍數无端，其變未竟，何以决斯世之疑哉？所謂再變有所始者如此。是則曆法難知也，而策法與之合；筮法至妙也，而曆法與之準。大傳聖人闡之以告人，得无意歟？抑論之，聖人幽贊於神明而生蓍，參天兩地而倚數，筮法之立豈但象閏而已耶？觀其分二以象兩儀，掛一以象三才，揲四以象四時，何
translation_en:
…counting the left-hand stalks and lodging their remainder between the fingers symbolizes the surplus days accumulated through the excesses and deficiencies over three years, set apart to make one intercalary month. Counting the right-hand stalks and lodging their remainder symbolizes the surplus days accumulated through the excesses and deficiencies over five years, combined to make a second intercalary month. This is what is meant by saying that gathering the remainders has its corresponding principle.

But why does the divination procedure prescribe setting aside a stalk after lodging the remainders twice? In calendrical reckoning, within five years the accumulated surplus has already produced one intercalary month, and a further accumulation has produced a second. Only then does the accumulation of fractional days begin anew. Thus, in the procedure for counting yarrow stalks, once the stalks on the left and right have each been counted and their remainders lodged, one begins anew by setting aside a single stalk, thereby initiating the next transformation. In the method for obtaining a hexagram, once the stalks on the left and right have been counted in fours and the remainders gathered, one again sets aside a single stalk to begin the next transformation.

Nine transformations produce three lines. Although this yields the inner trigram, every instance of lodging the remainders twice within this process follows the same rule. Otherwise, the manipulation of the yarrow stalks would continue without limit and their transformations would never reach completion: how could they guide the practical affairs of the myriad people? Eighteen transformations produce a hexagram. Although this yields the complete figure, every instance of lodging the remainders twice within it likewise follows this rule. Otherwise, the reckoning of the yarrow stalks would have no definite beginning and their transformations would never be completed: how could they resolve the doubts of the world? This is what is meant by saying that the next transformation has its point of commencement.

Thus, although calendrical reckoning is difficult to understand, the procedure with the stalks accords with it; although divination is supremely subtle, calendrical reckoning provides its counterpart. Could the sage have had no purpose in elucidating this in the Great Commentary to instruct others? To consider the matter further: the sage, mysteriously assisting the spiritual powers, brought forth the use of yarrow stalks; assigning three to Heaven and two to Earth, he established the numbers upon this basis. Could the institution of divination have served merely to symbolize intercalation? Consider how dividing the stalks into two symbolizes the Two Modes, Heaven and Earth; setting aside one symbolizes the Three Powers, Heaven, Earth, and humanity; and counting in fours symbolizes the four seasons. What…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者不寓於其間哉噫天生神物非聖人制而用
之不過植物之流耳甚何以通天下之志定天
下之業斷天下之疑哉嗚呼聖人之功大矣
書
惟德動天無遠弗屆滿招損謙受益時乃
天道帝初于歷山往于田日號泣于旻
天于父母負罪引慝祗載見瞽瞍夔夔

戴希顥
===

大臣歷著遠人有可感之理所以贊相臣之脩
德也甚矣德之無所不感也然則遠人未化亦
