text:
其成必關
內閣亦如周之六卿分職以倡九牧而冢宰
實掌邦治焉其大要合於周制者蓋在此
矣自周而降若漢之規模略定于三章唐
之儀式僅頒乎六典會要作於宋而光嶽
弗完經世紀於元而彞倫斯斁擬諸會典
不可同日而語明矣至於制異墳典者蓋
謂欲宜於今而不泥於古法殊紀傳者蓋
謂叙其事而不錄其名體有所重故事雖
===
微而必錄義可以訓故令雖寢而必書文
字之間盡用行移之語而不少潤飾者蓋
將使山谷田野之民易於誦習而便於遵
守然耳嗚呼天地之道所以博厚高明者
由其為物不貳我
祖宗之制作所以光前裕後者本乎
聖德之至誠自洪武以至于今百六十年間天
下一統而無敝者其本端在于此愚也不
識不知順帝之則而已蕪詞不足以復明
punctuated:
其成必關內閣，亦如周之六卿分職以倡九牧，而冢宰實掌邦治焉。其大要合於周制者，蓋在此矣。自周而降，若漢之規模略定于三章，唐之儀式僅頒乎六典，會要作於宋而光嶽弗完，經世紀於元而彞倫斯斁，擬諸會典，不可同日而語明矣。至於制異墳典者，蓋謂欲宜於今而不泥於古；法殊紀傳者，蓋謂叙其事而不錄其名。體有所重，故事雖微而必錄；義可以訓，故令雖寢而必書。文字之間，盡用行移之語而不少潤飾者，蓋將使山谷田野之民易於誦習而便於遵守，然耳。
嗚呼！天地之道所以博厚高明者，由其為物不貳。我祖宗之制作所以光前裕後者，本乎聖德之至誠。自洪武以至于今，百六十年間，天下一統而無敝者，其本端在于此。愚也不識不知，順帝之則而已。蕪詞不足以復明
translation_en:
…the completion of their business must involve the Grand Secretariat. This is likewise comparable to the Zhou arrangement, in which the six ministers divided their duties to lead the nine regional governors, while the Grand Steward held actual responsibility for governing the realm. Here, surely, lies its essential conformity with the institutions of Zhou. After Zhou, the broad framework of Han government was roughly established in the Three Articles, while Tang administrative forms were promulgated only in the Six Canons. The Collected Essentials were compiled under the Song, yet the realm was not territorially whole; the institutions for Ordering the World were recorded under the Yuan, yet the enduring moral relationships had fallen into disorder. Clearly, these cannot be spoken of in the same breath as the Collected Statutes. As for its organization differing from the ancient canonical writings, this means that it seeks suitability for the present without clinging to antiquity. As for its method differing from annals and biographies, this means that it relates the affairs rather than recording the names of those involved. Because its organizing principles give weight to certain matters, even minor affairs must be recorded; because their significance can provide instruction, even orders no longer in force must be written down. Its wording uses throughout the language of official correspondence, without the slightest embellishment, simply so that people in mountain valleys and the countryside may easily recite and study it and conveniently observe its provisions.
Ah! The Way of Heaven and Earth is broad and substantial, lofty and luminous, because its operation is undivided. The institutions established by our imperial ancestors bring glory to their predecessors and abundant provision to posterity because they are rooted in the utmost sincerity of their sagely virtue. From the Hongwu reign down to the present, throughout a hundred and sixty years, the realm has remained united without falling into decay: its fundamental basis lies precisely here. Ignorant as I am, without conscious understanding or knowledge, I merely follow the Supreme Ruler’s standards. These uncultivated words are insufficient to answer your enlightened…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
問惟進教之幸甚
第二問
唐昫
同考試官教諭李批三場勻稱儒業一策上
下古今出入子史而評論明當末復重於所養非窹
然有識者不能如此且反覆辨鬱而筆力愈健几近
者殆未可窺其際也表而出之用勵多士
考試官教諭周批策場所以觀士之閎博
此篇故實不遺而品藻精當且辭氣整贍若有未盡
其才者得士如此可稱賢科矣
===
考試官教諭方批策目淺易答者類見其
難此卷能答所問而文且典重豈亦有德者之言乎
對儒有鳴世盛而垂世遠必本諸中者深
而發乎外者宏矣德也功也言也所以鳴
世即所以垂世也是故德而不一非純德
也功而不正非崇功也言而不經非通言
也真儒無不純之德不崇之功不通之言
也上而兼焉次而各舉其盛焉後世猶有
punctuated:
問，惟進教之幸甚。
第二問
唐昫
同考試官教諭李批：三場勻稱。儒業一策，上下古今，出入子史，而評論明當，末復重於所養。非窹然有識者，不能如此。且反覆辨鬱，而筆力愈健，几近者殆未可窺其際也。表而出之，用勵多士。
考試官教諭周批：策場所以觀士之閎博。此篇故實不遺，而品藻精當，且辭氣整贍，若有未盡其才者。得士如此，可稱賢科矣。
考試官教諭方批：策目淺易，答者類見其難。此卷能答所問，而文且典重，豈亦有德者之言乎？
對：儒有鳴世盛而垂世遠，必本諸中者深，而發乎外者宏矣。德也，功也，言也，所以鳴世，即所以垂世也。是故德而不一，非純德也；功而不正，非崇功也；言而不經，非通言也。真儒無不純之德、不崇之功、不通之言也。上而兼焉，次而各舉其盛焉，後世猶有
translation_en:
…question. I would be most fortunate to receive further instruction.

Second policy question
Tang Xu

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: His work is well balanced across all three sessions. His policy essay on Confucian learning ranges through ancient and modern times, drawing freely upon the philosophical masters and histories; its judgments are clear and apt. At the end he returns to emphasize personal cultivation. Only someone possessing awakened understanding [?] could accomplish this. Moreover, he repeatedly elucidates tangled matters [?], while his writing grows ever more vigorous. Those who come close [?] may still be unable to discern the full extent of his achievement. We single out and publish this essay to encourage the many scholars.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The policy-essay session serves to reveal the breadth of a scholar’s learning. This essay overlooks no historical precedents, and its assessments are precise and appropriate. Its language, moreover, is orderly and ample, as though the author had yet to exhaust his abilities. An examination that obtains scholars like this may be called a worthy examination indeed.

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: Although the policy questions are straightforward and easy, those answering them generally find them difficult. This script answers what was asked, and its writing is also classical and dignified. Could these, too, be the words of a man of virtue?

Response: When a Confucian scholar wins great renown in his own age and leaves an enduring legacy to later ages, what is rooted within him must be profound, and what issues outward must be expansive. Virtue, achievement, and words—the means by which he wins renown in his own age are precisely those by which he leaves a legacy to later ages. Thus virtue that lacks constancy is not pure virtue; achievement that is not upright is not exalted achievement; words that do not accord with enduring standards are not words of universal validity. A true Confucian has no virtue that is impure, no achievement that is unexalted, and no words that lack universal validity. Those of the highest order unite all three; those of the next order each display their particular excellence. In later ages there have still been…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
矣焉可也德不足而求之功功不足而求
之言抑淺爾噫天下微全人而君子有定
論矣夫德由身脩而大小分功由時建而
邪正形言由道考而醇駁判裒小而成大
去邪而就正袪駁而歸之醇吾以是觀其
養矣執事者于德于功于言皆屬舉而詢
焉愚有以知君子嘅世之深意矣且忠如
屈原朱子以為過直如汲黯楊氏疑其褊
廉如時苗元世祖乃斥其矯約如王安石
===
蘇洵乃辯其姦蓋嘗眩於其迹至於自湛
其身與淮南寢謀之事夫然後知過之者
乃所以許之疑之者乃所以信之而似德
之害者固不容巳於辯且斥耳義如張巡
未免流俗之毀斷如宼準卒來孤注之喻
勇如李靖而東坡譏其失才如姚崇而穎
濱病其非蓋嘗惑於其說至於敘全天下
之半與親扶日轂之事夫然後知温公之
論一出於至公欽若之讒不失為壬儉而
punctuated: 矣，焉可也？德不足而求之功，功不足而求之言，抑淺爾。噫！天下微全人，而君子有定論矣。夫德由身脩而大小分，功由時建而邪正形，言由道考而醇駁判。裒小而成大，去邪而就正，袪駁而歸之醇，吾以是觀其養矣。執事者于德、于功、于言，皆屬舉而詢焉，愚有以知君子嘅世之深意矣。且忠如屈原，朱子以為過；直如汲黯，楊氏疑其褊；廉如時苗，元世祖乃斥其矯；約如王安石，蘇洵乃辯其姦。蓋嘗眩於其迹，至於自湛其身與淮南寢謀之事，夫然後知過之者乃所以許之，疑之者乃所以信之，而似德之害者固不容巳於辯且斥耳。義如張巡，未免流俗之毀；斷如宼準，卒來孤注之喻；勇如李靖，而東坡譏其失；才如姚崇，而穎濱病其非。蓋嘗惑於其說，至於敘全天下之半與親扶日轂之事，夫然後知温公之論一出於至公，欽若之讒不失為壬儉，而
translation_en:
…how could that be acceptable? To seek achievement when virtue is insufficient, and to seek distinction in words when achievement is insufficient, is shallow indeed. Alas! The world lacks wholly accomplished men, yet the gentleman has settled standards of judgment. Virtue is distinguished as great or small through the cultivation of the self; achievement reveals itself as perverse or upright as it is established in the circumstances of the time; words are judged pure or mixed by testing them against the Way. Accumulating what is small to make it great, rejecting perversity to approach uprightness, and eliminating impurities to attain purity: by these means I assess a person's cultivation. You, honored examiners, have brought virtue, achievement, and words together in your question. Thus I, in my ignorance, can perceive the profound concern for the age that lies behind your inquiry.
Even with loyalty such as Qu Yuan's, Master Zhu considered it excessive; with frankness such as Ji An's, Master Yang suspected narrow-mindedness; with incorruptibility such as Shi Miao's, Emperor Shizu of the Yuan denounced affectation; and with frugality such as Wang Anshi's, Su Xun exposed treachery. One may initially be bewildered by their outward conduct. Only upon considering such events as Qu Yuan's drowning himself and the abandonment of the Prince of Huainan's conspiracy does one understand that censuring the former's excess was a means of acknowledging his worth, and questioning the latter was a means of affirming him. As for the harm done by counterfeit virtue, one certainly cannot refrain from exposing and denouncing it.
Righteousness such as Zhang Xun's did not escape vulgar slander; decisiveness such as Kou Zhun's ultimately invited the comparison to staking everything on a single throw; despite Li Jing's courage, Dongpo criticized his failings; and despite Yao Chong's talent, Yingbin found fault with his wrongdoing. One may initially be confused by these judgments. Only upon considering the accounts of preserving half the realm and personally supporting the imperial chariot does one understand that the judgment of the Duke of Wen proceeded entirely from the utmost impartiality, while Qinruo's slander remained the work of a treacherous flatterer [?], and…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
逢君之惡者亦不容已於譏且病耳若夫
董仲舒潜心大業而真氏論其流於災異
揚子雲博極群書而程子貶其首撰美新
王褒著僮約而顏氏示戒韓愈頌聖德而
子由鄙焉夫以仲舒承秦滅學之後六經
離析之餘賢良之策度越諸子其推陰陽
錯行之故蓋有得乎春秋災異之變視雄
承諛之語可並觀耶昌黎文起八代之衰
道濟天下之溺泰山北斗學者依歸其警
===
藩鎮叛逆之意蓋脗合乎風雅勸懲之旨
視王襃之文可例論耶執此以往則先
正之取舍後賢之定論可具見矣雖然有
三義焉蓋自其一者而論之必德盛者業
可大而言可法也自其分者而言之蘊之
為德發之為功為言也自其脩於人者言
之天質之美固不足以勝其涵養之力也
是以原之忠鯁之直張之烈冠之斷董之
學得本原韓之佐佑六經皆有端厚以為
punctuated:
逢君之惡者，亦不容已於譏且病耳。若夫董仲舒潜心大業，而真氏論其流於災異；揚子雲博極群書，而程子貶其首撰美新；王褒著僮約，而顏氏示戒；韓愈頌聖德，而子由鄙焉。夫以仲舒承秦滅學之後、六經離析之餘，賢良之策度越諸子，其推陰陽錯行之故，蓋有得乎春秋災異之變，視雄承諛之語，可並觀耶？昌黎文起八代之衰，道濟天下之溺，泰山北斗，學者依歸。其警藩鎮叛逆之意，蓋脗合乎風雅勸懲之旨，視王襃之文，可例論耶？執此以往，則先正之取舍、後賢之定論，可具見矣。
雖然，有三義焉。蓋自其一者而論之，必德盛者，業可大而言可法也；自其分者而言之，蘊之為德，發之為功、為言也；自其脩於人者言之，天質之美，固不足以勝其涵養之力也。是以原之忠、鯁之直、張之烈、冠之斷、董之學得本原、韓之佐佑六經，皆有端厚以為
translation_en:
…those who indulge their ruler’s wickedness likewise cannot be spared criticism and censure. Consider Dong Zhongshu, who devoted himself to the great undertaking of learning, yet whom Master Zhen criticized for straying into the study of calamities and anomalies; Yang Ziyun, whose learning encompassed the full range of books, yet whom Master Cheng disparaged for taking the lead in composing In Praise of the New Dynasty; Wang Bao, who wrote A Contract with a Servant, against which Master Yan issued a warning; and Han Yu, who celebrated imperial virtue, yet was scorned by Ziyou.
Dong Zhongshu lived after the Qin destruction of learning, when the Six Classics had been dispersed and fragmented. His policy essays for the examination of the Worthy and Good surpassed the writings of the various masters. His investigation of why yin and yang operate out of order surely grasped something of the anomalous events and calamities recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Can this be placed on the same footing as Yang Xiong’s sycophantic language? Han Yu of Changli revived literary writing after eight dynasties of decline, and through the Way rescued the world from drowning. Like Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper, he was the guide upon whom scholars relied. His intention of warning against rebellion by the regional military commands surely accorded with the purpose of encouragement and admonition in the Airs and Odes. Can his writing be judged in the same category as Wang Bao’s? Proceeding on this basis, one can fully discern both the judgments of earlier worthies and the settled assessments of later sages.
Nevertheless, there are three principles here. Viewed in their unity, only a person abundant in virtue can achieve great things and produce words worthy of emulation. Viewed in their distinctions, what is stored within is virtue; expressed outwardly, it becomes achievement and words. Viewed in terms of personal cultivation, the excellence of one’s natural endowment cannot surpass the power of sustained moral nurture. Thus Yuan’s loyalty [?], Geng’s uprightness [?], Zhang’s heroic resolve, Guan’s decisiveness [?], Dong’s learning that reached the fundamental source, and Han’s support of the Six Classics all had integrity and generosity as their…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之質剛大以為之氣而濟之以雄偉不常
之才考其所立德雖未合乎中庸功則高
視乎一世而其言又有聖人之道賴之以
復明者多矣後之論者猶復云爾何哉蓋
聖賢之學體用一原而存養之密內外兼
致故其德足以動高玄功足以周物務而
其言又足以宣人文而憲萬世自夫道學
不明而人才之成就大抵不能無可論者
要亦非數子之責也然愚竊有憾焉原之
===
怨黜之忿寇之不學韓之好進此君子所
以喜其天質之美而惜其涵養之力也嗚
呼孰謂千載而下而有仲舒之醇正睢陽
之忠義者哉謹對
第三問
楊琇
同考試官教諭常 批 評論古人行事得失乃
學者一項窮理工夫所不可缺然非博極群書不能也
今子於此條答無遺豈非尚友者邪
punctuated:
之質，剛大以為之氣，而濟之以雄偉不常之才。考其所立，德雖未合乎中庸，功則高視乎一世，而其言又有聖人之道賴之以復明者多矣。後之論者猶復云爾，何哉？蓋聖賢之學，體用一原，而存養之密，內外兼致，故其德足以動高玄，功足以周物務，而其言又足以宣人文而憲萬世。自夫道學不明，而人才之成就，大抵不能無可論者，要亦非數子之責也。然愚竊有憾焉：原之怨黜之忿，寇之不學，韓之好進，此君子所以喜其天質之美，而惜其涵養之力也。嗚呼！孰謂千載而下，而有仲舒之醇正、睢陽之忠義者哉！謹對。
第三問
楊琇
同考試官教諭常批：評論古人行事得失，乃學者一項窮理工夫所不可缺，然非博極群書不能也。今子於此條答無遺，豈非尚友者邪？
translation_en:
…as their essential character, with firmness and greatness as their vital spirit, supplemented by extraordinary and imposing talent. Examining what they established, although their virtue did not fully accord with the Mean, their achievements towered above their age; and in many instances their writings enabled the Way of the sages to shine forth again. Why, then, do later critics still speak of them thus? In the learning of sages and worthies, substance and function share a single source, and their meticulous preservation and cultivation of the mind extend fully to both the inward and the outward. Thus their virtue can move high Heaven, their achievements can encompass worldly affairs, and their words can illuminate human culture and serve as a model for countless generations. Since learning concerning the Way became obscured, the attainments of talented men have generally been open to some criticism. Ultimately, these few men cannot alone be held responsible for this. Yet I venture to feel regret: Qu Yuan’s resentment and anger at dismissal [?], Kou’s lack of learning, and Han’s fondness for advancement—these are why the gentleman delights in the beauty of their natural endowments but regrets the inadequacy of their efforts at self-cultivation. Alas! Who would have thought that, a thousand years later, there would be men possessing Zhongshu’s purity and rectitude, or the loyalty and righteousness of Suiyang [Zhang Xun]! Respectfully submitted in reply.
Third Question
Yang Xiu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chang, Instructor: Assessing the successes and failures of the ancients’ conduct is an indispensable part of a student’s work of investigating principle. Yet this cannot be done without extensive mastery of the books. Now you have answered this question point by point, omitting nothing. Are you not one who seeks friendship with the worthies of antiquity?

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭周批觀此一策蓋博學宏辭
之流也健羨健羨
考試官教諭方批叙事詳盡而斷制精明
非若左氏專以成敗論事者矣佳士佳士
不患乎疑事之難决而貴存至公之心不
畏乎衆論之難折而貴操大中之矩蓋公
則不私而天下之猶豫自定中則不偏而
天下之議論自明不私不偏其於衆言之
混淆吾折以本然之則而有餘力尚何狐
===
疑之患哉請因明問而陳之事之交於前
者雖無常形理之具於心者自有定則理
同而事異不害其為同理異而事同適所
以為異慨自嬴秦黷武邯鄲幾傾無忌襲
擊晉鄙以赴平原之急雖非大義而勇於
救患猶或可嘉項籍何為者顧以偏裨之
職矯殺宋義以救新趙而又戕害主帥大
義乖矣陳勝舉事尺土未階張耳勸立六
國以為自固之計雖非公謀而外假虛名
punctuated:
考試官教諭周批：觀此一策，蓋博學宏辭之流也。健羨，健羨！

考試官教諭方批：叙事詳盡，而斷制精明，非若左氏專以成敗論事者矣。佳士，佳士！

不患乎疑事之難决，而貴存至公之心；不畏乎衆論之難折，而貴操大中之矩。蓋公則不私，而天下之猶豫自定；中則不偏，而天下之議論自明。不私不偏，其於衆言之混淆，吾折以本然之則而有餘力，尚何狐疑之患哉？請因明問而陳之。事之交於前者雖無常形，理之具於心者自有定則。理同而事異，不害其為同；理異而事同，適所以為異。慨自嬴秦黷武，邯鄲幾傾，無忌襲擊晉鄙，以赴平原之急。雖非大義，而勇於救患，猶或可嘉。項籍何為者？顧以偏裨之職，矯殺宋義，以救新趙，而又戕害主帥，大義乖矣。陳勝舉事，尺土未階，張耳勸立六國，以為自固之計。雖非公謀，而外假虛名，
translation_en:
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: Reading this policy essay, I place its author among those of broad learning and magnificent literary expression. Admirable, admirable!

Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: His account of events is thorough, and his judgments are discerning. He is unlike Master Zuo, who judges affairs solely by success or failure. A worthy scholar, a worthy scholar!

Rather than worry that doubtful matters are hard to decide, one should prize preserving a wholly impartial mind; rather than fear that contending opinions are hard to adjudicate, one should prize holding to the standard of perfect equilibrium. For impartiality excludes selfishness, and the uncertainties of the world settle themselves; equilibrium excludes bias, and the debates of the world become clear of themselves. Without selfishness or bias, I can adjudicate the confusion of competing claims by the inherent standard of principle, with strength to spare. What cause remains to worry about doubt and hesitation? Allow me to explain in response to your illuminating question.

Although the affairs that confront us have no constant form, the principles inherent in the mind have fixed standards. When the principle is the same but the circumstances differ, their underlying sameness remains intact; when the principle differs but the circumstances are the same, that is precisely what makes them different.

Alas, when Qin under the Ying house recklessly resorted to war and Handan was on the verge of falling, Wuji attacked Jin Bi to hasten to the aid of the Lord of Pingyuan. Although this did not accord with the highest righteousness, his courage in relieving distress might still deserve praise. What, however, was Xiang Ji doing? Holding only a subordinate command, he presumed upon authority to kill Song Yi in order to rescue the newly restored state of Zhao. In murdering his commander-in-chief, he violated the highest righteousness.

When Chen Sheng rose in revolt and had not yet gained even a foot of territory [?], Zhang Er urged him to establish rulers for the Six States as a means of securing his own position. Although this was no plan for the common good, by outwardly borrowing their nominal prestige…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
或能樹黨酈食其何為者乃於垂成之漢
賛立六國以撓楚權是為割地資敵淺謀
甚矣韓信伐趙置背水陣而士卒有死之
心其致勝宜也漢王以惰卒而當强大之
楚於睢水非納侮而何王翦伐楚將六十
萬衆而函谷為虛其成功幸也符堅舉大
衆而寇安輯之晉於淮淝非取敗而何甘
陳矯詔以斬郅支匡衡以為不當封者義
也劉向謂其排妬不免於計利之言薄昭
===
===
恃勢而殺漢使李德裕以為殺之當者正
也温公謂其未然不免於公義之損管仲
不死子糾蓋桓公當立而子糾不當立耳
故孔子與其功若王魏之苟難殊於仲矣
子程子謂其先有罪而後有功不亦當歟
梁悅為父復讎蓋知義不共天而法令不
暇顧耳故昌黎薄其罪元慶之復父讎等
於悅矣陳子昂乃欲誅其人而表其閭不
亦過歟靈州為宋人保障之境不可棄者
punctuated: 或能樹黨。酈食其何為者？乃於垂成之漢，賛立六國以撓楚權，是為割地資敵，淺謀甚矣！韓信伐趙，置背水陣，而士卒有死之心，其致勝宜也。漢王以惰卒而當强大之楚於睢水，非納侮而何？王翦伐楚，將六十萬衆，而函谷為虛，其成功幸也。符堅舉大衆而寇安輯之晉於淮淝，非取敗而何？甘陳矯詔以斬郅支，匡衡以為不當封者，義也；劉向謂其排妬，不免於計利之言。薄昭恃勢而殺漢使，李德裕以為殺之當者，正也；温公謂其未然，不免於公義之損。管仲不死子糾，蓋桓公當立，而子糾不當立耳，故孔子與其功。若王魏之苟難，殊於仲矣。子程子謂其先有罪而後有功，不亦當歟？梁悅為父復讎，蓋知義不共天，而法令不暇顧耳，故昌黎薄其罪。元慶之復父讎，等於悅矣。陳子昂乃欲誅其人而表其閭，不亦過歟？靈州為宋人保障之境，不可棄者
translation_en:
…might perhaps establish a body of supporters. But what was Li Yiji doing? When the Han was on the verge of success, he advocated restoring the Six States to undermine Chu’s power. This amounted to ceding territory to supply the enemy: how shallow a strategy! When Han Xin attacked Zhao, he arrayed his troops with their backs to the river, and his soldiers were resolved to die; it was fitting that he achieved victory. The King of Han, however, confronted mighty Chu at the Sui River with indolent troops. What was this but inviting humiliation? When Wang Jian attacked Chu, he commanded six hundred thousand men, leaving Hangu Pass undefended; his success was fortunate. Fu Jian raised a vast army and invaded the peaceful, well-ordered Jin in the region of the Huai and Fei rivers. What was this but courting defeat?

Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang forged an imperial command to execute Zhizhi. Kuang Heng’s judgment that they should not be enfeoffed accorded with righteousness. Liu Xiang’s claim that his opposition arose from jealousy could not escape the charge of arguing in terms of advantage. Bo Zhao relied on his powerful position and killed a Han envoy. Li Deyu’s judgment that putting him to death was appropriate was correct. Duke Wen’s disagreement could not escape the charge of impairing public righteousness.

Guan Zhong did not die for Prince Jiu because Duke Huan was entitled to succeed, whereas Prince Jiu was not. Thus Confucius approved his achievements. The expedient conduct of Wang Gui and Wei Zheng in adversity [?] was quite different from Guan Zhong’s. Master Cheng said that they were culpable at first but subsequently rendered meritorious service. Was this not an appropriate judgment?

Liang Yue avenged his father because he understood that righteousness forbade him to share the same heaven with his father’s murderer, and he had no time to heed the laws. Thus Han Yu of Changli judged his culpability to be slight. Yuanqing’s vengeance for his father was equivalent to Liang Yue’s. Yet Chen Zi’ang wished to execute him while honoring his neighborhood gate. Was this not mistaken?

Lingzhou was territory that served as a defensive bulwark for the people of Song and could not be abandoned…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也輔臣之言爲是楊億李沆以爲可棄其
殆未之思乎綏州乃敵人戎馬之塲不可
城者也洪湛之言爲非孫全照以爲宜綏
其亦計之熟乎吁群疑滿腹判之在於一
心眾難塞胸折之憑乎一理傳曰權然後
知輕重度然後知長短舍至公之鑑其何
以決天下之疑昧大中之矩又何以斷天
下之務哉雖然評古人之得失將以驗吾
身之得失較往行之是非期以審吾行之
===
是非苟徒觀人而昧反觀察人而忘自察
則亦何益於身心哉末學管窺未知是否
幸執事進而教之
第四問
拱廷臣
同考試官教諭陳 批 聽言信行孔門自有故
步此篇貫串經史品量人物而不失權衡况議論𧮂
博辭氣莊整若德人儼雅色不可犯察子所存殆
非無之而工言者也將信子爲端士矣薦之以華科目
punctuated:
也。輔臣之言爲是，楊億、李沆以爲可棄，其殆未之思乎？綏州乃敵人戎馬之塲，不可城者也。洪湛之言爲非，孫全照以爲宜綏，其亦計之熟乎？吁！群疑滿腹，判之在於一心；眾難塞胸，折之憑乎一理。傳曰：「權然後知輕重，度然後知長短。」舍至公之鑑，其何以決天下之疑？昧大中之矩，又何以斷天下之務哉？雖然，評古人之得失，將以驗吾身之得失；較往行之是非，期以審吾行之是非。苟徒觀人而昧反觀，察人而忘自察，則亦何益於身心哉？末學管窺，未知是否，幸執事進而教之。
第四問
拱廷臣
同考試官教諭陳批：聽言信行，孔門自有故步。此篇貫串經史，品量人物，而不失權衡。况議論𧮂博，辭氣莊整，若德人儼雅，色不可犯。察子所存，殆非無之而工言者也。將信子爲端士矣。薦之以華科目。
translation_en:
…indeed. The chief minister’s statement was correct. Yang Yi and Li Hang considered that it could be abandoned; perhaps they had not thought the matter through? Suizhou was ground traversed by the enemy’s cavalry and should not have been fortified. Hong Zhan’s statement was wrong. Sun Quanzhao considered that it should be pacified [?]; surely he had deliberated thoroughly? Alas! When doubts fill the belly, their resolution rests with a single mind; when difficulties crowd the breast, their settlement depends upon a single principle. The transmitted text says: “Only after weighing do we know what is light or heavy; only after measuring do we know what is long or short.” Without the mirror of utmost impartiality, how could one resolve the doubts of the realm? Ignorant of the standard of perfect centrality, how could one adjudicate the affairs of the realm? Nevertheless, judging the successes and failures of the ancients should serve to test our own successes and failures; comparing right and wrong in past conduct should help us scrutinize right and wrong in our own conduct. If we merely observe others but fail to turn our gaze upon ourselves, scrutinizing others while forgetting self-scrutiny, what benefit is there to our own persons and minds? These are the narrow views of a junior student; I do not know whether they are correct. I hope that you, sir, will advance me through your instruction.
Fourth Question
Gong Tingchen
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: In listening to words and trusting conduct, the school of Confucius has its established precedents. This essay draws together the Classics and histories and appraises individuals without losing its balance of judgment. Moreover, its arguments are expansive [?] and wide-ranging, its language dignified and orderly, like a virtuous man whose solemn elegance and bearing command respect. Examining what you hold within, I judge that you are hardly someone who lacks these qualities yet speaks skillfully of them. I am inclined to trust that you are an upright scholar. I recommend you to bring distinction to the examination.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭周批言行一策正關士習此篇
斂華就實黜通尚儉辭氣舂容而斷制有據世有如
此才宜其穎脫而出矣
考試官敎諭方批五策皆無可疵而言行
一篇尤敻出諸士之右錄之將以喻浮誕者云
對道術正士之言行初無可擇氣習異士
之言行始有所偏天下之事以言而傳將
亦以言而廢以行而立將亦以行而荒蓋
言有切謾而行有夷險也今夫叩鐘鼓而
===
聽其鏗訇天下無異聲由道路而騁夫康
莊天下無異徑人之於言行也亦然節而
後言志而後動則鏗訇之聲徹於外而康
莊之馳將達於天下矣夫惟言必簡而節
始中行至中而志始堅不中乎節不堅乎
志則言固苟言而行亦詖行耳善乎宋儒
之論曰先道而言故無不信之言先義而
行故無不果之行知此然後可與論言行
矣是故聖賢者萬世言行之準也觀夫賛
punctuated:
考試官敎諭周批：言行一策，正關士習。此篇斂華就實，黜通尚儉，辭氣舂容，而斷制有據。世有如此才，宜其穎脫而出矣。

考試官敎諭方批：五策皆無可疵，而言行一篇尤敻出諸士之右。錄之，將以喻浮誕者云。

對：道術正，士之言行初無可擇；氣習異，士之言行始有所偏。天下之事，以言而傳，將亦以言而廢；以行而立，將亦以行而荒。蓋言有切謾，而行有夷險也。今夫叩鐘鼓而聽其鏗訇，天下無異聲；由道路而騁夫康莊，天下無異徑。人之於言行也亦然：節而後言，志而後動，則鏗訇之聲徹於外，而康莊之馳將達於天下矣。夫惟言必簡而節始中，行至中而志始堅。不中乎節，不堅乎志，則言固苟言，而行亦詖行耳。善乎宋儒之論曰：「先道而言，故無不信之言；先義而行，故無不果之行。」知此，然後可與論言行矣。是故聖賢者，萬世言行之準也。觀夫賛
translation_en:
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: This policy essay on speech and conduct bears directly upon the habits of scholars. It restrains ornament and pursues substance, rejects expedient accommodation and esteems restraint. Its language is measured and ample, and its judgments are well grounded. When such talent exists in the world, it deserves to distinguish itself and emerge.

Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: All five policy essays are beyond reproach, but the essay on speech and conduct stands especially far above those of the other candidates. We record it to admonish the frivolous and extravagant.

Answer: When the pursuit of the Way is correct, there is initially nothing to choose between scholars’ speech and conduct; only when their dispositions and habits diverge do their speech and conduct begin to become one-sided. The affairs of the world are transmitted through speech, yet may also be undone through speech; they are established through conduct, yet may also fall into neglect through conduct. For speech may be pertinent or deceptive, and conduct straightforward or treacherous. Strike bells and drums and listen to their resounding notes: throughout the world, their sound is the same. Follow the roads and travel along the broad highways: throughout the world, the paths are the same. So it is with people’s speech and conduct. Exercise restraint before speaking and establish your purpose before acting; then the resounding notes will carry outward, and travel along the broad highways will reach throughout the world. Only when speech is concise does its restraint attain the proper measure; only when conduct attains the mean does one’s purpose become firm. Without proper measure in restraint or firmness of purpose, speech is merely careless speech, and conduct merely perverse conduct.

Excellent is the judgment of the Song Confucians: “Put the Way first when speaking, and no words will fail to be trustworthy; put righteousness first when acting, and no action will fail to be resolute.” Only with this understanding can one discuss speech and conduct. Thus the sages and worthies are the standard for speech and conduct through all ages. Consider how they praise …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
吉人而稱寡辭叙敝俗而病利口語世變
而薄尚通敦操已而重危行至於四方之
使則未嘗以有言棄中庸之道又未嘗以
怪異求何也夫言慎者德崇而誕者風靡
行果者德久而通者詭隨此固言行之大
端也若夫子貢無私叔向所召子產有辭
諸侯賴之柴愚參魯著任高業而狷者不
為亦惟所取焉是言果不可已而通果不
必尚也審爾雖然君子豈樂為是費辭者
===
哉誠以道術不可以不明人心不可以不
正故也大道既隱民訛寢彰柔巽流而為
諛佞貞實散而為夸毗其言行之可觀者
亦其習俗之近古者也蓋嘗求之古人語
默之間而有得乎宇文融之應對辯給周
勃之言若不出王夷甫之詞甚清辯李廣
之終日恂恂嵇康之輕肆直言徐穉之不
答國事矣又嘗稽之古人通檢之迹而有
得乎卓茂之束身自修郗超之任心獨詣
punctuated:
吉人而稱寡辭，叙敝俗而病利口，語世變而薄尚通，敦操已而重危行。至於四方之使，則未嘗以有言棄；中庸之道，又未嘗以怪異求。何也？夫言慎者德崇，而誕者風靡；行果者德久，而通者詭隨。此固言行之大端也。若夫子貢無私，叔向所召；子產有辭，諸侯賴之；柴愚參魯，著任高業，而狷者不為，亦惟所取焉。是言果不可已，而通果不必尚也，審爾。雖然，君子豈樂為是費辭者哉？誠以道術不可以不明，人心不可以不正故也。
大道既隱，民訛寢彰，柔巽流而為諛佞，貞實散而為夸毗。其言行之可觀者，亦其習俗之近古者也。蓋嘗求之古人語默之間，而有得乎宇文融之應對辯給、周勃之言若不出、王夷甫之詞甚清辯、李廣之終日恂恂、嵇康之輕肆直言、徐穉之不答國事矣。又嘗稽之古人通檢之迹，而有得乎卓茂之束身自修、郗超之任心獨詣
translation_en:
…good men are praised for speaking little; in accounts of corrupt customs, glibness is condemned; in discussions of changing times, the esteem for accommodating conduct is disparaged; and in urging strict personal discipline, upright conduct is valued. Yet those sent as envoys to the four quarters have never been rejected for their eloquence, nor has the Way of the Mean ever been sought through strange and extraordinary behavior. Why is this? Those cautious in speech possess lofty virtue, whereas those given to extravagant talk bend with the wind. Those resolute in conduct possess enduring virtue, whereas the accommodating follow others deceitfully. These are indeed the essentials of speech and conduct. As for Zigong’s impartiality, which Shuxiang commended [?]; Zichan’s eloquence, upon which the feudal lords relied; and Chai’s simplicity and Shen’s dullness, through which they established great achievements [?]—there is also something to approve in the things that scrupulous men refuse to do. Thus speech truly cannot be dispensed with, while accommodating conduct need not be esteemed: this is certain. Nevertheless, does the gentleman delight in expending so many words on this? He does so because the teachings of the Way must be clarified and people’s hearts must be rectified.
Once the Great Way became hidden, the people’s errors gradually grew manifest. Gentleness and deference degenerated into flattery and obsequiousness; integrity and sincerity dissolved into fawning servility. Those whose speech and conduct remain worthy of regard are also those whose customary practices approach antiquity. I have sought understanding in the speech and silence of the ancients, and have gained insights from Yuwen Rong’s fluent replies, Zhou Bo’s seeming inability to get his words out, Wang Yifu’s exceptionally lucid and eloquent discourse, Li Guang’s quiet reserve throughout the day, Ji Kang’s uninhibited and forthright speech, and Xu Zhi’s refusal to answer questions about affairs of state. I have also examined the traces of the ancients’ accommodating and restrained conduct, and have gained insights from Zhuo Mao’s self-discipline and cultivation, and Xi Chao’s following his own mind to attain an understanding uniquely his own…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
闕康之之候見不顧何思澄之惟事造謁
陸龜蒙之恥與俗交申屠蟠之自同傭人
矣蓋求之而不辯稽之而不察果能有以
盡夫人乎否耶故曰言有切謾而行有夷
險者也夫以聚斂禍唐者孰與厚重之安
劉廢事亂晉者孰與簡易之効績直遂戕
生者孰與明哲之自容曠世不羈者孰與
恭愛之被聘俗方婁護者又孰與人不敢
干之高尚及乎樂開入學之賢見幾而作
===
之智或者殆未可以醇疵判矣由是觀之
誕者不必述事而謹者然後可以營道通
者不必周務而果者然後可以育德噫聖
人之言動又豈有舍道德而為之度者哉
而執事者下詢又欲求以去夫口過怨惡
之道焉蓋有以見開示承學之盛心矣夫
言由中出行由心制者也君子先立其誠
於是乎有易心之語比義之行矣韓愈儒
者也其著言行之箴顧不推本於此何耶
punctuated: 闕康之之候見不顧，何思澄之惟事造謁，陸龜蒙之恥與俗交，申屠蟠之自同傭人矣。蓋求之而不辯，稽之而不察，果能有以盡夫人乎？否耶？故曰：言有切謾，而行有夷險者也。夫以聚斂禍唐者，孰與厚重之安劉？廢事亂晉者，孰與簡易之効績？直遂戕生者，孰與明哲之自容？曠世不羈者，孰與恭愛之被聘？俗方婁護者，又孰與人不敢干之高尚？及乎樂開入學之賢、見幾而作之智，或者殆未可以醇疵判矣。由是觀之，誕者不必述事，而謹者然後可以營道；通者不必周務，而果者然後可以育德。噫！聖人之言動，又豈有舍道德而為之度者哉？而執事者下詢，又欲求以去夫口過怨惡之道焉，蓋有以見開示承學之盛心矣。夫言由中出，行由心制者也。君子先立其誠，於是乎有易心之語、比義之行矣。韓愈，儒者也；其著言行之箴，顧不推本於此，何耶？
translation_en:
…Que Kangzhi’s refusal to turn his gaze while awaiting an audience [?], He Sicheng’s exclusive devotion to paying visits, Lu Guimeng’s shame at associating with the vulgar, and Shentu Pan’s placing himself on the same footing as hired laborers. Yet if one seeks examples without distinguishing among them, and examines precedents without scrutinizing them, can one truly understand these men fully—or not? Thus it is said: speech may be earnest or deceitful, and conduct straightforward or treacherous.

How does the man whose exactions brought calamity upon the Tang compare with the man whose gravity and integrity secured the Liu ruling house? How does the man whose neglect of affairs brought disorder upon the Jin compare with the man whose simplicity and ease produced achievements? How does the man whose headlong frankness destroyed his life compare with the man whose insight and wisdom enabled him to preserve himself? How does the man who stood aloof from his age, unrestrained, compare with the man whose reverence and affection won him an invitation to serve? And how does the man whose vulgarity was likened to that of Lou Hu compare with the lofty recluse whom others dared not importune? As for the worthiness of delighting in opening access to learning [?], and the wisdom of discerning the first signs and acting upon them, perhaps these cannot readily be judged in terms of purity and flaws.

Viewed in this light, the extravagant do not necessarily accomplish undertakings; only the circumspect can cultivate the Way. The accommodating do not necessarily attend comprehensively to affairs; only the resolute can nurture virtue. Ah! In their speech and actions, could the sages ever set aside the Way and virtue as their measure? You, honored examiners, have graciously asked further about the means of avoiding faults of speech and the resentment and hatred they provoke. This reveals your earnest wish to enlighten and instruct those pursuing learning.

Speech issues from within, and conduct is governed by the heart. The gentleman first establishes his sincerity; from this come words expressing an unassuming heart and actions conforming to righteousness. Han Yu was a Confucian scholar. Why, then, when writing his Admonitions on Speech and Conduct, did he fail to trace them back to this foundation?

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
噫誠豈易言哉昔顏淵問仁而請其目夫
子曰非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言非禮
勿動程子嗣而為之四箴誠之一語蓋三
致意焉退之之學非心學也無惑乎其未
之前聞也雖然何以知要曰言忠信行篤
敬雖蠻貊之邦行矣此孔氏家法也請敬
事斯語
第五問
蔣識
===
同考試官教諭林批民事敝而不脩軍政渙
而無緒廣西之恒患也此策首言任人任權已得
其要而叙事精確初無浮冗不根之談見於施行
當亦有濟如子者豈亦先天下之憂者歟吾將卜
子於用矣
考試官教諭周批士子適用之學類於時
務一策見之此篇辭醇事覈諒非能言而不能行者
考試官教諭方批士子叙時政者不激即
迂此篇酌古準今言利害處尤明白痛切而文復渾
punctuated:
噫！誠豈易言哉！昔顏淵問仁而請其目，夫子曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」程子嗣而為之四箴，誠之一語，蓋三致意焉。退之之學非心學也，無惑乎其未之前聞也。雖然，何以知要？曰：「言忠信，行篤敬，雖蠻貊之邦行矣。」此孔氏家法也，請敬事斯語。

第五問
蔣識

同考試官教諭林批：民事敝而不脩，軍政渙而無緒，廣西之恒患也。此策首言任人任權，已得其要，而叙事精確，初無浮冗不根之談。見於施行，當亦有濟。如子者，豈亦先天下之憂者歟？吾將卜子於用矣。

考試官教諭周批：士子適用之學，類於時務一策見之。此篇辭醇事覈，諒非能言而不能行者。

考試官教諭方批：士子叙時政者，不激即迂。此篇酌古準今，言利害處尤明白痛切，而文復渾
translation_en:
Ah! How could sincerity be easy to discuss! In former times, when Yan Yuan asked about benevolence and requested its particulars, the Master said: “Look at nothing contrary to ritual propriety; listen to nothing contrary to ritual propriety; say nothing contrary to ritual propriety; make no movement contrary to ritual propriety.” Master Cheng subsequently composed four admonitions on these injunctions, repeatedly emphasizing the word “sincerity.” Tuizhi’s learning was not the learning of the mind; it is no wonder that he had not previously heard this teaching. Even so, how may one grasp the essentials? It is said: “Be loyal and trustworthy in speech, earnest and respectful in conduct; then, even in the lands of the Man and Mo peoples, you may make your way.” This is the teaching handed down in the school of Confucius. Let me respectfully put these words into practice.

Fifth Question
Jiang Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Civil affairs are in disrepair and remain unattended to; military administration is fragmented and disordered. These are Guangxi’s persistent troubles. This policy essay begins by discussing the appointment of men and the entrusting of authority, already grasping the essentials. Its account of affairs is precise, entirely free of empty, excessive, or unfounded talk. If put into practice, its proposals should also prove beneficial. Is someone like you perhaps one who worries before all others under Heaven? I shall look to your service to test my judgment of you.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: A candidate’s learning for practical application can generally be seen in a single policy essay on current affairs. This piece is sound in expression and exact in its treatment of matters. Surely its author is no mere talker incapable of action.

Comment by Examiner Fang, Instructor: Candidates discussing current government are either intemperate or impractical. This piece weighs antiquity against the present; its discussion of benefits and harms is especially clear, incisive, and pertinent, while its prose is also rounded …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
厚深暢經濟之學也
善養民者任賢其先也善養兵者任將其
要也蓋裕民非難民且不足而國計方殷
欲一於裕民為難也强兵非難兵且不足
而時難荐至欲急於强兵為難也雖然事
有難為之勢而亦有不難為之理殆未可
執一論也察耗敝之原廣豐殖之利均撫
馭之政然必量緩急之宜而詳夫施為之
方理之所易也如此愚故先之以任賢任
===
將之論矣廣西之民困矣而致困之原曰
有盜賊以撓其生有征派以屈其力有侵
漁以蝕其心然究其歸則守令之未擇也
廣西之卒耗矣而致耗之原曰工巧者敝
於投附姦宄者敝於脫漏貧懦者敝於征
調然求其故則將禁之未一也夫以至困
極耗之際而猶泥夫故常之迹必欲如昔
人之減苗削猺抑配斂今也逃亡之租亦
旣停無經之費亦嘗節矣必欲如昔人之
punctuated:
厚深暢，經濟之學也。

善養民者，任賢其先也；善養兵者，任將其要也。蓋裕民非難，民且不足而國計方殷，欲一於裕民為難也；强兵非難，兵且不足而時難荐至，欲急於强兵為難也。雖然，事有難為之勢，而亦有不難為之理，殆未可執一論也。察耗敝之原，廣豐殖之利，均撫馭之政，然必量緩急之宜，而詳夫施為之方。理之所易也如此，愚故先之以任賢任將之論矣。

廣西之民困矣，而致困之原，曰有盜賊以撓其生，有征派以屈其力，有侵漁以蝕其心；然究其歸，則守令之未擇也。廣西之卒耗矣，而致耗之原，曰工巧者敝於投附，姦宄者敝於脫漏，貧懦者敝於征調；然求其故，則將禁之未一也。夫以至困極耗之際，而猶泥夫故常之迹，必欲如昔人之減苗削猺、抑配斂，今也逃亡之租亦旣停，無經之費亦嘗節矣。必欲如昔人之
translation_en:
…substantial, profound, and fluent: this is learning directed toward governing the realm and ordering its affairs.

Those skilled at nurturing the people put the appointment of worthy men first; those skilled at sustaining troops regard the appointment of commanders as essential. Enriching the people is not itself difficult. What is difficult is to devote oneself wholly to enriching them when they lack sufficient resources and the demands of state finance are pressing. Strengthening the army is not itself difficult. What is difficult is to make strengthening it an urgent priority when its resources are inadequate and crises repeatedly arise. Nevertheless, although circumstances may make action difficult, there are also principles by which it need not be difficult. We surely cannot insist upon a single line of argument. Investigate the sources of depletion and exhaustion, expand the benefits of productive activity, and make policies of nurturing and governing equitable. Yet one must assess what should be deferred and what requires urgency, and carefully examine the means of implementation. These are the ways in which sound principles make the task easier. Thus I have begun with the argument for appointing worthy men and capable commanders.

The people of Guangxi are impoverished. The sources of their impoverishment are these: bandits disrupt their livelihoods, levies and requisitions exhaust their strength, and official depredations eat away at their resolve. Yet traced to its ultimate source, the problem lies in the failure to select prefects and county magistrates properly. Guangxi’s troops are depleted. The sources of their depletion are these: skilled craftsmen are lost through attachment to powerful patrons; the unscrupulous evade service by slipping off the registers; and the poor and weak are exhausted by mobilization. Yet the underlying cause is the lack of uniformity in commanders’ prohibitions [?]. At a time of such extreme impoverishment and depletion, would one still cling to established precedents and insist upon following earlier men in ‘reducing the Miao and cutting back the Yao’ [?], and curbing apportioned exactions? Taxes owed by those who have fled have already been suspended, and irregular expenses have already been curtailed. If one insists upon following earlier men in…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
罷征交屯近郡歟今也寇則在門庭兵則
不出境而廣東之餉且歲至湖廣遞戍之
軍日接踵於道矣必欲滅四郊之盜蠲兩
稅之征逐侵漁之吏編戶之民非不足以
刷積歲之忿而快其心吾恐十室九空緩
急之宜吾民不能以懸俟矣必欲正投附
之罰完脫漏之伍節貪懦之差尺籍之衆
非不足以申號令之重而作其氣吾恐十
羊九牧施為之方吾人不得以專制矣夫
===
惟至困之民而守之以不能懸俟之勢枯
魚之肆不其多乎且歲入不登於舊經費
遂踰於初官之所急即民之所需也為民
計者惟廣豐殖之利而已昔羊祜之始鎮
襄陽也軍無百日之儲祜乃墾田八百餘
頃及其季年遂有十年之積蓋古人已試
之效也廣西之野原田久於蕪穢水泉廢
於荒窒列郡蓋相望也必若募逃逋之徒
給墾闢之具分疆刊石使有定分再歲而
punctuated:
罷征交，屯近郡歟？今也寇則在門庭，兵則不出境，而廣東之餉且歲至，湖廣遞戍之軍日接踵於道矣。必欲滅四郊之盜，蠲兩稅之征，逐侵漁之吏，編戶之民非不足以刷積歲之忿而快其心，吾恐十室九空，緩急之宜，吾民不能以懸俟矣。必欲正投附之罰，完脫漏之伍，節貪懦之差，尺籍之衆非不足以申號令之重而作其氣，吾恐十羊九牧，施為之方，吾人不得以專制矣。
夫惟至困之民，而守之以不能懸俟之勢，枯魚之肆不其多乎？且歲入不登於舊，經費遂踰於初，官之所急，即民之所需也。為民計者，惟廣豐殖之利而已。昔羊祜之始鎮襄陽也，軍無百日之儲，祜乃墾田八百餘頃，及其季年，遂有十年之積，蓋古人已試之效也。廣西之野，原田久於蕪穢，水泉廢於荒窒，列郡蓋相望也。必若募逃逋之徒，給墾闢之具，分疆刊石，使有定分，再歲而
translation_en:
…cease campaigning against Jiaozhi and station troops in nearby prefectures? Today, however, the raiders are at our very doors, and our troops do not leave the provincial boundaries. Moreover, supplies from Guangdong arrive annually, while troops from Huguang coming for successive garrison rotations follow one another along the roads every day. If we insist upon eliminating the bandits on all sides, remitting the twice-yearly taxes, and expelling predatory officials, these measures could indeed enable registered households to clear away their accumulated resentment and find satisfaction. Yet I fear that, with nine households in ten deserted, our people cannot wait indefinitely for measures suited to their pressing needs. If we insist upon properly enforcing penalties for seeking attachment to powerful patrons, restoring the ranks depleted by evasion of registration, and regulating the service assignments of the greedy and cowardly [?], these measures could indeed reaffirm the authority of commands and raise the spirits of the registered soldiers. Yet I fear that, with nine shepherds for every ten sheep, we cannot exercise undivided authority over the measures to be taken.
When people in the utmost distress are kept in circumstances in which they cannot afford to wait indefinitely, will not many end up in the dried-fish shop—that is, beyond rescue? Moreover, annual revenues fall short of their former level, while regular expenditures exceed what they were at first. What the authorities urgently require is precisely what the people themselves need. Those who plan for the people must simply expand the benefits of productive cultivation. When Yang Hu first took up his command at Xiangyang, the army lacked even a hundred days’ reserves. He therefore brought more than eight hundred qing of land under cultivation; by his final years there, reserves sufficient for ten years had accumulated. This was an effective measure already tried by a man of antiquity. Throughout the countryside of Guangxi, fields have long lain overgrown, and watercourses and springs have fallen into disuse through neglect and blockage. Such conditions are found in prefecture after prefecture. If we were to recruit fugitives, provide tools for reclaiming land, demarcate boundaries and inscribe them on stones so that each had a fixed allotment, then after two years…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
熟民知所趨矣由是於常賦則放陂納而
徵土著於公田則給傭直而收贏餘雖微
叔子之效公私其或少贍乎夫惟極耗之
卒而振之以不能專制之威枘鑿之用可
相入乎且衛乏而需於所所乏而需於軍
下之所惡即上之所欲也為軍計者惟均
撫馭之政而已昔雍子之為謀主於晉也
彭城之役歸老幼返孤疾二人役歸一人
陣楚次而降彭城又古人已成之績也廣
===
西之兵丁壯役之樵蘇孱幼沒之奴隸宿
弊蓋相緣也必若嚴貴精之法廣營屯之
田招亡察隱俾無欺蔽踰時而定軍實可
閱矣由是精練者則執干戈而衛社稷羸
弱者則負耒耜而助饟糧雖無雍子之績
什伍其或少復乎振飭之務此其梗槩耳
夫民無定情而政且繁守令不擇則苟且
之意多而化不流軍有常局而弊易濫驩
禁不一則影占之私盛而法不統苟得其
punctuated:
熟，民知所趨矣。由是，於常賦則放陂納而徵土著，於公田則給傭直而收贏餘。雖微叔子之效，公私其或少贍乎？
夫惟極耗之卒，而振之以不能專制之威，枘鑿之用可相入乎？且衛乏而需於所，所乏而需於軍，下之所惡即上之所欲也。為軍計者，惟均撫馭之政而已。昔雍子之為謀主於晉也，彭城之役，歸老幼，返孤疾，二人役歸一人，陣楚次而降彭城，又古人已成之績也。廣西之兵，丁壯役之樵蘇，孱幼沒之奴隸，宿弊蓋相緣也。必若嚴貴精之法，廣營屯之田，招亡察隱，俾無欺蔽，踰時而定，軍實可閱矣。由是，精練者則執干戈而衛社稷，羸弱者則負耒耜而助饟糧。雖無雍子之績，什伍其或少復乎？振飭之務，此其梗槩耳。
夫民無定情，而政且繁，守令不擇，則苟且之意多而化不流；軍有常局，而弊易濫，驩禁不一，則影占之私盛而法不統。苟得其
translation_en:
…the land becomes productive, and the people will know where to direct their efforts. Thereafter, in the matter of regular taxes, adjust remissions and payments [?] and levy taxes on the settled inhabitants; on public fields, pay wages and collect the surplus. Even without attaining Shuzi’s results, might public and private resources not become somewhat more ample?
To take utterly depleted troops and try to reinvigorate them through an authority that cannot exercise sole command—is this not like trying to fit an incompatible tenon and mortise together? Moreover, when the guards lack resources, they demand them from the battalions; when the battalions lack resources, they demand them from the soldiers. What those below detest is precisely what those above desire. Those planning for the army need only make its care and command equitable. Formerly, when Yongzi served as chief strategist for Jin, during the campaign against Pengcheng he sent home the old and young and returned the orphaned and sick; where two men from one household were serving, he sent one home. He arrayed the troops at the Chu encampment [?] and brought Pengcheng to surrender. This, too, was an accomplishment already achieved by the ancients. Among Guangxi’s troops, able-bodied men are put to work gathering firewood and fodder, while the weak and young are reduced to servitude: these longstanding abuses perpetuate one another. If the principle of valuing quality in troops were rigorously enforced, the fields cultivated by military colonies expanded, deserters recalled, and concealed manpower investigated, so that there were no deception or concealment, matters would be settled within a season, and the army’s actual strength could be inspected. Thereafter, the well-trained would take up shields and spears to defend the state, while the weak would shoulder ploughs and spades to help supply military provisions. Even without Yongzi’s achievements, might the military ranks not be somewhat restored? These are merely the broad outlines of the work of revitalization and reform.
The people’s dispositions are not fixed, and government affairs are numerous. If prefects and magistrates are not carefully selected, expediency will prevail and the transforming influence of government will not spread. The army has an established organization, yet abuses readily proliferate. If prohibitions [?] are not uniform, the private abuse of appropriating soldiers under the cover of official privilege will flourish, and the law will lack unity. If suitable men can be obtained…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人則撓民者有所控制屈民者有所通融
蝕民者有所畏憚而凡豐殖之利將經久
而無遺矣苟一其權則投附者無所依憑
姦宄者無所竄匿征調者無所恣咨而凡
撫馭之政將均齊而專一矣雖然豈特廣
西之患哉不恤緯而憂王室誠非嫠婦之
任也惟執事者教之
punctuated: 人，則撓民者有所控制，屈民者有所通融，蝕民者有所畏憚，而凡豐殖之利，將經久而無遺矣。苟一其權，則投附者無所依憑，姦宄者無所竄匿，征調者無所恣咨，而凡撫馭之政，將均齊而專一矣。雖然，豈特廣西之患哉？不恤緯而憂王室，誠非嫠婦之任也。惟執事者教之。
translation_en: …the right men are found, those who harass the people will be restrained, those who oppress them will be subject to corrective accommodation, and those who prey upon them will have something to fear. All the benefits of prosperity will thus endure, with none left unrealized. If authority is unified, those who attach themselves to powerful protectors will have no support to rely upon, evildoers will have nowhere to hide, and those responsible for military mobilization will have no scope to act arbitrarily [?]. All measures for pacifying and governing will thus be applied evenly and under unified direction. Yet is this a problem peculiar to Guangxi? To disregard the weft of one’s weaving and worry about the royal house is indeed no widow’s responsibility. I ask only that you who preside instruct me.

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
正德己卯秋八月下澣廣西
鄉試錄就緒有日矣尚文等
七人實受幣聘來典文衡方
事之殷寢不安席食不下咽
憂心忡忡惟恐其有負也撤
棘之前夕卷束于箱榜登于
===
堂待旦而出院尚文等暫憩
小集取館人嚮日所供酒殽
薄定禮飲獻酬有節雝雝愉
愉歡而不譁所以舒其和弛
其蘊節宣其勞而樂王事之
有成也旣而相與諗曰古者
列國卿大夫聘問宴饗必賦
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

正德己卯秋八月下澣，廣西鄉試錄就緒有日矣。尚文等七人實受幣聘，來典文衡。方事之殷，寢不安席，食不下咽，憂心忡忡，惟恐其有負也。撤棘之前夕，卷束于箱，榜登于堂，待旦而出院。尚文等暫憩小集，取館人嚮日所供酒殽，薄定禮飲，獻酬有節，雝雝愉愉，歡而不譁，所以舒其和，弛其蘊，節宣其勞，而樂王事之有成也。旣而相與諗曰：「古者列國卿大夫聘問宴饗，必賦
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the final ten days of the eighth month, in autumn of the jimao year of the Zhengde reign [1519], the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination was nearing completion. We seven, Shangwen and the others, had accepted ceremonial gifts of invitation and come to judge the examination essays. At the busiest stage of our duties, we could neither sleep peacefully nor swallow our food. Our hearts were filled with anxiety, fearing only that we might fail the trust placed in us.

On the evening before the thorn barriers were removed, the examination papers were bundled into chests and the list of successful candidates posted in the hall; we awaited dawn to leave the examination compound. Shangwen and the others rested briefly and gathered together. Taking the wine and dishes that our hosts had supplied earlier, we made modest arrangements for ceremonial drinking. Cups were offered and returned in due measure; in harmony and contentment, we rejoiced without clamour. Thus we gave expression to our concord, released our pent-up feelings, and regulated and relieved our fatigue, rejoicing that the king’s business had been accomplished.

Then we addressed one another, saying: “In antiquity, when ministers and grand masters of the various states exchanged diplomatic visits and attended banquets, they invariably recited odes…”

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In autumn, during the last ten days of the eighth month of the jimao year of Zhengde [1519], the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination was nearing completion. We seven, Shangwen and the others, had accepted the ceremonial gifts of engagement and come to preside over the assessment of literary merit. At the busiest stage of the work, we could neither sleep soundly nor swallow our food. Our hearts were full of anxiety, lest we fail in our charge. On the evening before the thorn barriers were removed, the examination papers were bundled into chests and the list of successful candidates posted in the hall. We awaited dawn to leave the examination compound.

Shangwen and the others rested briefly and gathered together. We took the wine and sliced meat previously supplied by the attendants and arranged a modest ceremonial drinking gathering. The offering and returning of cups followed due measure; we were harmonious and cheerful, merry without being boisterous. This allowed us to give expression to our concord, release our pent-up feelings, find measured relief from our labors, and rejoice in having brought the king’s business to completion. Then we said to one another: “In antiquity, when the ministers and grand masters of the various states exchanged diplomatic visits and attended banquets, they invariably recited verse …

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之矣吾徒此行得無內疚乎
好賢莫如緇衣杕杜近似之
矣誠之發於中心而敢有怠
於此乎淇澳之切磋琢磨求
其精而益致其精矣寧復有
遺材之憾乎菁莪棫樸雨露
之所濡也
===
國家作人造士之功莫大焉南
山之臺其德盛矣邦家之基
以人事君之謂也當軸諸君
子有焉雖然受賜不報豈只
尚文等之愆抑亦諸士之耻
也遂歌天保以祝
聖明坐者皆肅容拱而立御史專
punctuated: 之矣。吾徒此行，得無內疚乎？好賢莫如《緇衣》，《杕杜》近似之矣。誠之發於中心，而敢有怠於此乎？《淇澳》之切磋琢磨，求其精而益致其精矣，寧復有遺材之憾乎？《菁莪》《棫樸》，雨露之所濡也，國家作人造士之功莫大焉。《南山之臺》，其德盛矣。「邦家之基」，以人事君之謂也。當軸諸君子有焉。雖然，受賜不報，豈只尚文等之愆，抑亦諸士之耻也。遂歌《天保》以祝聖明，坐者皆肅容，拱而立。御史專
translation_en: …recite them. Could we, on this undertaking, have no inward misgivings? For delight in worthy men, no poem surpasses “Black Robes” (Ziyi); “The Solitary Pear Tree” (Didu) comes close. When sincerity springs from the heart, dare we be remiss in this? The cutting, filing, chiseling, and polishing of “The Bend of the Qi” (Qi’ao) mean seeking refinement and bringing it to still greater perfection. Could there then remain any regret over overlooked talent? “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing’e) and “The Oak Thicket” (Yupu) speak of nourishment by rain and dew: nothing surpasses the state’s achievement in fostering men and cultivating scholars. In “The Terrace on the Southern Mountain” (Nanshan zhi tai), virtue is abundant. “The foundation of the realm” means serving one’s ruler by supplying worthy men. The gentlemen at the helm possess this virtue. Nevertheless, to receive favors without requiting them would be not only a fault of Shangwen and his colleagues, but also a disgrace to the scholars. They accordingly sang “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao) to invoke blessings upon the sagely sovereign. All those seated assumed solemn expressions and stood with hands clasped. Censor Zhuan…

title: 正德十四年廣西鄉試錄
text:
珪聞之曰是可以警有位華
鹿鳴矣命附諸末簡以為序
江西南昌府新建縣儒學教
諭周尚文謹序
punctuated:
珪聞之曰：「是可以警有位，華鹿鳴矣。」命附諸末簡，以為序。
江西南昌府新建縣儒學教諭周尚文謹序。
translation_en:
…Gui heard this and said, “This can admonish those in office and lend distinction to the Deer Cry banquet.” He ordered that it be appended to the final leaves as a preface.
Preface respectfully composed by Zhou Shangwen, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi.
